docs.title: Chaining rules
docs.text:
• Two attention mappings, never mixed: query-major qk_scores_* → attn_v_*, and key-major attn_scores_km_* → attn_v_bcast_*. Each attn@V kernel only reads its own chain's score layout.

  • Q must be pre-scaled. No score kernel applies 1/√head_dim; fold it into the Q rows of the QKV weights once:

    Layer head_dim scale L3 36 0.166667 L4 48 0.144338 L5 60 0.129099

  • Producers write full rows; only the final consumer crops. One output channel per XMEM row, even where fewer than 128 lanes are valid.

docs.title: layernorm
docs.text:
output[ch, i] = γ[ch] × (x[ch, i] − μ[i]) / σ[i] + β[ch]

normalizing across channels, independently per token (μ, σ are per-token, not per-channel — the opposite axis from a typical batch norm).

No eps (Q57): a zero variance gives rsqrt = 0, so a constant token column becomes β. The golden is the shared ipu_kernels.reference.ops.layernorm (dim = 0).

The four kernels are entries of kernels/normalize/registry.toml over the layernorm template (one program per shape), each run as //kernels/normalize:<kernel>.

Kernel Channels Tokens layernorm_128x16 16 128 layernorm_64x192 192 64 layernorm_16x240 240 16 layernorm_256x144 144 256

Query: bazel run //kernels:query -- layernorm channels=C tokens=T. x and y are one 128-element FP32 row per channel and token group (row ch * ceil(tokens / 128) + g), tokens in the first lanes; x is zero past them, and y holds beta[ch] there. gamma and beta are channels FP32 values in zero-padded rows. x sits at row 0: the program reads its base through CR0.

docs.title: l2_normalize
docs.text:
y[ch, n] = x[ch, n] / sqrt(Σ_ch x[ch, n]²)

per column, down the channels. One kernel, l2_normalize_channels (//kernels/normalize/l2_normalize_channels), takes any channels and columns, 128 columns a tile: bazel run //kernels:query -- l2_normalize channels=C columns=N. An all-zero column gives 0, not NaN: the rsqrt activation maps a non-positive sum to 0.

docs.title: The MobileViT packed layout
docs.text:
The Layer 4 and Layer 5 transformer blocks also run in a packed layout: 128 / tokens channels share a row, channel c's tokens at row c / (128 / tokens), lanes (c % (128 / tokens)) * tokens on (2 channels a row at Layer 4, 8 at Layer 5). It is row-major over the flattened (channels, tokens) tensor, so each kernel declares a packed tensor as its rows. LayerNorm, pack, unpack and the linear use their own op names, so no unpacked query reaches them; the residual adds share residual_add with the unpacked ones and are told apart by per_row:

Kernel Family Op What packed_layernorm_192x64, packed_layernorm_240x16 kernels/normalize packed_layernorm LayerNorm over the channels, ops.layernorm (no eps) packed_pack_192x64, packed_pack_240x16 kernels/reshape pack one channel a row → packed packed_unpack_192x64, packed_unpack_240x16 kernels/reshape unpack packed → one channel a row (the attention seam) packed_output_linear{,_silu}_240, packed_output_linear{,_silu}_192 kernels/projections packed_linear one packed output row of activation(a @ b) a call; k is a parameter packed_residual_add_192x64, packed_residual_add_240x16 kernels/elementwise residual_add the residual_add_rows program with per_row 2 and 8

All but the residual add load an R_MASK row (a scratch region whose bytes the family's gen.py makes from ipu_kernels.pack.r_mask). Pack, unpack and the linear leave R_MASK changed (LayerNorm ends by reloading all ones): the residual add relies on R_MASK's all-ones reset value, so it needs R_MASK reloaded first when it runs after one of them. Query, for example: bazel run //kernels:query -- packed_layernorm channels=240 tokens=16.

docs.title: residual_add
docs.text:
Plain elementwise y = a + b. The three unpacked kernels are entries of kernels/elementwise/registry.toml over the residual_add_rows template (one program), each run as //kernels/elementwise:<kernel>. For residual_add_16x240 and residual_add_64x192, one whole row per channel (tokens elements of data, the rest zero padding) — the same layout as layernorm's input; residual_add_256x144 has tokens > 128, so each channel takes ceil(tokens / 128) full rows.

Kernel Tokens Channels residual_add_16x240 16 240 residual_add_64x192 64 192 residual_add_256x144 256 144

Query: bazel run //kernels:query -- residual_add tokens=T channels=C. Two more entries, packed_residual_add_{192x64,240x16}, run the same program on the packed layout (per_row 2 and 8; above).

The CHW residual_add kernel (convolution stages) shares this operation but is queried by num_channels; see Convolutions.

docs.title: unfold
docs.text:
A stride-2 space-to-depth decimation (PixelUnshuffle(2)'s phase decomposition): for each of 4 output streams s = (r_ph, c_ph),

output[s] = x[:, r_ph::2, c_ph::2]
Kernel H W C unfold_8x8x240 8 8 240 unfold_16x16x192 16 16 192 unfold_32x32x144 32 32 144

Each runs as //kernels/reshape/<kernel>. Query: bazel run //kernels:query -- unfold h=H w=W c=C. The input x [C, H, W] is laid out in spatial stripes, one row per channel and stripe (the family pack.py transform stripes); unfold_8x8x240's rows are permuted (paired_rows). The output y [4, C, tokens] holds the four phases one after another, the first tokens lanes of each row valid (phase_rows).

fold_8x8x240, fold_16x16x192 and fold_32x32x144 (op fold, the same h w c query) are the inverses: x [4, C, tokens] in, y [C, H, W] out in stripes. kernels/reshape/test_fold_unfold.py runs each pair end to end on one model. concat_8x8x160x160, concat_16x16x128x128 and concat_32x32x96x96 concatenate two tensors along the channel axis, one channel per row: entries of kernels/reshape/registry.toml over the concat template, each run as //kernels/reshape:<kernel>. Query: bazel run //kernels:query -- concat h=H w=W c_a=C_A c_b=C_B.

docs.title: Softmax
docs.text:
Five kernels covering every 1-D softmax shape. They differ in which direction the reduction runs and how the reduced length relates to the 128-element datapath — but they share one formulation and one four-pass structure, so understanding one gets you most of the way through the others.

All five run in the FP32 element format only. They build on exp2 and reciprocal through ACTIVATE.EXACT, the emulator-only FP32 store, and have no NX8 variant. Each is a folder under kernels/softmax/ (its .asm, with the design notes in its header, and its kernel.toml), run and tested as //kernels/softmax/<kernel>.

docs.title: Picking one
docs.text:
Don't pick by hand — ask the registry:

bazel run //kernels:query -- softmax rows=32 n=300 dim=1

A query names the row count, the axis (dim=1 along each row, dim=0 down each column) and the length along it: n for rows, width for columns. A framework layer routes through Registry.from_layer: the Softmax adapter (ipu_kernels/softmax/layers.py) turns nn.Softmax(dim=d) on a tensor of any shape into that query, with torch's dim convention (a rank > 2 tensor flattens around a first or last softmax axis; an interior axis is refused).

The routing below is generated by probing the kernels (bazel run //kernels:query -- softmax rows=8 n=n dim=1 --sweep n=1..200, and rows=8 width=width dim=0 --sweep width=1..200 for columns), and kernels/softmax/test_routing.py checks it against the registry.

Along each row (torch.softmax(x, dim=1) on a (rows, n) tensor):

n 1..127        softmax_rows_partial
n = 128         softmax_rows
n 129..         softmax_rows_long

Down each column (dim=0 on a (rows, width) tensor):

width 1..64     softmax_columns_packed
width 65..      softmax_columns

Row count never affects routing: every row kernel loops internally.

docs.title: The shared formulation
docs.text:
The IPU's activation unit provides exp2, not exp. Rather than approximating e^x, the kernels reformulate in base 2:

softmax(x_i) = 2^(c * (x_i - xmax)) / SUM_j 2^(c * (x_j - xmax))     c = log2(e)

which is exactly equal to the usual definition, because 2^(c*d) == e^d. The constant c = log2(e) lives in a resident 128-element vector, so applying it costs one multiply.

Subtracting xmax is the standard numerical-stability step: it makes the largest exponent zero, so nothing overflows. It is free here — ACC.SUB against CR1 does it in the accumulate slot.

Every kernel then runs the same four passes:

  1. max — per-row (or per-column) maximum
  2. numerators — 2^(c*(x - xmax)), written out
  3. sum — reduce the numerators
  4. normalise — multiply by the reciprocal of the sum

docs.title: The row kernels
docs.text: The reduction runs along a row, collapsing 128 elements to one scalar. That is what AGG does, and the per-row scalars are then fanned back out.

docs.title: softmax_rows — exactly 128 elements
docs.text: The straightforward case: one row fills the vector exactly. No packing, no chunking, no padding.

docs.title: softmax_rows_partial — shorter than 128
docs.text:
Several logical rows share one 128-element chunk. The partition size ps is the next power of two ≥ N (clamped to [16, 128]), so P = 128 / ps rows fit per chunk:

N ps rows per chunk 65–128 128 1 33–64 64 2 17–32 32 4 1–16 16 8

To reduce partition p, MULT.RC.VV reads r_cyclic at element offset p*ps, which slides that partition down to elements 0..N-1; a masked AGG then reduces exactly those elements. Pass 4 reverses the slide to re-pack the results.

Why Pass 4 needs a mask

ACC.ADD writes all 128 elements unconditionally, and MULT.RC.VE leaves other rows' real data in the elements outside the current partition — so without masking, partitions overwrite each other's results. Each partition therefore gets its own R_MASK slot restricting the write to its own element range.

Because mask_offset is a compile-time immediate, the per-partition sequence is unrolled with Jinja (one block per P value) rather than written as a runtime loop, with a runtime branch selecting the right block.

docs.title: softmax_rows_long — longer than 128
docs.text:
A row spans several chunks, so the max and the sum span them too. Each pass keeps a running per-row scalar: AGG.*.FIRST on the first chunk, then plain AGG.* on the rest, combining into the same accumulator slot.

When N is not a multiple of 128 the last chunk is partial and reduces with valid_elements = tail instead of 128. When N is a multiple of 128 there is no tail chunk at all.

docs.title: The column kernels
docs.text:
Column softmax is the transpose of row softmax, and the difference is structural rather than cosmetic.

In row softmax the reduction collapses the elements of one vector to a scalar. In column softmax every element is an independent column, and the reduction runs across rows, staying in-element. So there is no AGG and no fan-out: the per-column max and sum are themselves full 128-element vectors, accumulated with ACC.MAX/ACC.ADD down the rows.

That also removes the row-group cap — per-column scalars are full vectors, not one slot per row — so row count is an ordinary loop bound.

docs.title: softmax_columns — width ≥ 65
docs.text:
Width is padded up to a multiple of 128. Padding elements are simply separate columns that happen to be all-zero; they never enter a real column's reduction, and they are dropped on read-back.

Widths that are not a multiple of 128 leave elements idle: width 100 uses 100 of every 128 elements (78%) and runs at the cost of width 128.

docs.title: softmax_columns_packed — width ≤ 64
docs.text:
Below 65, several whole rows fit in one vector (rows_per_vec = 128 / padded width), so the kernel packs them and reduces in two stages: a partial reduce down the vector, then a cross-group fold that combines the groups using cyclic shifts.

Padding is filled with a large negative value rather than zero, so it loses every max comparison and contributes nothing to the sums — without that, the fold would mix padding into real columns.

docs.title: Row counts
docs.text:
Per-row scalars hold one slot per row in a single 128-element vector, so at most 128 rows can be in flight. Every row kernel therefore processes rows in groups of at most 128, running all four passes per group before advancing.

This is a correctness requirement, not bookkeeping. The row index feeds MULT.RC.VE's scalar-select and AGG's destination slot, both of which index R0 for 0..127 and switch to R1 — never loaded in these passes — at 128. Restarting the index each group makes that unreachable. Group size is exact (min(128, rows_left)), so no padding row is ever processed.

docs.title: Data layout
docs.text:
Every kernel reads and writes row-major (rows, cols) float32: y has the same layout as x.

Internally the layouts differ considerably — softmax_rows_partial packs P rows per chunk and pads the row count; softmax_rows_long pads a tail chunk; softmax_columns pads the width — but none of that reaches the files. The harness packs on the way in and un-packs on the way out: the slot-packed kernels name pack = "row_slots" and "col_slots_negpad" (ipu_kernels/softmax/pack.py).

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
From each kernel's benchmark ([benchmark] in its kernel.toml):

Kernel Config cyc/row MULT util Effective MAC softmax_rows 128 rows 18.15 27.6% 16.5% softmax_rows_partial n=16, 512 rows 18.43 27.1% 2.0% softmax_rows_long n=200, 200 rows 48.17 20.8% 11.5% softmax_columns width 128, 128 rows 19.18 26.1% 15.6% softmax_columns_packed width 32, 100 rows 5.25 25.5% 14.5%

MULT util counts every cycle the multiplier is busy. About 40% of those are identity multiplies — data routing the ISA has no other path for (see the ISA idioms) — and narrow rows leave lanes idle, so Effective MAC, the share of peak MACs actually retired, is lower. softmax_rows_partial at n=16 keeps the multiplier 27% busy but uses only 16 of its 128 lanes.

Two things worth reading off this. The packed column kernel is far cheaper per row because it processes several rows per vector. And the group loop costs essentially nothing: softmax_rows_partial at n=128 runs 28.23 cyc/row over 300 rows versus 28.48 over 50, despite crossing group boundaries.

Run them yourself with:

bazel run //kernels/softmax/<kernel> -- --benchmark

A kernel's [benchmark] only lists points — overrides of its default case's parameters. Every point is held to the kernel's golden like any case, so a benchmark cannot report a fast wrong answer: a point that fails is shown as FAIL and fails the command.

docs.title: Running one directly
docs.text:
bazel run //kernels/softmax/softmax_rows_long -- --list-cases
bazel run //kernels/softmax/softmax_rows_long -- --case default --output out/
bazel run //kernels/softmax/softmax_rows_long -- --input x=logits.npy --output out/

The last replaces the default case's x ((8, 300) float32) with your own array of that shape and writes out/y.npy. See Kernel coverage for the registry.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
These pages are for looking things up: instructions, operands, commands and terms.

Page What it covers Instructions Every instruction, by slot, generated from instruction_spec.py. Operand types The operand types the instruction reference uses. Assembly syntax Instruction words, separators, labels, registers and Jinja2 preprocessing. Instruction format The bit layout of the instruction word, and the SystemVerilog package download. Programmer's guide The pseudo-instructions the assembler expands, such as BGT.S and BZ. Registers Every register, its size and its assembly names. Configuration registers The CR constants, the CR halves (DS and QF layouts) and the MULT constant. ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, ACTIVATE.EXACT and LD.LUT The AaQ stage: activation, NX8 quantization, the store and the LUT. kernel.toml Every key of a kernel's kernel.toml and a family's registry.toml, generated from the loader. Command-line tools Every command-line tool (ipu-as, the kernel runner and the debugger), with its subcommands and options. Reference model API The stable emulator API and the trace schema. Kernels The kernel catalogue, by family. Code conventions How code in this repository is written, and what checks each rule. Code review What a PR author states and runs, and what reviewers check beyond CI. Glossary The terms these docs use.

docs.title: Command-line tools
docs.text: Every command-line tool in the repository, with its subcommands and options. The option tables are generated at docs build time from each tool's own option declarations (docs/cli_reference_page.py), so they list exactly what the tool parses. Run any of them through bazel run; everything after -- goes to the tool. Relative paths are read from the directory you run bazel in. Every tool also takes --help.

docs.title: Assembler: ipu-as
docs.text:
ipu-as assembles, disassembles, checks and formats IPU assembly. A source can be a Jinja2 template: --define gives the values its ipu:params header declares, and -I adds include directories after the source's own one.

bazel run //src/ipu-as:ipu-as -- assemble --input "$PWD/prog.asm" --output "$PWD/prog.bin" --define rows=8

assemble writes bin for an --output ending in .bin and mem otherwise, unless --format says which. --target hardware assembles the hardware slots only, and an emulator-only instruction such as BREAK is then an error. check exits 0 for a clean source and 1 otherwise; format exits 1 under --check when the source would change and 3 when it cannot format it.

docs.title: ipu-as assemble
docs.text:
Assembles the given input file.

ipu-as assemble [OPTIONS]
Option Value Default Description --input PATH required The assembly source to assemble. --output PATH required The program file to write. --format mem | bin Output format; by default bin for a .bin --output, else mem. --define KEY=VALUE, repeatable A template value, checked against the source's ipu:params header. Repeatable. -I / --include-dir DIRECTORY, repeatable A directory {% include %} and {% import %} resolve in, after the input's own directory. Repeatable. --abi FILE A kernel.toml whose [abi] table names the registers the template reads as {{ cr.<name> }} / {{ lr.<name> }}. --target emulator | hardware emulator The word to assemble: every slot, as the emulator runs it, or the hardware slots only (an emulator-only instruction is then an error).

docs.title: ipu-as disassemble
docs.text:
Disassembles the given input file.

ipu-as disassemble [OPTIONS]
Option Value Default Description --input PATH required The program file to read. --output PATH required The text file to write. --format mem | bin Input format; by default bin for a .bin --input, else mem. --target emulator | hardware emulator The word to assemble: every slot, as the emulator runs it, or the hardware slots only (an emulator-only instruction is then an error). --syntax fields | assembly fields fields: every field of every slot, by word; assembly: source that assembles back to the same words.

docs.title: ipu-as check
docs.text:
Report errors in an assembly source without producing output.

ipu-as check [OPTIONS]
Option Value Default Description --input TEXT required Source file to check, or "-" to read from stdin. --json / --text flag Emit machine-readable diagnostics (used by the VS Code extension). --json-version 1 to 2 Which --json layout to print: 1 (the default) is a bare array of diagnostics, 2 is {"schemaVersion": 2, "diagnostics": [...]}. --json-versions flag Print the --json versions this assembler supports, as a JSON array, and exit. --define KEY=VALUE, repeatable A template value, checked against the source's ipu:params header. Repeatable. -I / --include-dir DIRECTORY, repeatable A directory {% include %} and {% import %} resolve in, after the input's own directory. Repeatable. --target emulator | hardware emulator The word to assemble: every slot, as the emulator runs it, or the hardware slots only (an emulator-only instruction is then an error). --tokens flag Add the semantic tokens of the source. Needs v2. --words flag Add whether each word's instructions fit its slots. Needs v2. --jinja flag Add the Jinja regions, with the names each defines and uses. Needs v2.

docs.title: ipu-as format
docs.text:
Print an assembly source in the repository's layout.

ipu-as format [OPTIONS]
Option Value Default Description --input FILE required Source file to format, or "-" to read from stdin. --check flag Write nothing; exit 1 if formatting would change the source, 0 if not. --in-place flag Rewrite the input file instead of printing the result. --indent N\|tab 4 One level of indentation: N spaces, or a tab. --blank-line flag Separate each ;; word from the next by an empty line. --range L1:L2 Format only lines L1 to L2 (1-based, inclusive); the others stay as they are.

docs.title: Kernel runner: kernel targets and run_kernel
docs.text:
Each kernel under kernels/ is a Bazel target that runs one of its cases end to end, in one element format or all of them, and checks every output against its golden: bazel run //kernels/<family>/<name>, or //kernels/<family>:<entry> for a family's registry entry. The target passes the kernel itself; the options below come after --. run_kernel takes the kernel's folder instead, for a kernel outside the tree.

bazel run //kernels/softmax/softmax_rows -- --case constant_row --profile-aliases
bazel run //src/ipu-harness:run_kernel -- path/to/kernel --case default --format all

Each run prints KERNEL/CASE/FORMAT: PASS cycles=N MAC util=P%, then the fault, if the run faulted, and each output's comparison with its expected values. It exits 0 when every run passed; 1 when a run failed or faulted, or the request was wrong (one line, no traceback); and 2 for a bug in the runner or in the kernel's Python (with the traceback). bazel test on the same label runs every case in every format.

run_kernel [-h] [--case CASE] [--format FORMAT] [--input NAME=PATH.npy] [--output OUTPUT] [--trace TRACE] [--context CONTEXT] [--max-cycles MAX_CYCLES] [--list-cases] [--benchmark] [--markdown MARKDOWN] [--json JSON] [--debug] [--profile-aliases] [--alias-report ALIAS_REPORT] kernel
Option Value Default Description kernel positional required the kernel's folder (it holds kernel.toml), or REGISTRY.toml::NAME for an entry --case CASE default a case name, e.g. 'sweep[rows=7]' --format FORMAT an element format, or 'all' (default: the first of the case's formats) --input NAME=PATH.npy, repeatable replace an input (repeatable) --output OUTPUT write each output as DIR/<name>.npy --trace TRACE write the run's trace (JSON Lines) --context CONTEXT with --trace, also write the Cycle Inspector's context (JSON): the source, the starting registers, and each word's lanes and XMEM reads --max-cycles MAX_CYCLES the cycle limit (0: no limit; default: the model's) --list-cases flag list the cases and stop --benchmark flag run the [benchmark] points and print their table --markdown MARKDOWN with --benchmark, write the table here --json JSON with --benchmark, write the rows as JSON here --debug flag stop in the debugger TUI --profile-aliases flag profile the ISA aliases of the run and print the summary --alias-report ALIAS_REPORT write the alias profile as JSON instead (implies profiling; with --format all, PATH.<format>.json each)

docs.title: Run statistics
docs.text:
MAC util is the effective MAC utilization of the run, from the counters the reference model keeps for one run (ReferenceModel.stats(), the reference-model API); --benchmark reports them for each [benchmark] point:

Counter What it counts Total cycles Instruction words retired. Mult active, Acc active Cycles whose MULT or ACC slot was not a no-op, and their fraction of the total cycles. XMEM reads LD.MULT, LD.MULT.CYCLIC, LD.MASK and LD.LUT executed. XMEM writes ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE and ACTIVATE.EXACT executed (each stores one row). XMEM accesses Reads plus writes. Mult idle Cycles whose MULT slot was a no-op. Identity mult Active multiply cycles that multiplied by a constant 1 to move data, and their fraction of the active cycles. Lane ops Multiplier lanes that passed the mask and lay within valid_elements, summed over every multiply; occupancy is that over the total cycles times 128 lanes. Effective MAC Lane ops less the identity multiplies' lanes, over the run's peak: the multiplier work that was real arithmetic.

The counters describe one run: loading a program resets them, so a second program on the same model reports only itself.

A run that reaches its cycle limit faults F-9, with the PC of the word that would have run next. The default limit is ipu_emu.emulator.DEFAULT_MAX_CYCLES (1 000 000); --max-cycles N sets it for one run, and 0 removes it. A run that executed an ISA idiom counts it: --profile-aliases prints the idioms' measurements, and --alias-report FILE writes them as JSON.

docs.title: Debugger
docs.text:
The debugger is the kernel runner in a terminal user interface: add --config=debug to bazel run on any kernel target. It stops at cycle 0, before the first word runs, and takes the same options as an ordinary run.

bazel run --config=debug //kernels/reshape/identity -- --case single_row

--config=debug sets IPU_DEBUG_TUI=1 (.bazelrc). An interactive terminal is required. Debug a kernel explains the panes and the tab editor. The controls, from the debugger's own key table:

Execution and layout

Key Action Panes Shift-Tab Focus the next pane all 1-4 Focus a pane directly, left to right all F5 Continue to the next breakpoint all F8 Execute one instruction all Shift-Left / Shift-Right Move the focused row's split all Shift-Up / Shift-Down Move the top / bottom split all = Reset every split all ? Show this help overlay all q Halt execution and exit the debugger all

Focused pane

Key Action Panes F2 Add a tab to the focused pane all F3 Edit the active tab all F4 Close the active tab all f Cycle the active tab's format all d / a Select the next / previous tab all Arrows Move the cursor inside the focused pane all Tab Select the next tab all PgUp / PgDn Move the cursor by one page all Home / End Jump to the first / last value all Click Select panes, tabs, values, and footer actions all Wheel Scroll panes, help, or tabs under the pointer all Shift-wheel Move sideways within a pane all Double-click Edit the selected register or memory value all Code gutter Click to toggle an instruction breakpoint all Drag Drag a pane divider or scrollbar all F9 Disassembly: toggle breakpoint disassembly F10 Disassembly: run to cursor or next stop disassembly e Edit the selected value (PC in Disassembly) disassembly, registers, pipeline, xmem

docs.title: Trace recorder
docs.text:
The kernel runner records a case itself: --trace writes its trace (JSON Lines, the trace schema), and --context adds the context the Cycle Inspector needs beside it.

bazel run //kernels/reshape/identity -- --case single_row --trace "$PWD/trace.jsonl" --context "$PWD/context.json"

docs.title: Kernel query: query
docs.text:
query asks the kernel registry which kernel computes an operation, and why. With no operation it prints the coverage report.

bazel run //kernels:query -- maxpool2d channels=2 height=8 width=8 kernel_size=7 stride=1 padding=3

NAME=VALUE parameters go to the registry as given: a value with a comma is a tuple of integers, an integer is an int, a number with a point a float, true and false are booleans, and anything else is a string; format=e4 limits the answer to one element format. It exits 0 when the query is covered (for a sweep, every value) and 1 when it is not.

query [-h] [--sweep NAME=START..END] [--json] [op] [NAME=VALUE ...]
Option Value Default Description op positional operation, e.g. scale (omit for the coverage report) NAME=VALUE positional, repeatable kernel parameters --sweep NAME=START..END the routing table as NAME runs --json flag print the verdict as JSON (one query)

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
These rules say how code in this repository is written. Reviewers cite a rule by its section instead of a preference; people and agents read the same page.

Each rule names what checks it. Review means no tool checks it: the reviewer owns it (Code review). The ISA rules (opcodes from position, one source of instruction metadata, handler argument names) and the docs conventions are in CLAUDE.md, "Key Constraints", and in ADR 0001; this page does not repeat them.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Prefer deep modules: a small interface over a lot of behaviour. A caller learns little and gets a lot; the module can change inside without breaking callers. Review One responsibility per package. A package with one job has one reason to change. Review Dependencies point one way and are declared in the target's Bazel deps. A cycle makes packages impossible to test, build or replace alone. Bazel deps (an import outside them fails in the sandbox); //tools:test_import_graph checks package edges No function-level imports to dodge an import cycle. A lazy import hides a cycle instead of removing it. Move the shared code to the lower package instead. Review Files stay under about 600 lines. A file over the limit is split along a seam, not by moving code into a utils module. Long files hold several responsibilities; a utils module is a second place with no responsibility at all. Review

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Rule Why Checked by About 60 lines at most. A function that fits on one screen can be read and tested as one unit. Ruff, with the thresholds in ruff.toml: C901 (complexity above 10), PLR0912 (more than 12 branches), PLR0915 (more than 50 statements), PLR0913 (more than 6 arguments) No flag arguments (run(x, fast=True)). Write two functions, or pass a strategy object. A flag means the function does two things; every caller pays for both. PLR0913 caps the argument count; the flag itself is Review

ruff.toml is the only home of these thresholds. A PR that changes one updates this table.

Files that broke a complexity rule before the rules existed are listed under [lint.per-file-ignores] in ruff.toml, grouped by the epic that removes them. Do not add entries; fix the code instead.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Do not use another module's _private names. Add a public function to the owning module instead. A private name carries no promise; its owner changes it without looking for callers. Review (the import-graph test covers package edges, not names)

docs.title: Types and docstrings
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Type hints on every public function. Types document the interface and let mypy find mistakes before a test runs. mypy_test targets (tools/typecheck.bzl) where a package has one; Review elsewhere A package with a mypy_test stays clean; one declared strict = True stays clean in strict mode. Strict mode comes first to ipu_isa and the reference-model API. A type check that is allowed to fail stops being read. bazel test --test_tag_filters=typecheck //... Google-style docstrings (Args:, Returns:, Raises:) on public modules, classes and functions. One format reads the same everywhere and renders in the docs. Review

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Two kinds of error. A hardware fault (F-1 to F-9, see Faults) carries a fault ID and has an enable bit. A configuration error is raised at setup time, or, for a CR content no layout allows, in the check phase of the word that reads it, before any of its writes (ADR 0007). Both derive from IpuError. Callers tell a faulting program from a wrong setup by type alone. Review No assert for input validation. Raise an exception. python -O removes every assert. Review No bare except Exception: pass. It hides the fault the test or the user needs to see. Review

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Rule Why Checked by Test through public interfaces, not private helpers. A test of a private helper breaks on every refactor and proves nothing about the interface. Review Expected values come from an independent source: a hand-written table, a reference implementation, ml_dtypes. Never from the code under test. A value computed by the code under test only proves the code agrees with itself. Review Put a test in the default tier unless it repeats coverage a default-tier test already gives, or takes more than about 2 minutes on CI. Then it goes in the heavy tier (size = "enormous"). The default tier runs on every pull request and must stay fast; the heavy tier runs nightly. Review

The two tiers:

Tier Holds Command Default Every test except size enormous. CI runs it on every pull request. bazel test //... Heavy Size enormous tests. Runs nightly. bazel test --config=full //...

Run the heavy tier before review when a change touches code that only heavy-tier tests exercise.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
Rule Why Checked by A refactor PR changes no output, and its description says how that is proven (golden tests, or the full suite with digests). A reviewer cannot check by reading that a large refactor kept behaviour. Golden tests; the PR template asks for the proof A behaviour change is its own PR, labelled behaviour change. Mixed into a refactor, a behaviour change goes unnoticed. Review; the PR template asks for the label

The PR template asks for both; Code review says what the author and the reviewer check.

docs.title: Baselines
docs.text:
A baseline is a checked-in file that pins today's output. Its test fails on any change. The baselines are how a refactor PR proves it changes no output. A package keeps its baselines in test/baselines/, with the scripts that rewrite them beside them:

Baseline Location Update target Assembled-program digests src/ipu-as/test/baselines/asm_digests.json //src/ipu-as:update_asm_digests Field names, emulator field maps, enum descriptors src/ipu-as/test/baselines/*.json //src/ipu-as:update_decode_snapshots Disassembly text src/ipu-as/test/baselines/disassembly/ //src/ipu-as:update_disassembly_snapshots SV package golden src/ipu-gen/test/baselines/ipu_instr_pkg.sv, plus the EXPECTED_LOCALPARAMS table in test_sv_package_golden.py (edited by hand) //src/ipu-gen:update_sv_golden Generated artifacts src/ipu-gen/test/baselines/generated/ //src/ipu-gen:update_generated_artifacts The ISA view as JSON, and the F-1 table of the faults requirements page src/ipu-isa/test/baselines/spec_snapshot.json, docs/content/requirements/faults.md //src/ipu-isa:update_isa_baselines Conformance suite (programs, setups, expected traces) src/ipu-isa/conformance/ //src/ipu-emu:update_conformance The check command's JSON output (v1), the VS Code extension's contract src/ipu-as/test/baselines/check_json_v1.json none: a difference is a contract change; the test writes the new file to its undeclared outputs to copy over The assemble command's error output over the check corpus src/ipu-as/test/baselines/cli_assemble_errors.json none: the test writes the new file to its undeclared outputs to copy over Formatter output (the extension's corpus in full, every kernel as digests) src/ipu-as/test/baselines/format/ node vscode-ipu-asm/test/record-format.js Debugger TUI screens src/ipu-debug/test/baselines/tui/ none: recorded once, before E08-08; edited by hand

tools/update_baselines.sh runs every update target and then lists the baseline files that changed. A kernel of kernels/ has no baseline file: its tests hold every case to its golden (kernel.toml, [golden]), and its :assemble_<name> writes its program. The timing tests have no baseline file: their expected values are code, changed by hand in the behaviour PR that changes the timing rule.

Rule Why Checked by A PR labelled refactor modifies no baseline file. An unchanged baseline is the proof that the refactor changes no output. Regenerating a baseline to make a refactor pass hides the change it was there to catch. Review; the PR template asks for it A PR labelled behaviour change regenerates only the baselines it means to change. Its description says why each one changed, in one sentence. The reviewer reads each baseline diff as the effect of the change. Review; the PR template asks for the list Every *_WIDTH localparam of the SV package stays identical to the base, or the PR calls the change out as breaking. tools/sv_localparam_diff.sh <base-ref> prints nothing when they are identical. Each width is wire format for the downstream RTL repository (CLAUDE.md, "Generated SystemVerilog Package"). //src/ipu-gen:test_sv_package_golden; the diff script; Review A new update target is added to tools/update_baselines.sh. One command must regenerate every baseline. //tools:test_update_baselines

docs.title: Words
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Use the terms in the Glossary (GLOSSARY.md). Avoid the alternatives it lists, in new code and in docs. One name per concept; a different word makes a reader look for a different thing. //tools:test_glossary_adoption for the hand-written docs (avoided terms outside code; counts in tools/glossary_baseline.json may only go down); review for code Architecture decisions live in docs/adr/. Code does not contradict an accepted ADR; a change of decision is a new ADR. Decisions stay findable and are not re-argued in every PR. Review

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
Task Command Format bazel run //tools:ruff -- format Fix lint automatically bazel run //tools:ruff -- check --fix Check lint and format bazel test --test_tag_filters=lint //... (or bazel test //tools:lint) Type-check bazel test --test_tag_filters=typecheck //... Lower the glossary baseline after removing avoided terms from the docs bazel run //tools:glossary_baseline Refresh the dependency lock after editing a pyproject.toml bazel run //tools:update_requirements_lock

A commit that only reformats code goes into .git-blame-ignore-revs, with a comment naming the change; git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs makes git blame skip it. Runtime dependencies are also listed in the package's deps.bzl; //tools:test_deps_consistency fails if the two disagree.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Rule Why Checked by Pure Python and numpy. Speed comes from vectorising and from better data structures, not from compiled extensions. Every contributor can read, debug and build the code. Review A PR that claims a speed change pastes the bazel run //tools/bench:bench -- --quick table from before and after the change; a PR that changes only the emulator may paste the bazel run //src/ipu-emu:bench_emulator -- --quick table instead (the PR template's Performance section). A speed-up without numbers cannot be checked or kept. The nightly history (tools/bench/README.md) shows slow drift. Review

docs.title: Code review
docs.text: Every pull request uses the template in .github/pull_request_template.md, which GitHub fills in when the PR is opened. The rules code is checked against are on the Code conventions page.

docs.title: Author
docs.text:
1. Keep a PR small: one issue per PR.
  2. Fill in every section of the template.
  3. Mark the kind of change. A refactor changes no output; name the golden tests (or the full suite with digests) that prove it. A behaviour change is its own PR with the behaviour change label.
  4. Treat each golden update as a behaviour change. Give one sentence of justification per updated golden. The baseline rule and the one command that regenerates every baseline (tools/update_baselines.sh) are in Code conventions, Baselines.

  5. Run all tests locally, including the heavy tier, and say so in the template:

    bazel test --config=full //...                  # every test, including the nightly tier
bazel test --config=proto //...                 # if the emulator changed
bazel test --test_tag_filters=lint //...        # ruff lint and format

    If a run was not possible, say which part did not run and why. CI runs only the default tier; the heavy tier runs nightly, so a break there shows up only the next morning unless the author ran it.

  6. After an ISA change, check the generated SystemVerilog package as CLAUDE.md describes ("Generated SystemVerilog Package"). The *_WIDTH localparams stay identical to the base, or the PR calls the change out as breaking.

  7. When //tools:test_glossary_adoption reports fewer uses of an avoided term than its baseline, run bazel run //tools:glossary_baseline and commit tools/glossary_baseline.json. When it reports more, use the glossary term it names; a raised count in the baseline needs a reason in the PR.

docs.title: Reviewer
docs.text:
GitHub requests review from the owners of each path the PR touches, as listed in .github/CODEOWNERS.

Check the PR against the Code conventions and the issue's acceptance criteria. Leave what CI checks to CI: a formatting or lint remark is not a review comment.

CI checks (not review comments) The reviewer checks Formatting and lint (ruff, the thresholds in ruff.toml) The rules marked Review on the conventions page Type checks of packages with a mypy_test Test independence: expected values come from an independent source, not from the code under test The default test tier, including the glossary check on the docs (//tools:test_glossary_adoption) Names in code against GLOSSARY.md, and any raised count in tools/glossary_baseline.json The default tier in prototyping mode (--config=proto) The refactor-versus-behaviour split: a refactor PR changes no output and says how that is proven; a behaviour change is labelled and separate Docs drift tests (asm blocks assemble, commands are real, links resolve) The author's statement that all tests ran locally, and a reason for any part that did not One sentence of justification per golden update

docs.title: Merging
docs.text:
• The required checks are green.
  • One approval.
  • Squash or rebase, as the repository is set up.
  • A behaviour change that touches the SystemVerilog package (ipu_instr_pkg.sv): inform the downstream RTL owners. List renamed fields in a rename table and call out width changes as breaking.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: An agent that writes a PR description uses the mattpocock-skills:pr skill and fills in the template. An agent that reviews a branch or PR uses the mattpocock-skills:code-review skill, with this page and the conventions page as its standards.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
These docs use the terms below. Their source is GLOSSARY.md at the repository root.

The IPU is a 128-lane VLIW vector processor for neural-network inference. This repository defines its instruction set, assembles programs for it, emulates it, and holds the kernels that run on it.

docs.title: Program and encoding
docs.text:
Instruction word: One VLIW word fetched and executed per cycle. It holds one instruction per slot. Avoid: VLIW word, compound instruction, bundle, line

Slot: A fixed position in the instruction word that holds one instruction for one stage (COND, LR0–LR2, LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ, and the emulator-only AAQ_EXACT and BREAK). Avoid: lane (for slots), slot type, slot name

Instruction: One operation in one slot of an instruction word, written as a mnemonic and operands. Avoid: inst, instr, op (in prose)

Mnemonic: The upper-case name of an instruction. Control-stage instructions use plain names (ADD, BEQ); datapath instructions use UNIT.OP[.VARIANT] (LD.MULT, ACC.ADD.FIRST). Mnemonics never contain underscores.

Pseudo-instruction: A mnemonic the assembler expands into real instructions (B, BZ, BNZ, BGT.S, BLE.S). It has no opcode.

HALT instruction: The COND instruction that ends a kernel: the kernel is done when the word that holds it retires. Not the host's HALT command, which stops a running kernel in the HALTED state.

Hardware word: The part of the instruction word that real hardware decodes: every slot tagged hardware. Avoid: RTL word

Emulator word: The full instruction word the emulator decodes: the hardware word followed by the emulator-only slots.

Hardware / emulator-only / assembler-only: The tag every slot, instruction and element format carries in the ISA package. Emulator-only parts exist only in the emulator; assembler-only parts are pseudo-instructions. Avoid: simulation-only, debug-only

pc: The index of the instruction word being executed. Avoid: program counter, PC (in code)

docs.title: Machine
docs.text:
Stage: A pipeline unit that executes one slot kind: Control (LR and COND), LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ. The AaQ stage activates, quantizes and stores its own row (ADR 0007); there is no STORE stage.

Control stage: The stage that executes LR and COND instructions: loop-register arithmetic and branches.

Lane: One of the 128 parallel element positions of a vector.

Element: The value one lane holds. Its width depends on the element format.

Element format: The numeric encoding of elements for a run, one per mode (ADR 0007): NX8 on hardware, and the emulator-only FP32. It fixes element width, row width and whether rows carry metadata. INT8, INT32 and the former biased E1–E7 formats are gone. Avoid: dtype, wide mode, wide-vector debug mode, narrow mode

Mode: Which element format a run is in: NX8 (the hardware) or FP32 (emulator-only, for debugging a kernel that will run in NX8). Chosen when the state is built; every load and store moves one row of the mode.

NX8: The hardware's element format: a row of 128 elements of at most 8 bits plus a metadata word. Each element's exponent is a distance below the row's scale; its type (sign, exponent width fe, width W, dynamic) comes from a QF half.

NX8 type: One QF value, such as e4 (signed, fe 4, 8 bits) or dynamic (fe 1 or 2 per row). A kernel names its NX8 types in kernel.toml formats (e1–e7, dynamic, s<sign>e<fe>w<bits>), beside fp32.

Metadata word: The 16-bit word each NX8 row carries: scale[7:0] (an e8m0 exponent, bias 127) and dynamic_exponent[8]. XMEM keeps one per 128-byte unit; LD.MULT copies it into R0, R1 or an R_CYCLIC slot, and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE writes it.

QF (quantization format): A 16-bit CR half naming an NX8 type: num_bits[3:0], exp_format[7:4], sign[11:8], dynamic[15:12]. MULT decodes its vectors with one, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE quantizes to one. The FP32 mode ignores it.

DS (data structure): A 16-bit CR half shaping a vector operation: valid_elements[7:0], num_partitions[9:8] (1, 2, 4 or 8), mask_type[11:10], valid_partitions[15:12]. By convention CR15.L. It replaces the old 32-bit dstructure.

CR half: The low or high 16 bits of a CR, written CR13.L or CR13.H. DS and QF operands always name one; an LR or COND source may read one, sign-extended.

MULT constant: A CR read as a scalar by MULT.VE, MULT.EE or MULT.RC.VE: in NX8 one element with its own scale and type, in FP32 a float32. CR0 and CR1 read as 0.0 and 1.0 in both modes.

Accumulator type: FP32 in both modes: MULT expands each NX8 element to FP32, and MULT results and R_ACC hold FP32.

Element codec: The encoding of one NX8 element and back: decode a code with its row's scale, quantize a row with round-to-nearest (ties up) and saturation. It lives in ipu_isa.nx8.

Lane codec: The emulator's numerics for one mode (ipu_emu.numerics): decodes a row of lanes (in NX8 with the QF and the row's metadata), multiplies and accumulates. Handlers are written against it.

XMEM: The IPU's external memory, addressed in rows. Avoid: DRAM, main memory

Row: The XMEM unit one vector occupies: 128 elements, so 128 bytes and a metadata word in NX8 and 512 bytes in FP32. Avoid: word, chunk, line (for XMEM units)

LR (loop register): One of LR0–LR15, the 32-bit scalar registers that Control-stage instructions compute with: loop counters, row indices, addresses.

CR (configuration register): One of CR0–CR15, 32-bit scalar registers the host sets before a run and kernels only read, each also two CR halves. CR0 is 0 and CR1 is 1.

dstructure: The architecture specs' name for what the ISA calls the DS: see DS.

Cycle start: Register values as they were when the current instruction word began. The Control stage reads LRs at cycle start; MULT reads R0, R1, R_CYCLIC, their metadata and R_MASK at cycle start. Avoid: snapshot (in prose), pre-instruction value

Forwarded value: A value written earlier in the same cycle and seen by a later stage in that cycle: post-LR-write LRs outside the Control stage, MULT_RES in ACC, R_ACC in AAQ and AAQ_EXACT. Avoid: live value

Timing contract: The rules for which value, cycle start or forwarded, each register read sees within one cycle, with the slot execution order (ADR 0002). Declared in ipu_isa.timing; each instruction declares its register reads and writes.

Known deviation: A read where today's emulator differs from the timing contract, listed in KNOWN_DEVIATIONS with the E04 issue that removes it. The list can only shrink. It is empty today.

docs.title: Faults and events
docs.text:
Fault: An illegal state the IPU detects, numbered F-1 to F-9 in the requirements. An enabled fault halts and records its code and pc; a disabled one sets a sticky flag. Avoid: exception, trap, illegal program error

Arithmetic event: Accumulator overflow, a NaN result or quantization saturation. It never halts; it sets a sticky flag.

Configuration error: A mistake detected before the first cycle, such as an unsupported element format, invalid kernel parameters or ACTIVATE.EXACT in an NX8 program (refused at load), or in a word's check phase, such as an invalid QF or DS half (ADR 0007). It is not a fault.

docs.title: Kernels
docs.text:
Kernel: An assembly program implementing one operation, plus its declaration in kernel.toml. Avoid: app, application, harness (for the kernel itself)

Family: A group of kernels for one kind of operation (projections, convolutions, softmax), often sharing one template. One family, mobilevit, has no kernels: it holds the chain tests that run several families' kernels together.

Variant: A kernel defined as an entry in a family's registry over a shared template, differing only in parameters such as shape or activation.

Region: A named block of rows in XMEM that holds one kernel input or output. Avoid: buffer, image, blob

ABI: The mapping from a kernel's named values (region bases, sizes, scalars) to the CRs its program reads. Avoid: CR map, calling convention

Case: One concrete test run of a kernel: parameter values, inputs (generated or user-supplied) and how the output is judged. Avoid: test vector, scenario

Reference: The independent computation of a kernel's expected output, normally in PyTorch, rounded to the element format. Avoid: golden model, oracle

Golden: The expected output a case is compared against: the reference result or a user-supplied file.

Tolerance tier: A named, shared accuracy bound for comparing a kernel output with its golden in a given element format.

Harness: The framework that runs a kernel case: places regions, packs data, programs CRs, assembles, runs and compares.

docs.title: Emulator as reference model
docs.text:
Reference model: The emulator used through its stable API as the expected behaviour for RTL verification.

Commit record: What one instruction word did: pc before and after, the instruction retired in each slot, register and XMEM writes, and any halt or fault.

Trace: The sequence of commit records of one run.

Prototyping mode: An opt-in emulator mode that skips work proven not to change results, for faster runs.

docs.title: kernel.toml
docs.text:
Every key a kernel's kernel.toml takes, and a family's registry.toml. For a walk-through that builds a kernel step by step, see Write a kernel.

A kernel.toml declares everything about a kernel except its program: its parameters and their domain, its input, output and scratch regions, which register holds each value, its cases, and how outputs are checked. The harness reads it once (ipu_harness.manifest.load_manifest) and every later step reads that checked view. An error names the file, the line and the key, for example kernels/elementwise/scale/kernel.toml:14: [abi] binds CR1, a hardwired constant. An unknown key names the closest valid one.

The text below comes from the loader's own documentation, and the table of keys from the key lists it checks against, so the page changes when the schema does.

docs.title: [kernel] (required)
docs.text: op (str, required): the operation, also the shared reference's name. formats (list, required): the variants the kernel runs in (ipu_harness.variants, ADR 0007): fp32 (FP32 mode), and NX8 element types e1..e7 (signed, 8 bits), dynamic and s<sign>e<fe>w<bits>. asm (path): the program, default <folder>.asm. stages ("file.py:fn"): a multi-program pipeline (E06-14). cost: what routing (E06-16) minimises among the kernels that accept a query: a number (negative to prefer a kernel), or an expression in the shape grammar over integer parameter and derived names; default 0.

docs.title: [params.<name>] (or <name> = { ... } under [params])
docs.text: type (required): int, float, bool or str. min and max (int and float), multiple_of (int, at least 1), choices (a non-empty list, each in the domain), default, and unit: count (default), rows or bytes (bytes only for a kernel in BYTE_UNIT_KERNELS, L16). Floats are finite. query_required (bool, default false): a routing query that leaves the parameter out is refused at this kernel, naming it, whatever its default; a case takes its own or the default value as before.

docs.title: [inputs.<name>], [outputs.<name>], [scratch.<name>]
docs.text: shape (non-empty list, required): positive ints, or expressions over parameter and derived names in E06-03's grammar ("rows * 4", "ceil(k / 128)"). row: pin the region's first XMEM row (Q81), an int or an expression like a shape's, which may also read row_bytes, the bytes of one row in the case's format ("131072 / row_bytes" pins the region at byte 0x20000 in every variant: a legacy layout). after ("<tensor>"): place the region right after that tensor's in placement order (by default inputs, then outputs, then scratch, each in file order), so scratch can come before an output; not with row. when ("<bool param>" or "not <bool param>", such terms joined by and, and those joined by or: "has_bias or apply_relu", "not has_bias and not apply_relu"): the tensor exists only in a case where that holds; otherwise it is not placed, generated, passed to the reference or bound. pack (inputs and outputs): a named pack transform (E06-05); an output's lays out the stored rows that ipu_harness.packing.unpack reads back. store (outputs): element, the only value (accumulator left with ST.ACC, ADR 0007). fill (scratch): the value the region is filled with, default 0: a number, or an expression over int and float parameters and derived values in the shape grammar, evaluated exactly when the case is planned ("-1 / channels", whole or not; a float parameter is its exact binary value) and rounded to the format when stored. bytes (scratch, not with fill): "file.py:fn", or "../file.py:fn" in the family's folder as a generator may be, fn(plan) returns the region's exact starting bytes, format-blind (a lane mask, which no element value can carry). The runner writes either through ipu_harness.packing.region_fill. Scratch regions are placed and filled, never compared. range (inputs): [lo, hi] for the generated values in every variant, or { e4 = [lo, hi], nx8 = [lo, hi] } per variant or per mode (E06-08); lo may equal hi (a constant input).

docs.title: [abi]
docs.text: <name> = "CR2" .. "CR15", or "LR0" .. "LR15" (a preset, E06-06). CR0 and CR1 are hardwired constants and cannot be bound, except that a tensor pinned at a literal row = 0 may bind CR0: the program reads its base through the hardwired 0 and nothing is written. A binding may be a table with register and optional keys: a tensor's may add offset, { register = "CR2", offset = -1 } for its base row plus an int (in a unit = "bytes" kernel the base and the offset count bytes). Any binding may be a table with when (as a tensor's): it binds only in a case where that holds; a conditional tensor's binding takes the tensor's condition. Two bindings may share a register only when their conditions exclude each other (bias and not bias; a condition with or excludes another only when every term of one contradicts every term of the other), or when both are tensors pinned at literal rows that put the same value in it (acc at row = 8 and relu = { register = "CR7", offset = -12 } at row = 20: the program reaches relu from acc's base). A float parameter (an element scalar) binds a CR. Every key names a parameter, a tensor or a derived value, and every tensor is bound (its base row must reach the program), itself or through a bound [derived] value that reads its base().

docs.title: [derived]
docs.text: <name> = "<expression>" over parameters and earlier derived values, in the shape grammar (E06-06). An expression may also read base(<tensor>), the region's base row once placed (in bytes in a unit = "bytes" kernel, as a tensor's binding): such a value, and any that reads it, is placed (KernelManifest.placed), known only when the registers are written, so only [abi] binds it; a shape, a pin or the cost cannot read it. w1 = "base(weights) + 1" gives one region several offset registers, which a { register, offset } binding cannot. A value that reads row_bytes (the bytes of one XMEM row in the case's variant: 128 in NX8, 512 in FP32) or case_qf (the case variant's QF half-CR, 0 in FP32) is placed too. The helpers ds(), qf(), constant() and halves() (ipu_harness.expressions) build DS, QF, MULT-constant and two-half CR values.

docs.title: [cases.<name>]
docs.text: Parameter values: a scalar, or a non-empty list (a sweep axis). Reserved keys: formats (a non-empty subset of the kernel's variants), inputs and expected (tensor name to a user file, Q82; an expected may instead be "file.py:fn", or "../file.py:fn" in the family's folder, whose fn(plan) returns the output's values in the case's format: a golden kept in another encoding, such as fully_connected's .bin), generator ("file.py:fn", or "../file.py:fn" in the family's folder, a generator its kernels share), tier (default or nightly, Q73). [cases.default] is required.

docs.title: [benchmark] (optional, E06-11)
docs.text: points: a non-empty list of tables of parameter values, each over the default case's, which must take one value each (one run per point and format, paired, not swept; a point keeps the default case's generator but not its files, and may not change a registry entry's fixed parameter); per: an int parameter the report divides cycles by; max_cycles: each run's limit (the model's by default). It needs a [golden] reference or op, which each point is held to; no two points may be equal. python -m ipu_harness.cli KERNEL --benchmark (bazel run :<kernel> -- --benchmark) runs them; ipu_harness.benchmark.

docs.title: [golden] (optional)
docs.text:
reference ("file.py:fn"; default reference.py:reference when the kernel has a reference.py) or op (a shared reference in ipu_kernels.reference), not both; tolerance (format to a tier name of ipu_harness.tolerance.TIERS, or a table overriding a tier's numbers: tier and why (required), rtol, atol, ulps; a key is a variant the kernel runs in, or a mode (nx8) for its variants without their own key; an override may set only what compare reads for that variant: ulps (NX8 steps) only in NX8, and then not rtol/atol; a variant not listed is compared at EXACT).

Every declared name (parameter, tensor, derived value) is an identifier that does not start with _ and is not cr, lr or a reserved case key. Every file path stays inside the kernel directory: .. and absolute paths are refused (checked lexically). A case generator's file that is not in the kernel's folder is its family folder's (kernels/<family>/gen.py), as a pack transform may be the family folder's pack.py: a family's templates share them. An unknown section or key is an error that names the closest valid one.

A family registry.toml entry (E06-17, ipu_harness.family) loads its template with overrides: name, formats (a subset), params (fixed values: each becomes the parameter's only choice and its value in every case; a default the template gives stays, so a query that leaves the parameter out means that default, else the fixed value stands in) and cases (the template cases the entry runs, default among them).

docs.title: Every key
docs.text:
The tables and keys the loader accepts; any other key is an error that names the closest valid one.

Table Keys [kernel] op, formats, asm, stages, cost [params.<name>] type, min, max, multiple_of, choices, default, unit, query_required [inputs.<name>] shape, row, after, when, pack, range [outputs.<name>] shape, row, after, when, pack, store [scratch.<name>] shape, row, after, when, fill, bytes [abi] table binding register, offset, when [cases.<name>] (reserved keys) formats, inputs, expected, generator, tier [golden] reference, op, tolerance [golden] tolerance override tier, rtol, atol, ulps, why

docs.title: registry.toml
docs.text:
A family declares its variants, kernels that differ from a template kernel only in parameter values, as entries of kernels/<family>/registry.toml. An entry is its template's kernel.toml with the entry's params fixed: each becomes the parameter's only value. A default the template gives stays, so a query that leaves the parameter out means that default, and an entry fixing another value refuses it. Without one the entry's value stands in, and a query that leaves out a parameter its entries fix differently is refused for it. The entry runs the template's cases with those values, in the template's formats unless it narrows them. Its Bazel targets are //kernels/<family>:<name>, :<name>_nightly and :assemble_<name>.

# kernels/projections/registry.toml
[[kernel]]
name = "proj_ffn1_192_p4"        # kernel name == Bazel target name
template = "proj_p4"             # kernels/projections/proj_p4/ (an ordinary kernel folder)
params = { k = 192, n_out = 384, n_tok = 64, n_tg = 1, activation = "silu" }
doc = "Layer 4 FFN1"             # one line, for the kernel page and query output
formats = ["fp32"]               # optional: a subset of the template's
cases = ["default", "edge"]      # optional: the template cases it runs, default among them

A [[kernel]] entry takes name, template, params, formats, cases, doc.

Bazel reads the entries from the generated registry.bzl beside the TOML. After editing registry.toml, rewrite it:

bazel run //kernels:update_registry_bzl

The family's registry_bzl_test fails while registry.bzl is stale.

docs.title: Reference model API
docs.text:
ipu_emu.reference is the emulator's stable interface for RTL verification. A cocotb testbench resets the model, loads a program, sets registers and XMEM, steps it one word at a time and compares each commit record with what the RTL retired. How-to: use the reference model from cocotb walks through a testbench.

API version 2.0.0 (ipu_emu.reference.API_VERSION); commit record schema 1.1.0, trace header schema 1.0.0.

The API, schema and fault sections of this page are generated from the code and the schema files, so they always match the version above.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
The contract is:

  • the names in ipu_emu.reference.__all__, with their signatures, dataclass fields and enum values;
  • the commit records step() returns (ipu_emu.commit), field by field;
  • the commit record and trace header schemas, which are language-neutral JSON Schema files in ipu_isa/schemas/.

Everything else in ipu_emu is internal and can change in any release. The other symbols on this page (TraceWriter, the schema helpers, the argument types) are listed because the contract hands them out or takes them, not as a separate promise.

API_VERSION is a semantic version:

  • Major (breaking): a public name removed or renamed, a parameter removed or made required, a field removed, renamed or retyped, or a meaning changed (a method that now refuses what it accepted, a field that now counts something else). Version 2.0.0 is the run modes of ADR 0007: ElementFormat keeps FP32 and NX8 (value "nx8") and loses INT8, E1–E7 and INT32, so the constructor and reset() take one of the two modes, and the constructor defaults to NX8 instead of INT8; load_program() refuses a program that uses the FP32-only ACTIVATE.EXACT when the model runs in NX8 mode, and reset() refuses to switch a model holding such a program to NX8; the post_aaq_reg register bank is removed, and read_register() and write_register() take the r_meta, r_cyclic_meta and aaq_lut banks as bytes; and a commit record's slots no longer include store or acc_store, and can include aaq_exact. It also adds the XMEM metadata side store: read_xmem_metadata(), write_xmem_metadata() and the CommitRecord.xmem_meta_writes field (default empty), with the commit record schema's optional xmem_meta_writes (schema 1.1.0). The other method signatures and commit record fields are 1.4.0's.
  • Minor: an addition that leaves every existing call working, such as a new method, a new optional parameter or a new dataclass field with a default. Version 1.1.0 added Stats and stats(); 1.2.0 added the flag and enable reads (fault_enabled(), fault_flags(), arith_flags()), trace_header(), and TraceWriter and read_trace to __all__; 1.3.0 added debug_run(), attach_alias_profile(), alias_profile() and the RunResult.quit field (default False); 1.4.0 added observe_xmem_reads(), which reports each XMEM read the program makes (a commit record carries writes only; the Cycle Inspector's recorder shows the reads). Nothing earlier changed.

debug_run() is the one escape hatch for tools such as the debugger: its callback receives the emulator's internal state, and that argument's type, like its control argument's, is outside the contract. The method's signature and what it returns follow the version.

Each schema carries its own version, at the end of its $id. An optional field added is a minor bump; a field removed or renamed, or a meaning changed, is a major one. A trace header names the commit record schema's version (schema_version).

Two tests hold the promise. src/ipu-emu/test/test_reference_api_contract.py pins every public name, signature and record field under the version that introduced it, so a surface change fails until a new version's entry matches. src/ipu-emu/test/test_commit.py pins each schema file's bytes to its version. A strict mypy test (//src/ipu-emu:mypy_reference) types the module.

docs.title: A lockstep test
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from ipu_emu.reference import ReferenceModel
from ipu_isa.formats import ElementFormat


async def test_lockstep(dut):
    model = ReferenceModel()
    model.reset(ElementFormat.NX8)
    model.load_program(Path("prog.bin").read_bytes())  # a program file, or its words as ints
    model.write_register("lr", 5, index=0)              # LR0 = 5
    model.write_xmem(0, bytes(range(128)))              # XMEM row 0

    while True:
        record = model.step()                           # one word's CommitRecord
        rtl = await rtl_retire(dut)                     # your testbench's own monitor
        assert record.to_json() == rtl
        if record.outcome in ("halt", "fault"):         # model.status names the fault
            break

step() returns the word's commit record, the same object a run writes to a trace. Its outcome is retired, halt or fault: the model never stops at a BREAK slot, so break does not occur. A stepped record's cycle counts the words since the last reset() or load_program(); in a trace run() writes, it counts the trace's records, as the schema says.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• The model is HALTED after a reset, a program load or a HALT word, and RUNNING once stepped. After a HALT word or a fault, status.pc is that word's PC.
  • The host accesses the IPU refuses with an AXI error raise ConfigurationError: writing a register, XMEM or a program while running; writing CR0 or CR1 (constants in hardware); a bank, index or range that does not exist; a value that does not fit.
  • After a fault, step(), run(), load_program() and the register and XMEM writes raise ConfigurationError until reset() (IPU-FLT-7). After a HALT word, step() and run() raise it until reset() or load_program().
  • No method returns an emulator object: values are ints, floats, bytes, the dataclasses below and CommitRecord.
  • Registers are named by bank, as ipu_isa.registers names them (lr: LR0-LR15, cr: CR0-CR15, r: R0-R1, ...), and index picks the register within the bank. r_wide_debug and r_cyclic_wide_debug are emulator-only banks: they hold the operands of the FP32 mode, which the hardware does not have; r_meta and r_cyclic_meta hold the row metadata of R0, R1 and each R_CYCLIC slot in the NX8 mode.

Run one word. A BREAK slot never stops it (Q39): the word retires. A step has no cycle limit (F-9 is run's); its word counts toward the statistics' cycles.

Returns

Arguments

  • max_cycles: The cycle limit of this run: None keeps the model's, 0 disables it.
  • trace: Where to write each word's commit record, as it retires; None keeps none. Its records number from 0 (the schema's cycle: records before this one in the trace).

Raises

docs.title: ReferenceModel.debug_run()
docs.text:
ReferenceModel.debug_run(callback: DebugCallback, break_on_entry: bool = False, *, max_cycles: int | None = None, control: RunControl | None = None) -> RunResult

Run as run does, stopping for a debugger (1.3.0).

The one escape hatch for tools such as ipu_debug: at each stop (a breakpoint or run target in control, a BREAK slot that fires, a step, or the entry when break_on_entry) it calls callback(state, cycles) with the emulator's internal state and the words retired so far, and the callback's DebugAction says whether to continue, step or quit (ipu_emu.emulator.run_with_debug's contract). Unlike the rest of this API, the callback's argument type and control's are internal and may change in any release; the method itself, and what it returns, follow API_VERSION.

Arguments

  • callback: Called at each stop; returns a DebugAction.
  • break_on_entry: Stop before the first word.
  • max_cycles: The cycle limit of this run, as for run.
  • control: The breakpoints and run target to honour, shared with a debugger frontend (ipu_emu.run_control.RunControl); a fresh one when None.

Returns

  • The status the run stopped in, the words it retired, and quit: whether the callback returned QUIT or Ctrl-C ended the run. A Ctrl-C at a stop leaves the model between words; one during a word may leave it partly done, and a later step or run re-runs it from the start (its finished part applies twice, and the statistics other than cycles may already count it), so reset or load_program when results must be exact. A QUIT pauses the model where it stopped (RUNNING): a later step or run carries on from that PC. A callback that also moves the PC past IMEM (ipu_debug's quit) leaves the model HALTED there: the host may write again, and stepping needs reset or load_program. A callback that moves the PC past IMEM without QUIT leaves the model RUNNING there: its next fetch faults F-2.

Raises

  • ConfigurationError: As step.

class Stats  # ipu_emu.reference.Stats

The run statistics since the program started (1.1.0).

They count every word retired since the last ReferenceModel.reset or ReferenceModel.load_program, stepped or run (a faulting word retires nothing, so it adds nothing). They depend on operand values (a multiply by a constant 1.0 is an identity multiply), so a commit record does not carry them.

A frozen dataclass.

Field Type Default Meaning cycles int The words retired. mult_active_cycles int Words whose MULT slot was not NOP. acc_active_cycles int Words whose ACC slot was not NOP. xmem_reads int XMEM rows read. xmem_writes int XMEM rows written. mult_lane_ops int Multiplier lanes that carried data (passed the mask and lay within valid_elements), summed over every multiply. mult_identity_lane_ops int The part of mult_lane_ops that multiplied by a constant 1.0 (data routing, not MACs). lane_occupancy float mult_lane_ops / (cycles * LANES); 0.0 before the first word. effective_mac_utilization float (mult_lane_ops - mult_identity_lane_ops) / (cycles * LANES), the fraction of peak MACs retired; 0.0 before the first word.
