docs.title: Commit record and trace schema
docs.text:
A commit record's JSON form (CommitRecord.to_json()) is a document of the commit record schema. A trace is a JSON Lines file: a header line of the trace header schema, then one commit record per word. Download the schema files to validate either with any JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) validator.

IPU commit record, version 1.1.0 (commit_record.v1.json): One retired VLIW word (E04-29). Integers up to 32 bits are JSON numbers; wider data are lowercase hex strings, little-endian. Register names are ipu_isa's. NOP slots are omitted. A write is a range the word wrote, with its value at the end of the cycle. A faulting word has no effect (precise faults), so a fault record has no writes.

Field Type Required Meaning cycle integer (≥ 0) yes Records before this one in the trace. pc_before integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The word's PC. pc_after integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The PC of the next word. slots array of object yes The word's ops, one per non-NOP slot. slots[].slot string yes The slot, as ipu_isa.slots names it. slots[].mnemonic string yes The op's mnemonic. slots[].fields object of integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The encoded operand values, by operand name. slots[].tag "emulator" no Present only on an op with no hardware equivalent. reg_writes array of object yes The registers the word wrote, at their end-of-cycle values. reg_writes[].register string yes The bank, as ipu_isa.registers names it. reg_writes[].index integer (≥ 0) yes, in form 1 of 2 A scalar register (lr, cr): the register within the bank. reg_writes[].value integer (0 to 4294967295) yes, in form 1 of 2 A scalar register: its unsigned 32-bit value. reg_writes[].tag "emulator" no Present only on a register with no hardware equivalent (wide-vector debug). reg_writes[].offset integer (≥ 0) yes, in form 2 of 2 A vector register: the first byte written, within the bank. reg_writes[].data string (^([0-9a-f]{2})*$) yes, in form 2 of 2 A vector register: the bytes written. xmem_writes array of object yes The XMEM ranges the word wrote. xmem_writes[].address integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The first XMEM byte written. xmem_writes[].data string (^([0-9a-f]{2})*$) yes The bytes written. outcome one of "retired", "break", "halt", "fault" yes break: the word's BREAK slot fired, and the word retired when the run went on. halt: a HALT word retired. fault: the word faulted (fault says which). fault null or object yes The fault the word raised, or null. fault.id string (^F-[1-9]$) yes The fault ID, as the fault list writes it. fault.pc integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The faulting word's PC. arith_events array of string yes Arithmetic events of the word (E04-23); empty until they are modelled. xmem_meta_writes array of object no Optional (1.1.0): the XMEM metadata words the word wrote, one per 128-byte unit, at their end-of-cycle values. A record with none may leave the field out. xmem_meta_writes[].address integer (0 to 4294967295) yes The first byte of the 128-byte XMEM unit the word describes. xmem_meta_writes[].value integer (0 to 65535) yes The unit's 16-bit metadata word (ADR 0007: scale[7:0], dynamic_exponent[8]).
  • When outcome is "fault": fault is an object, reg_writes is empty, xmem_writes is empty, xmem_meta_writes is empty. Otherwise fault is null.

IPU trace header, version 1.0.0 (trace.v1.json): A trace is JSON Lines: this header on the first line, then one commit record (commit_record schema) per line (E04-29).

Field Type Required Meaning schema_version string (^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$) yes The commit record schema's version. isa_digest string (^[0-9a-f]{64}$) yes SHA-256 of the ISA definition (ipu_isa.trace_schema.isa_digest). format string yes The element format the program ran in. program_digest string (^[0-9a-f]{64}$) yes SHA-256 of the program as it is loaded: each IMEM word up to the program length, packed little-endian in its emulator word width (ipu_isa.codec.word.word_bytes()), an empty word as zeros. emulator_version string yes The version of the model that wrote the trace (ipu_emu.trace.EMULATOR_VERSION for this emulator).

arith_events holds the names of ipu_isa.faults.ArithmeticEvent: acc_overflow, nan_result, quant_saturation, sorted. An event never halts the model.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text:
A faulting word's commit record has outcome fault and names the fault in fault.id; status.fault is the same fault as a FaultId. These are the IDs of the fault list; the emulator section of Faults says what the model checks for each.

ID FaultId Fault Detected in In the model F-1 FaultId.F1 A slot holds a reserved opcode or a reserved operand encoding. ctrl Reported. F-2 FaultId.F2 CTRL fetches at a PC at or beyond the program length, by sequential flow, branch or BR. ctrl Reported. F-3 FaultId.F3 Two LR lanes of one word write the same LR. ctrl Reported. F-4 FaultId.F4 The index of LD.MULT.CYCLIC is not 0, 128, 256 or 384. ctrl Reported. F-5 FaultId.F5 ACC.RESHAPE has a mask above 8, or a participating source or destination index of 128 or more. ctrl Reported. F-6 FaultId.F6 A load or a store addresses a table that is not configured, or a row beyond the table size. cache_agent Reported. F-7 FaultId.F7 A load addresses a write-only table, or a store addresses a read-only table. cache_agent Never raised: the emulator has no table configuration, so no table is read-only or write-only. F-8 FaultId.F8 A word stalls for longer than a programmable limit. cache_agent Not modelled: never reported; the emulator has no stall model (OQ-28). F-9 FaultId.F9 A kernel runs for more cycles than a programmable limit. ctrl Reported.

docs.title: Conformance suite
docs.text:
src/ipu-isa/conformance/ holds the ISA's expected behaviour as data: for each case a program (program.asm, program.bin), its starting state (setup.json, schema setup.schema.json) and the trace of its run (expected.trace.jsonl). No case contains Python, so another implementation (the RTL under cocotb, another model) needs only these files and the schemas.

To run the suite against another implementation, for each case:

  1. Skip it if setup.json has "emulator_only": true.
  2. Reset in the case's format and load program.bin.
  3. Zero every register and XMEM byte (CR0 and CR1 aside), then write the registers, XMEM regions and XMEM row metadata words of setup.json and set its fault enables.
  4. Run until HALT, a fault or max_cycles, recording a commit record per word.
  5. Compare the header's schema_version, isa_digest, format and program_digest with the expected trace's, then each record, field by field.

The suite's README.md has the details of each step. bazel test //src/ipu-emu:test_conformance runs every case through this API.

docs.title: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, ACTIVATE.EXACT and LD.LUT
docs.text:
The AaQ stage activates the accumulator, quantizes the result and stores it: one instruction does all three, and no register stages the result (ADR 0007). The emulator follows the AaQ architecture spec; where the microarchitecture spec disagrees, the difference is an open question (OQ-42).

Instruction Slot Tag Modes Stores ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE AAQ HARDWARE NX8 and FP32 one row: 128 NX8 bytes and the row's metadata word, or 128 FP32 values LD.LUT AAQ HARDWARE both nothing: loads one LUT segment from XMEM ACTIVATE.EXACT AAQ_EXACT EMULATOR FP32 only one row of 128 FP32 values 
    LD.LUT 0 CR4 LR0 ;;                             # LUT segment 0 <- row CR4 + LR0
    ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR15.L CR14.L CR2 LR1 ;; # relu, quantize, store row CR2 + LR1
    ACTIVATE.EXACT silu CR15.L CR3 LR1 ;;           # FP32 mode only: exact silu, store

The instruction reference has each instruction's operands, operation and register reads: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, LD.LUT and ACTIVATE.EXACT.

docs.title: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
docs.text:
Syntax: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activation_fn ds qf table_id table_offset.

  • activation_fn is the 3-bit function of the architecture spec: identity, relu, relu6, reciprocal, rsqrt, exp2 or generic (encodings 0–6; 7 is reserved). The keyword order is AAQ_ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES in src/ipu-isa/src/ipu_isa/activations.py, the operand type AaqActivationFn.
  • ds is the DS half (CR15.L by convention) naming the active elements; qf the QF half naming the NX8 output format (Configuration registers). Both always name a half: a bare CR15 is an assembler error.
  • table_id (a CR) and table_offset (an LR) give the row, CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset] (OQ-8).

Operation. The instruction reads the forwarded R_ACC (this word's ACC result, timing model) and leaves it unchanged.

  1. Activate each active element with the architecture spec's special cases (§4.3.1): reciprocal and rsqrt of a subnormal or zero input add the smallest epsilon, 2^-127, with the input's sign; of ±inf they are 0; rsqrt of a negative input is NaN; exp2(-inf) is 0.
  2. Quantize (NX8 mode) the active elements to one row in the QF half's format (§4.3.2): the row's scale comes from the largest magnitude, each element is rounded to nearest with ties half up, and a dynamic format picks the exponent width of the row by the §4.3.2.3 rule, with errors measured in units of the row's scale (OQ-49) (ipu_isa.nx8.encode_row).
  3. Store the 128 bytes and the row's metadata word (scale[7:0], dynamic_exponent[8]) at the row. In the FP32 mode the activated row is stored as 128 FP32 values (512 bytes) instead, with no metadata, and qf is ignored.

Inactive elements are written as 0 in both modes: the architecture spec writes NaN, which NX8 cannot hold (OQ-36).

What is an error. ±inf saturates to the largest magnitude and is left out of the scale; a saturation sets the QUANT_SATURATION arithmetic event. An invalid DS or QF half is a configuration error, raised in the word's check phase: the word leaves the state as a fault does. A row outside XMEM is fault F-6, found in the same phase. A NaN to quantize in NX8 (for example rsqrt of a negative input), exp2 of a positive input, and generic with no declared function depend on R_ACC, which the same word's ACC forwards. They are emulator errors raised when ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE executes, after the word's LR, LOAD, MULT and ACC writes have landed.

The LUT and generic. The hardware evaluates generic through the LUT that five LD.LUT loads fill. The 17-bit entry format and the interpolation are not published yet (OQ-38), so every function, generic included, is evaluated with exact math. generic computes the function the test declares as loaded:

from ipu_emu.activations import AaqOptions
from ipu_emu.ipu_state import IpuState

state = IpuState(aaq=AaqOptions(generic=lambda x: x / (1 + abs(x))))

docs.title: LD.LUT
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.LUT lut_addr table_id table_offset.

LD.LUT copies the first 128 bytes (1024 bits) of row CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset] into LUT segment lut_addr (0–4; 5–7 are reserved). Segments 0–3 hold table bits; segment 4 holds the last 256 table bits and the 46-bit LUT metadata (max_exp_num, neg_c, pos_c, range_mode, neg_mode, pos_mode). It reads no row metadata and scales nothing, in both modes.

Both specs load the segment from R_ACC; the hardware reads XMEM, and so does the emulator (OQ-39). LD.LUT and an LD.* of the LOAD slot share the XMEM read port, so a word that holds both is an assembler error.

ipu_isa.lut.lut_image(fn, range_mode, range_exp) builds the five rows that load a function. The entry bits it writes are provisional until the entry format is published (ipu_isa/lut.py):

from ipu_isa.lut import lut_image

rows = lut_image(lambda x: x / (1 + abs(x)), range_mode=0, range_exp=3)
assert len(rows) == 5 and all(len(row) == 128 for row in rows)

docs.title: ACTIVATE.EXACT (emulator only)
docs.text:
Syntax: ACTIVATE.EXACT activation_fn ds table_id table_offset.

ACTIVATE.EXACT applies the exact Python activation (apply_activation in src/ipu-emu/src/ipu_emu/activations.py) to the active elements of the forwarded R_ACC and stores the row as 128 FP32 values at CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset], inactive lanes 0. It has the 13 functions of the ActivationFn operand (ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES): identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu and window. Unlike ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, rsqrt of an input at or below 0 is 0, and exp2 takes any input.

It is in its own emulator-only slot, AAQ_EXACT, which runs after ACC. It is for FP32 kernels that need a function the hardware list lacks: the emulator rejects it in an IPU in the NX8 mode, the harness rejects it for an NX8 case, and assemble --target hardware rejects it. A word may not hold both ACTIVATE.EXACT and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE.

docs.title: α and the window bounds (elu, window)
docs.text:
The ISA has no operand for elu's α or for the bounds of window. The emulator reads them from the state's activation field, an ActivationParams (elu_alpha, window_a, window_b). Unset, they take the defaults in ipu_emu/activations.py (DEFAULT_ELU_ALPHA, DEFAULT_WINDOW_A, DEFAULT_WINDOW_B).

window is the half-open indicator: window(x) = 1 for a <= x < b, else 0. The defaults are placeholders until calibration: a = 0.0, b = 0.1.

They are set on the state, like the run mode, not through a CR:

from ipu_emu.activations import ActivationParams
from ipu_emu.ipu_state import IpuState

state = IpuState(activation=ActivationParams(elu_alpha=1.0, window_a=0.0, window_b=0.1))
# or, after construction:
state.set_activation_alphas(elu_alpha=1.0, window_a=0.0, window_b=0.1)

A state keeps its values from run to run; change them with set_activation_alphas, or build a new IpuState.

docs.title: Assembly Language Syntax
docs.text: The IPU assembler is a Python-based tool that turns assembly source into binary VLIW instructions for the emulator. Instruction names, operands, and encoding are driven by instruction_spec.py in ipu_isa; the Instruction reference and Operand types are generated from that same toolchain.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Jinja2 preprocessing — templates and macros for generated assembly
  • Label resolution — forward and backward references
  • VLIW compounds — multiple pipeline slots per cycle (COND, LR×3, LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ; emulator-only: AAQ_EXACT, BREAK)
  • Syntax validation — Lark-based parser with detailed errors

docs.title: Basic Syntax
docs.text:
Assembly is line-oriented. One compound instruction may contain several slot instructions separated by ;, terminated by ;;.

# Comments start with # or //
label:                          # Labels end with a colon
    LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;           # LOAD: load into mult stage R0
    MULT.RC.VV LR1 R0 0 LR3 CR15.L CR14.L; # MULT: element-wise multiply (DS, QF halves)
    ACC.ADD;                      # ACC: accumulate
    INC LR0 1;                    # LR: bump address (increment via INC)
    BNE LR0 LR1 next;             # COND: branch
    ;;
next:
    HALT;;

By convention, instruction mnemonics are written in upper case in documentation and examples (e.g. MULT.RC.VV, LD.MULT). Register names are written in upper case (LR0, R0, CR0); operand placeholders such as dest are lower case. The assembler accepts any case for mnemonics and register tokens.

docs.title: Compound instructions
docs.text:
A full IPU instruction is one compound word: several slots execute in parallel in a single cycle.

Pattern:

load_inst; mult_inst; acc_inst; aaq_inst; aaq_exact_inst; lr_inst_a; lr_inst_b; lr_inst_c; cond_inst; break_inst;;

Rules:

  • Each slot appears a fixed number of times (see SLOT_COUNT in instruction_spec.py); unused slots are filled with that slot’s NOP by the assembler.
  • Slot order in the binary word (MSB → LSB) is defined by the toolchain: cond, three lr sub-slots, load, mult, acc, aaq, aaq_exact, break (see the layout diagram on the Instruction reference).
  • The slots of one word execute in a fixed order, and each register read sees either the value at cycle start or the value forwarded from an earlier slot of the same word: see Execution order and timing.
  • The emulator-only slots (AAQ_EXACT, BREAK) are not implemented in real IPU hardware: see the instruction format.

Example (parallel slots):

loop:
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0; MULT.RC.VV LR1 R0 0 LR3 CR15.L CR14.L; ACC.ADD; INC LR0 1; BNE LR0 LR1 loop;;

docs.title: Register names
docs.text:
The mult-stage and scalar register tokens below are derived from REGISTER_DEFINITIONS in ipu_isa.registers (same source as the assembler).

Kind Assembler tokens Notes Mult stage R0, R1 One XMEM row each (128 NX8 elements and the row's metadata word, or 128 FP32 elements in the FP32 mode); 2-bit mult-stage field (2 reserved). See MultStageReg. Cyclic / mask (architectural) Cyclic (RC) and mask (RM) register files are documented per instruction in the reference; operands pass byte offsets via LR values. Loop / scalar LR0–LR15 General-purpose; read/write. See LrIdx. Constant CR0–CR15 Read-only in assembly; the host writes CR2–CR15 before a kernel runs. CR0 and CR1 are the read-only constants 0 and 1 (see Configuration registers). Each CR is also two 16-bit halves, CR13.L and CR13.H: the DS (data structure) and QF (quantization format) operands always name a half (see HalfCrIdx), and an LR or COND source operand may read a full CR or a sign-extended half (see LcrHalfIdx). CR15.L conventionally holds the default DS, but any half is a valid operand. See CrIdx and Configuration registers.

The mem_bypass vector may still exist in the emulator regfile for debugging, but it is not a valid mult-stage assembly operand.

LR slot: SET copies from a CR register (see CrIdx); ADD/SUB's src_b is register-only (see LcrIdx) — use INC/DEC for an immediate operand instead (see LrIncDecImmediate); INC.MODP2 uses a dedicated k immediate (see LrModPow2KImmediate).

docs.title: Labels and branches
docs.text:
start:
    SET LR0 CR0;;
loop:
    INC LR0 1;;
    BNE LR0 LR1 loop;;
    HALT;;

Relative labels such as B +5 / B -2 are supported where the grammar accepts a label token (see cond-slot instructions in the reference).

docs.title: Local labels
docs.text:
A label made of decimal digits only, such as 1:, is a local label (the GNU assembler's numeric labels). It may be defined any number of times. 1f refers to the next 1: after the current instruction word, and 1b to the nearest 1: at or before it, so a word may branch to its own label with 1b. A bare 1 as a branch target is an error. Local labels let a macro or a loop body use one short label in every expansion:

{% macro count_to(limit_cr) %}
    SET LR0 CR0;;
1:
    INC LR0 1;;
    BNE LR0 {{ limit_cr }} 1b;;
{% endmacro %}
{{ count_to("CR2") }}
{{ count_to("CR3") }}
    HALT;;

docs.title: Execution order and timing
docs.text:
This section is generated from ipu_isa.timing and the register accesses each instruction declares in instruction_spec.py.

The slots of one instruction word execute in this order: BREAK → LR → LOAD → MULT → ACC → AAQ → AAQ_EXACT → COND. BREAK is evaluated before any slot writes (it may halt the word); the LR sub-slots all read before any of them writes.

A register read sees one of two values: the value at cycle start (when the word began), or the forwarded value (after the writes of earlier slots of the same word). The timing contract is four rules:

  1. The Control stage (LR, COND) reads LRs at cycle start; every other stage reads LRs after the LR writes of the same word.
  2. MULT reads R0, R1, R_CYCLIC, their row metadata and R_MASK at cycle start.
  3. MULT_RES is forwarded to ACC (including AGG and RESHAPE); R_ACC is forwarded to AAQ and AAQ_EXACT.
  4. LR sub-slots read cycle-start values.

Any other read is forwarded when every slot that writes the register runs earlier in the word, and at cycle start otherwise. CRs are never written during a run, so CR reads are at cycle start.

The timing model explains the rules, with an example of each.

docs.title: Known deviations
docs.text: None: every read in the emulator follows the contract.

docs.title: Masking
docs.text: Multiply instructions (MULT.RC.VV, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.VE, MULT.EE) support element masking: after the multiply, elements in MULT_RES whose corresponding mask bit is 1 are active and pass through to accumulation; elements whose bit is 0 are deactivated and hold the pad value of the DS half's mask_type (0 for mask_type 0, +inf for 1, −inf for 2; 3, NaN, is an emulator error because NX8 has no NaN). A mask of all-ones leaves every element active (the reset default); a mask of all-zeros deactivates every element.

docs.title: R_MASK register
docs.text:
R_MASK is a 128-byte register packed as 8 independent 128-bit slots (slots 0–7). Load it from XMEM with:

LD.MASK offset base;;

offset is an LR register holding the XMEM byte offset; base is a CR register holding the base address. The full 1024-bit register is always overwritten in one cycle. A multiply reads R_MASK at cycle start, so an LD.MASK in the same word as a masking multiply is not seen by it: that multiply uses the previous R_MASK, and the next word sees the new one.

docs.title: Selecting a slot: mask_offset
docs.text: Each masking multiply instruction carries a 3-bit mask_offset immediate (0–7) that selects which 128-bit slot of R_MASK is used for that cycle. Eight slots can co-exist in a single loaded R_MASK value, so one load can serve eight different mask patterns per kernel.

docs.title: Deriving the active mask: mask_shift
docs.text:
Rather than using the slot mask directly, mask_shift selects from 7 derived masks generated by sequentially shifting the selected slot one bit at a time and ANDing with a partition vector after each step. Let M be the 128-bit value in the selected slot. Positive and negative shifts use different partition vectors:

mask_shift Derived mask 0 M (slot mask, unmodified) +1 (M << 1) & partition_vector +2 (derived[+1] << 1) & partition_vector +3 (derived[+2] << 1) & partition_vector −1 (M >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector −2 (derived[−1] >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector −3 (derived[−2] >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector

mask_shift names an LR register. The ctrl stage reads that register each cycle and forwards the value through the pipeline to the mult stage — the mult stage itself does not access LR registers directly. LR registers are 32-bit; negative values use 32-bit two's complement. Values outside [−3, +3] clamp to ±3.

docs.title: Partition vectors
docs.text:
Each masking multiply instruction takes a mandatory DS operand, ds, naming the CR half that holds the 16-bit DS (data structure) — there is no implicit default. Both vectors are derived from that half's num_partitions field (see Configuration registers and HalfCrIdx). The valid values of P are {1, 2, 4, 8}. With num_partitions = 1 both vectors are all-ones (no boundaries). With num_partitions = P the 128 elements are split into P equal groups of 128 / P elements:

Vector 0-bit positions Used by partition_vector first element of each group positive shifts (+1, +2, +3) inverse_partition_vector last element of each group negative shifts (−1, −2, −3)

For num_partitions = 2 (groups of 64):

  • partition_vector = 0 1⁶³0 1⁶³ — 0 at element 0 and element 64
  • inverse_partition_vector = 1⁶³0 1⁶³0 — 0 at element 63 and element 127

For num_partitions = 4 (groups of 32):

  • partition_vector = 0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹ — 0 at elements 0, 32, 64, 96
  • inverse_partition_vector = 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 1³¹0 — 0 at elements 31, 63, 95, 127

The AND at each step prevents mask bits from crossing the group boundary in either shift direction.

CR15.L is the conventional DS half and is set by the host harness, but it must still be named explicitly as the instruction's ds operand — there is no implicit fallback to CR15.L. The second half operand, qf, names the QF (quantization format) half the NX8 elements are decoded with; the FP32 mode ignores it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# LR1 = XMEM byte offset of mask data; CR2 = XMEM base address
LD.MASK LR1 CR2;;

# Load a vector into R0, load cyclic data into R_CYCLIC
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;
LD.MULT.CYCLIC LR2 CR0 LR5;;

# Multiply R0 element-wise vs R_CYCLIC using slot 3, shift index in LR4, accumulate
MULT.RC.VV LR2 R0 3 LR4 CR15.L CR14.L; ACC.ADD;;

3 is the mask_offset (slot 3 of R_MASK); LR4 holds the mask_shift index; CR15.L is the DS half supplying num_partitions and CR14.L the QF half (any half CR0.L–CR15.H may be named).

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Both examples load all-ones (0xFF…FF, 128 bits) into the selected R_MASK slot. At mask_shift = 0 every mask bit is 1, so every element is active. Each shift step clears one boundary bit to 0, deactivating one element at a time.

The tables show active elements — those whose derived mask bit is 1 and therefore contribute to accumulation.

docs.title: Example 1 — no partitioning (num_partitions = 1)
docs.text:
With num_partitions = 1 the partition vector is all-ones, so shifts slide freely across all 128 elements.

mask_shift Active elements (mask bit = 1) −3 0–124 −2 0–125 −1 0–126 0 0–127 (all active) +1 1–127 +2 2–127 +3 3–127

Positive shifts deactivate elements from the low end (element 0 first); negative shifts deactivate elements from the high end (element 127 first). Each step removes exactly one active element.

docs.title: Example 2 — two partitions of 64 elements each (num_partitions = 2)
docs.text:
With num_partitions = 2 the 128 elements are split into group 0 (elements 0–63) and group 1 (elements 64–127). Each group evolves independently and symmetrically:

  • partition_vector has 0 at element 0 and element 64 (used for positive shifts).
  • inverse_partition_vector has 0 at element 63 and element 127 (used for negative shifts).
mask_shift Group 0 active (elements 0–63) Group 1 active (elements 64–127) −3 0–60 64–124 −2 0–61 64–125 −1 0–62 64–126 0 0–63 (all) 64–127 (all) +1 1–63 65–127 +2 2–63 66–127 +3 3–63 67–127

Positive shifts deactivate elements from the start of each group (element 0 and element 64). Negative shifts deactivate elements from the end of each group (element 63 and element 127). Each step removes exactly one element per group — a perfectly symmetric sliding window.

docs.title: Jinja2 preprocessing
docs.text:
The assembler runs Jinja2 on the source when {{, {%, and {# appear.

{% set off_reg = 6 %}
SET LR0 CR{{ off_reg }};;
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;

The harness must initialize CR6 (here: the memory offset) before this program runs.

docs.title: ABI names
docs.text:
A kernel can name its registers by role instead of by number. The assembler takes a name → register mapping (from the kernel's kernel.toml [abi] table, or ipu-as assemble --abi kernel.toml) and exposes it as two read-only namespaces: {{ cr.<name> }} renders a CR register and {{ lr.<name> }} an LR register. An unknown name is a template error at its line, and a mapping whose value is not a register of its namespace is rejected before rendering. cr and lr cannot be used as parameter or define names.

SET {{ lr.data_ptr }} {{ cr.data_base }};;
LD.MULT R0 {{ lr.data_ptr }} CR0;;

With [abi] data_base = "CR2" and data_ptr = "LR0", this renders SET LR0 CR2;;.

docs.title: Running the assembler
docs.text:
Command line (Bazel):

bazel run //src/ipu-as:ipu-as -- assemble --input prog.asm --output prog.bin

In Bazel build rules: a kernel's :assemble_<name> target writes its program (see Write a kernel); assemble_asm in src/ipu-as/defs.bzl assembles any other source.

docs.title: Configuration registers
docs.text: This page is generated from ipu_isa.constants and ipu_isa.cr_halves. The host writes the CRs before a kernel runs; a kernel only reads them.

docs.title: The CRs
docs.text:
Register Value Notes CR0 0 Read-only constant. As a MULT constant it reads 0.0. CR1 1 Read-only constant. As a MULT constant it reads 1.0 in both modes (see CR scalars). CR2–CR15 set by the host Base addresses, strides, loop bounds, MULT constants, DS and QF halves. By convention CR15.L holds the default DS, but any CR half is a valid operand.

Each LR and CR holds a 32-bit scalar. A negative constant is stored as its 32-bit two's complement (value & LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK). A CR also holds two 16-bit halves, CRn.L (bits 15:0) and CRn.H (bits 31:16); an LR or COND operand that names a half reads it sign-extended. The run mode (NX8 or FP32) is not a CR: see Element formats.

docs.title: DS half
docs.text:
A DS half describes the active elements of a 128-element vector. The instructions with a ds operand read it: ACTIVATE.EXACT, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, AGG.MAX, AGG.MAX.FIRST, AGG.SUM, AGG.SUM.FIRST, MULT.EE, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.RC.VV, MULT.VE.

Field Bits Values valid_elements [7:0] active elements per partition (0–128) num_partitions [9:8] 0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 4, 3: 8 partitions (groups of elements) mask_type [11:10] the fill of a masked-out element (below) valid_partitions [15:12] how many partitions are active (1–num_partitions)

The emulator's initial CR15.L is 0x1080: every element active, one partition. Any other CR starts at 0, which is no valid DS (valid_partitions 0): an instruction that reads it is refused.

docs.title: mask_type
docs.text: Type Code Fill value ZERO 0 0 POS_INF 1 +inf NEG_INF 2 -inf NAN 3 refused (CrContentError)

docs.title: QF half
docs.text:
A QF half names the NX8 type a row is read or quantized in. The instructions with a qf operand read it in NX8 mode: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, MULT.EE, MULT.RC.VE, MULT.RC.VS, MULT.RC.VV, MULT.VE.

Field Bits Values num_bits [3:0] element width (1–8) exp_format [7:4] exponent bits fe (1–7) sign [11:8] 1: signed dynamic [15:12] 1: dynamic exponent (signed 8-bit only)

docs.title: MULT constant
docs.text:
A MULT constant operand reads a whole CR as one NX8 element with its own scale and type (FP32 mode: its IEEE binary32 bits).

Field Bits Values value [7:0] the NX8 element code scale [15:8] its scale (2scale − 127) exp_format [19:16] its exponent bits fe sign [23:20] 1: signed 
AGG.SUM LR0 CR15.L;;
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR15.L CR14.L CR3 LR0;;
MULT.RC.VV LR2 R0 0 LR4 CR15.L CR14.L;;

docs.title: From the emulator
docs.text:
from ipu_isa.constants import LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK
from ipu_isa.cr_halves import ds, qf
from ipu_isa.nx8 import Nx8Format

state.regfile.set_cr(2, 0x40000)                           # a base address
state.regfile.set_cr(9, (-128) & LR_CR_SCALAR_VALUE_MASK)  # a negative constant
state.set_cr_half(3, False, ds(valid_elements=64))         # CR3.L: a DS
state.set_cr_half(14, False, qf(Nx8Format(sign=1, exp_format=4, num_bits=8)))  # CR14.L: E4

docs.title: IPU Assembly Instruction Reference
docs.text: Per-opcode documentation is generated from InstructionDoc entries in instruction_spec.py. Operand types link to the shared operand type reference.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
A VLIW instruction word encodes one sub-instruction per slot. Slots are grouped into pipeline stages that execute sequentially within a cycle: CTRL (COND + LR run concurrently; LOAD address is resolved here and the data feeds MULT) → MULT → ACC → AAQ, which activates, quantizes and stores its own row (ADR 0007). AAQ_EXACT, BREAK are emulator-only: not in the hardware word. Any omitted slot is filled with NOP by the assembler automatically.

Slot Count Tag Description COND 1 HARDWARE Conditional and unconditional branches; control flow based on register comparisons. LR 3 HARDWARE Loop register instructions for controlling addresses, counters, and scalars. Three independent sub-slots per cycle. LOAD 1 HARDWARE First-stage memory loads that feed the multiply unit (mult-stage, cyclic, and mask registers). MULT 1 HARDWARE Multiply-stage instructions: element-wise and vector multiply operations. ACC 1 HARDWARE Accumulation instructions for combining multiply results into R_ACC. AAQ 1 HARDWARE Activation and quantization: activate R_ACC, quantize to one NX8 row and store it with its metadata; load the LUT segments the generic activation reads. AAQ_EXACT 1 EMULATOR Emulator-only exact activation: activate R_ACC with the exact Python function and store one FP32 row (FP32 mode only). Not in the hardware word. BREAK 1 EMULATOR Debug break: halts execution or enters debug mode.

docs.title: NOP — No Operation
docs.text:
Syntax: NOP

Tag: HARDWARE in the hardware slots, EMULATOR in the emulator-only slots.

Faults: none (fault list).

No operation. Every slot accepts NOP. The assembler fills any omitted slot with NOP automatically. When written explicitly in a compound instruction, NOP is assigned to the next unfilled slot in compound-layout order (COND → LR → LOAD → MULT → ACC → AAQ → AAQ_EXACT → BREAK).

docs.title: Element formats
docs.text: The element format is selected at run time and sets the element width. Element formats lists the formats and how each encodes values.

docs.title: Conditional Branch Instructions

docs.title: BEQ — Branch if Equal
docs.text:
Syntax: BEQ reg1 reg2 label

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-2 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrHalfIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) reg2 LcrHalfIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if two registers are equal.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 == reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BEQ LR0 LR1 end;;
end:
HALT;;

Register reads: reg1 (LR): cycle start; reg1 (CR): cycle start; reg2 (LR): cycle start; reg2 (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: HALT — Halt
docs.text:
Syntax: HALT

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: End the kernel after every slot of this word has retired.

Unconditional. The other slots of the same word retire first; then the kernel is done. To stop for debugging, use BREAK (emulator-only) instead. Not the host's HALT command, which stops a running kernel.

Pseudo code: no further fetch; kernel done when this word retires

Example of usage: 

HALT;;

docs.text:
Syntax: INC.MODP2 dest step k

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrIdx dest: Destination loop register (LR0–LR15); read and written step LcrHalfIdx step: Signed 32-bit increment from LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H k LrModPow2KImmediate k: Immediate in [1, 9]; encoded in 4 bits as (k − 1); mask = (1 << k) - 1

docs.title: ADDB — Add Byte (Broadcast, Register)
docs.text:
Syntax: ADDB dest src_b

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrdIdx dest: Destination register pair (LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, ..., LRD14 — named after the lower register); LRDn = LR(n+1):LR(n), 8 byte elements; also the implicit source src_b LcrHalfIdx src_b: LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a half CR0.L–CR15.H; low byte is read and reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement byte

General description: Broadcast-add a signed byte from an LR/CR register's low byte to each of the 8 byte elements of an LRDn register pair, saturating each element to [0, 255].

There is no separate subtract opcode: since src_b's byte is reinterpreted as signed, a value ≥ 128 (i.e. negative in two's complement) subtracts from every element instead of adding. E.g. an LR/CR whose low byte is 200 (== -56) decreases each element by 56. Because elements saturate at both ends of [0, 255], subtracting past 0 clamps at 0 rather than wrapping — it does not behave like a plain two's-complement subtract.

Pseudo code: byte_val = src_b & 0xFF # interpreted as signed int8 (two's complement) for i in 0..7: dest_byte[i] = clamp(dest_byte[i] + byte_val, 0, 255)

Example of usage: 

ADDB LRD0 LR3;;
ADDB LRD2 CR5;;

Register reads: src_b (LR): cycle start; src_b (CR): cycle start; dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: ADDBI — Add Byte Immediate (Broadcast)
docs.text:
Syntax: ADDBI dest imm

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-3 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest LrdIdx dest: Destination register pair (LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, ..., LRD14 — named after the lower register); LRDn = LR(n+1):LR(n), 8 byte elements; also the implicit source imm AddbiImmediate imm: Unsigned byte 0–255 (or an equivalent signed −128–127 literal); reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement byte for the add

General description: Broadcast-add a signed immediate byte to each of the 8 byte elements of an LRDn register pair, saturating each element to [0, 255].

There is no separate subtract opcode: write imm as a negative literal (e.g. -56) or its equivalent unsigned encoding (200) to subtract from every element instead of adding — both spellings encode the same bit pattern. Because elements saturate at both ends of [0, 255], subtracting past 0 clamps at 0 rather than wrapping — it does not behave like a plain two's-complement subtract.

Pseudo code: byte_val = imm # interpreted as signed int8 (two's complement) for i in 0..7: dest_byte[i] = clamp(dest_byte[i] + byte_val, 0, 255)

Example of usage: 

ADDBI LRD0 200;;
ADDBI LRD2 7;;

Register reads: dest (LR): cycle start.

docs.title: LOAD Instructions
docs.text: First-stage memory loads that feed the multiply unit (mult-stage registers, cyclic register, and mask register).

docs.title: LD.MULT — Load Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MULT dest offset base

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest MultStageReg dest: R0 | R1 — mult-stage register to load (2-bit field; only these encodings are valid). offset LrIdx offset: LR0…LR15 — offset register, in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: CR0…CR15 — base address register, in XMEM rows.

General description: Load data from memory into a multiplication stage register.

Pseudo code: dest = Memory[row(offset + base)] # one row = 128 elements: 128 B in NX8 mode, 512 B in FP32 mode dest.metadata = Metadata[row(offset + base)] # NX8: scale, dynamic_exponent; FP32: 0

Example of usage: 

SET LR0 CR1;;
LD.MULT R0 LR0 CR0;;

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: LD.MULT.CYCLIC — Load Cyclic Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MULT.CYCLIC offset base index

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-4, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details offset LrIdx offset: Offset register (LR0–LR15), in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: Base address register (CR0–CR15), in XMEM rows. index LrIdx index: Index inside cyclic register (LR0–LR15); must hold 0, 128, 256, or 384 — the four R_CYCLIC slot boundaries, counted in elements. Any other value raises an error. All four are valid in both modes: R_CYCLIC is a 512-element ring in NX8 and FP32 mode alike, and a load always replaces one whole 128-element slot and its metadata.

General description: Load with cyclic addressing into R_CYCLIC.

Pseudo code: R_CYCLIC[index .. index+127] = Memory[row(offset + base)] # index ∈ {0, 128, 256, 384} R_CYCLIC.metadata[index / 128] = Metadata[row(offset + base)] # NX8; 0 in FP32 mode

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start; index (LR): after LR writes.

docs.title: LD.MASK — Load Mask Register
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.MASK offset base

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details offset LrIdx offset: Offset register (LR0–LR15), in XMEM rows. base CrIdx base: Base address register (CR0–CR15), in XMEM rows.

General description: Load mask data from memory.

Pseudo code: R_MASK = Memory[row(offset + base) .. +128B] # reads only the row's first 128 B, in both modes -- the mask is 1 bit/element and does not scale with element width

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; base (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT Instructions
docs.text: Multiplication instructions for element-wise and element-vector operations. The multiplication result (mult_result) is forwarded to the ACC stage in the CPU and not stored in any register in the way.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VV — RC Vector × Ra Vector Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VV rc_idx ra mask_offset mask_shift ds qf

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). ra MultStageReg ra: R0 | R1 — multiplicand mult-stage register (same cycle as LD.MULT into R0/R1 is allowed). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H — DS half-CR (ipu_isa.cr_halves): num_partitions builds the partition vectors for mask_shift, mask_type is the value written into deactivated elements (0, +inf or −inf; NaN is an emulator error). The whole DS is validated. qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L…CR15.H — QF half-CR naming the NX8 format of the vector elements: in NX8 mode each element expands to FP32 with its row's metadata (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1); ignored in FP32 mode.

General description: Multiply R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] by Ra (R0 or R1) element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift and the mask pad come from the DS half ds; in NX8 mode the elements are decoded with the QF half qf and their rows' metadata.

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the DS mask_type value (0, +inf or −inf) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: MULT_RES[i] = expand(R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512]) * expand(ra[i]); then apply mask and shift using DS[ds].num_partitions and DS[ds].mask_type.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VV LR0 R0 0 LR2 CR15.L CR14.L;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; ra (R): cycle start; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_CYCLIC_META: cycle start; R_META: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VE — RC Vector × Scalar Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VE rc_idx src mask_offset mask_shift ds qf

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). src LcrIdx src: LR0…LR15 | CR0…CR15 — if an LR, its stored value selects the scalar from R0/R1 (0..127 → R0[idx], 128..255 → R1[idx - 128], decoded with qf and that row's metadata); if a CR, the CR is a MULT constant (NX8: the constant layout, with its own scale and type; FP32: float32 bits; CR0 = 0.0, CR1 = 1.0; see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H — DS half-CR (ipu_isa.cr_halves): num_partitions builds the partition vectors for mask_shift, mask_type is the value written into deactivated elements (0, +inf or −inf; NaN is an emulator error). The whole DS is validated. qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L…CR15.H — QF half-CR naming the NX8 format of the vector elements: in NX8 mode each element expands to FP32 with its row's metadata (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1); ignored in FP32 mode.

General description: Multiply R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] by a scalar, element-wise. The scalar is either a single element of R0/R1 (selected by an LR value) or a CR constant. The partition used by mask_shift and the mask pad come from the DS half ds; in NX8 mode the vector elements are decoded with the QF half qf.

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the DS mask_type value (0, +inf or −inf) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: MULT_RES[i] = expand(R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512]) * src_value; then apply mask and shift using DS[ds].num_partitions and DS[ds].mask_type.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VE LR0 LR3 0 LR2 CR15.L CR14.L;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; src (LR): after LR writes; src (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_META: cycle start; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_CYCLIC_META: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.RC.VS — RC Vector Self-Multiply (Square)
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.RC.VS rc_idx mask_offset mask_shift ds qf

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx rc_idx: LR0…LR15 — base ELEMENT index into R_CYCLIC (cyclic, mod 512 elements; same unit as LD.MULT.CYCLIC's index). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H — DS half-CR (ipu_isa.cr_halves): num_partitions builds the partition vectors for mask_shift, mask_type is the value written into deactivated elements (0, +inf or −inf; NaN is an emulator error). The whole DS is validated. qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L…CR15.H — QF half-CR naming the NX8 format of the vector elements: in NX8 mode each element expands to FP32 with its row's metadata (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1); ignored in FP32 mode.

General description: Square R_CYCLIC[rc_idx:rc_idx+128] element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift and the mask pad come from the DS half ds; in NX8 mode the elements are decoded with the QF half qf.

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the DS mask_type value (0, +inf or −inf) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: rb = expand(R_CYCLIC[(rc_idx + i) % 512]); MULT_RES[i] = rb * rb; then apply mask and shift using DS[ds].num_partitions and DS[ds].mask_type.

Example of usage: 

MULT.RC.VS LR0 0 LR2 CR15.L CR14.L;;

Register reads: rc_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; R_CYCLIC: cycle start; R_CYCLIC_META: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.VE — Ra Vector × CR Scalar Multiply
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.VE ra_idx cr_idx mask_offset mask_shift ds qf

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details ra_idx LrIdx ra_idx: LR0…LR15 — base element offset into combined Ra (R0 ++ R1, 256 elements, cyclic mod 256). cr_idx CrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — the scalar: a MULT constant (NX8: value[7:0], scale[15:8], fe[19:16], sign[23:20], decoded with its own scale; FP32: float32 bits). CR0 reads as 0.0 and CR1 as 1.0 in both modes (see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H — DS half-CR (ipu_isa.cr_halves): num_partitions builds the partition vectors for mask_shift, mask_type is the value written into deactivated elements (0, +inf or −inf; NaN is an emulator error). The whole DS is validated. qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L…CR15.H — QF half-CR naming the NX8 format of the vector elements: in NX8 mode each element expands to FP32 with its row's metadata (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1); ignored in FP32 mode.

General description: Multiply Ra[ra_idx:ra_idx+128] (combined R0/R1) by a CR constant, element-wise. The partition used by mask_shift and the mask pad come from the DS half ds; in NX8 mode the Ra elements are decoded with the QF half qf.

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the DS mask_type value (0, +inf or −inf) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: For each element i: ra = expand(Ra[(ra_idx + i) % 256]); MULT_RES[i] = ra * constant(CR[cr_idx]); then apply mask and shift using DS[ds].num_partitions and DS[ds].mask_type.

Example of usage: 

MULT.VE LR0 CR3 0 LR2 CR15.L CR14.L;;

Register reads: ra_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_META: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: MULT.EE — Ra Element × CR Scalar Multiply (broadcast)
docs.text:
Syntax: MULT.EE ra_idx cr_idx mask_offset mask_shift ds qf

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details ra_idx LrIdx ra_idx: LR0…LR15 — index of the single Ra element to read (combined R0 ++ R1, 256 elements, mod 256). cr_idx CrIdx cr_idx: CR0…CR15 — the scalar: a MULT constant (NX8: value[7:0], scale[15:8], fe[19:16], sign[23:20], decoded with its own scale; FP32: float32 bits). CR0 reads as 0.0 and CR1 as 1.0 in both modes (see CrIdx and CR scalars). mask_offset MultMaskOffsetImmediate mask_offset: immediate mask slot 0…7 — selects one of eight 128-bit masks in R_MASK. mask_shift LrIdx mask_shift: LR0…LR15 — index ∈ [−3, +3] (values >3 clamp to 3, values <−3 clamp to −3) selecting one of seven masks via sequential shift-and-AND: positive indices use partition_vector (0 at group start), negative indices use inverse_partition_vector (0 at group end). ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H — DS half-CR (ipu_isa.cr_halves): num_partitions builds the partition vectors for mask_shift, mask_type is the value written into deactivated elements (0, +inf or −inf; NaN is an emulator error). The whole DS is validated. qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L…CR15.H — QF half-CR naming the NX8 format of the vector elements: in NX8 mode each element expands to FP32 with its row's metadata (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1); ignored in FP32 mode.

General description: Multiply a single Ra element by a CR constant; broadcast the product to all 128 elements. The partition used by mask_shift and the mask pad come from the DS half ds; in NX8 mode the Ra element is decoded with the QF half qf.

Element masking via mask_offset and mask_shift fills elements whose derived mask bit is 0 (deactivated) in MULT_RES with the DS mask_type value (0, +inf or −inf) before accumulation; elements with bit 1 pass through. See Masking for the full algorithm.

Pseudo code: ra = expand(Ra[ra_idx % 256]); result = ra * constant(CR[cr_idx]); for each element i: MULT_RES[i] = result; then apply mask and shift using DS[ds].num_partitions and DS[ds].mask_type.

Example of usage: 

MULT.EE LR0 CR3 0 LR2 CR15.L CR14.L;;

Register reads: ra_idx (LR): after LR writes; mask_shift (LR): after LR writes; cr_idx (CR): cycle start; R: cycle start; R_META: cycle start; R_MASK: cycle start; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start.

docs.title: ACC Instructions
docs.text: Accumulation instructions for combining values with optional masking and shifting.

docs.title: ACC.ADD — Accumulate Add
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.ADD

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Running add accumulation: add multiply result into each R_ACC element.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] += MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.ADD;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: ACC.ADD.FIRST — Accumulate Add (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.ADD.FIRST

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Clean-init add: overwrite each R_ACC element with the multiply result (ignores previous R_ACC).

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.ADD.FIRST;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: ACC.MAX — Accumulate Max
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.MAX

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Running max accumulation: each R_ACC element takes the max of its current value and the multiply result.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = max(R_ACC[i], MULT_RES[i]) # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.MAX;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: ACC.MAX.FIRST — Accumulate Max (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.MAX.FIRST

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Clean-init max: overwrite each R_ACC element unconditionally with the multiply result.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i] # for each element i (unconditional overwrite)

Example of usage: 

ACC.MAX.FIRST;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: ACC.SUB — Accumulate Subtract
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.SUB

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Running subtract accumulation: subtract the multiply result from each R_ACC element each cycle.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] -= MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.SUB;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: ACC.SUB.FIRST — Accumulate Subtract (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.SUB.FIRST

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Clean-init subtract: set each R_ACC element to the negated multiply result.

Pseudo code: R_ACC[i] = -MULT_RES[i] # for each element i

Example of usage: 

ACC.SUB.FIRST;;

Register reads: MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: ACC.STRIDE — Accumulator Stride
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.STRIDE elements_in_row horizontal_stride vertical_stride offset

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details elements_in_row ElementsInRow elements_in_row: Elements per row (16, 32, or 64; minimum is 16) horizontal_stride HorizontalStride horizontal_stride: Horizontal stride mode (off, on, on_inv) vertical_stride VerticalStride vertical_stride: Vertical stride mode (enabled, inverted) offset LrIdx offset: LR register; value % 4 gives start index in RACC (0, 32, 64, or 96)

General description: Reorder the multiplication result into R_ACC using horizontal/vertical stride decimation. Only updates the RACC indexes written; leaves the rest unchanged.

Pseudo code: Decimate MULT_RES as rows×cols; apply horizontal stride (take every 2nd column); then vertical stride (take every 2nd row). Write result into R_ACC[start:start+N] where start = (offset%4)*32, N = 32|64|128. When a data structure has fewer than 8 elements, hardware pads to 16 automatically (not programmable).

Example of usage: 

ACC.STRIDE 16 off off LR0;;

Register reads: offset (LR): after LR writes; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.SUM.FIRST — Aggregate Sum (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.SUM.FIRST dest_slot ds

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H, the DS half supplying valid_elements (the whole DS is validated)

General description: Sum active MULT_RES elements and write the result into R_ACC at the slot given by LR. The current value at the destination slot is NOT included in the sum (clean initialisation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) of the DS half ds is used: the first valid_elements elements (ARCH-stage-acc).

Pseudo code: Let n = DS[ds].valid_elements. dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]).

Example of usage: 

AGG.SUM.FIRST LR0 CR3.L;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.SUM — Aggregate Sum
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.SUM dest_slot ds

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H, the DS half supplying valid_elements (the whole DS is validated)

General description: Sum active MULT_RES elements and ADD the result to R_ACC at the slot given by LR (running cross-cycle accumulation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) of the DS half ds is used: the first valid_elements elements (ARCH-stage-acc).

Pseudo code: Let n = DS[ds].valid_elements. dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) + R_ACC[dest].

Example of usage: 

AGG.SUM LR0 CR3.L;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: AGG.MAX.FIRST — Aggregate Max (First)
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.MAX.FIRST dest_slot ds

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H, the DS half supplying valid_elements (the whole DS is validated)

General description: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements and write it into R_ACC at the slot given by LR. The current value at the destination slot is NOT used as a seed (clean initialisation). Only the active element count (valid_elements) of the DS half ds is used: the first valid_elements elements (ARCH-stage-acc).

Pseudo code: Let n = DS[ds].valid_elements. dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1]); when n = 0 the identity seed (-inf) is written.

Example of usage: 

AGG.MAX.FIRST LR0 CR3.L;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AGG.MAX — Aggregate Max
docs.text:
Syntax: AGG.MAX dest_slot ds

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx dest_slot: LR register whose value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L…CR15.H, the DS half supplying valid_elements (the whole DS is validated)

General description: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements seeded with the current destination slot value (running cross-cycle max). Only the active element count (valid_elements) of the DS half ds is used: the first valid_elements elements (ARCH-stage-acc).

Pseudo code: Let n = DS[ds].valid_elements. dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128. R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1], R_ACC[dest]).

Example of usage: 

AGG.MAX LR0 CR3.L;;

Register reads: dest_slot (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward; R_ACC: cycle start.

docs.title: ACC.RESHAPE — Reshape
docs.text:
Syntax: ACC.RESHAPE source dest reshape_mask

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-5 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details source LrdIdx source: LRDn register pair (LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14) read as source[0..7] — 8 byte elements, each a MULT_RES word index dest LrdIdx dest: LRDn register pair (LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14) read as dest[0..7] — 8 byte elements, each an R_ACC word index reshape_mask LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate reshape_mask: immediate 0-7 or an LR register; selects the first participating element index (elements reshape_mask..7 participate; reshape_mask = 0 uses all 8, reshape_mask = 7 uses only element 7). When an LR is given, its full value is used as the mask at runtime.

General description: Scatter MULT_RES elements into R_ACC: for each of the trailing (8 - reshape_mask) byte elements of the source/dest LRDn pairs (indices reshape_mask..7), copy MULT_RES[source[i]] to R_ACC[dest[i]].

reshape_mask skips the lowest-indexed elements 0..reshape_mask-1; the rest participate. Example: reshape_mask = 2 skips elements 0, 1; elements 2-7 participate. Example: reshape_mask = 5 skips elements 0-4; elements 5-7 participate.

Pseudo code: mult_res = MULT_RES (this cycle's MULT result) mask = reshape_mask if immediate else LR[reshape_mask] if mask > 8: raise error for i in mask..7: if source[i] >= 128 or dest[i] >= 128: raise error R_ACC[dest[i]] = mult_res[source[i]]

Example of usage: 

ACC.RESHAPE LRD0 LRD2 0;;

Register reads: source (LR): after LR writes; dest (LR): after LR writes; reshape_mask (LR): after LR writes; MULT_RES: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: AAQ Instructions
docs.text: Activation and quantization: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activates the forwarded R_ACC, quantizes it to one NX8 row and stores the row and its metadata to XMEM; LD.LUT loads one LUT segment from XMEM (ADR 0007).

docs.title: LD.LUT — Load LUT Segment
docs.text:
Syntax: LD.LUT lut_addr table_id table_offset

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details lut_addr LutAddrImmediate lut_addr: immediate segment index 0–4 (3-bit field; 5–7 are reserved) table_id CrIdx table_id: CR0–CR15 holding the base row table_offset LrIdx table_offset: LR0–LR15 holding the row offset (the row is CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset])

General description: Load the first 128 bytes (1024 bits) of one XMEM row into LUT segment lut_addr of the AaQ stage. Five loads (segments 0-4) fill the 4352 table bits and the 46-bit LUT metadata the generic activation reads. No row metadata, no scaling; the same in both modes.

The architecture specs read the LUT from R_ACC; the emulator reads XMEM (ADR 0007, OQ-39). A word with LD.LUT and any LD.* of the LOAD slot is an assembler error: they share the XMEM read port.

Pseudo code: row = CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset] LUT.segment[lut_addr] = Memory[row][0 .. 127] # 1024 bits, both modes

Example of usage: 

LD.LUT 0 CR4 LR0;;

Register reads: table_id (CR): cycle start; table_offset (LR): after LR writes.

docs.title: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE — Activate, Quantize and Store
docs.text:
Syntax: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activation_fn ds qf table_id table_offset

Tag: HARDWARE (implemented by the IPU)

Faults: F-1, F-6, F-7 (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details activation_fn AaqActivationFn activation_fn: identity, relu, relu6, reciprocal, rsqrt, exp2 or generic (3-bit ARCH encoding) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L–CR15.H, the DS half naming the active elements qf HalfCrIdx qf: CR0.L–CR15.H, the QF half naming the NX8 output format table_id CrIdx table_id: CR0–CR15 holding the base row table_offset LrIdx table_offset: LR0–LR15 holding the row offset

General description: Activate the forwarded R_ACC (this cycle's ACC result), quantize the active elements to one NX8 row in the format the QF half qf names, and store the 128-byte row and its metadata (scale, dynamic exponent) at XMEM row CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset]. Inactive elements are written 0. In FP32 mode the activated row is stored as 512 bytes of FP32, inactive lanes 0, and qf is ignored. R_ACC is not modified.

Special cases follow the architecture spec: reciprocal and rsqrt of a subnormal input add epsilon = 2^-127 with the input's sign; rsqrt of a negative input is NaN, which cannot be quantized (emulator error); exp2 of a positive input is an emulator error. ±inf saturates to the largest magnitude; a saturation sets QUANT_SATURATION. generic computes the function the test declares as loaded with LD.LUT.

Pseudo code: y[i] = activation(R_ACC[i]) for the active elements i of DS[ds] NX8: (bytes, scale, dynamic_exponent) = quantize(y, QF[qf]) # ARCH-stage-aaq-str §4.3.2 Memory[row] = bytes; Metadata[row] = (scale, dynamic_exponent) FP32: Memory[row] = y as 128 FP32 (inactive lanes 0) where row = CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset]

Example of usage: 

ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu CR15.L CR14.L CR2 LR0;;

Register reads: table_id (CR): cycle start; table_offset (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; qf (CR): cycle start; R_ACC: same-cycle forward; AAQ_LUT: cycle start.

docs.title: AAQ_EXACT Instructions
docs.text:
Emulator-only slot — not implemented in real IPU hardware: not in the hardware word or the SV package.

Emulator-only slot: ACTIVATE.EXACT applies the exact activation to the forwarded R_ACC and stores one FP32 row (512 B). Valid in FP32 mode only (ADR 0007).

docs.title: ACTIVATE.EXACT — Activate Exactly and Store FP32
docs.text:
Syntax: ACTIVATE.EXACT activation_fn ds table_id table_offset

Tag: EMULATOR (emulator only; not in the hardware word or the SV package)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details activation_fn ActivationFn activation_fn: one of identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu, window (see ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES) ds HalfCrIdx ds: CR0.L–CR15.H, the DS half naming the active elements table_id CrIdx table_id: CR0–CR15 holding the base row table_offset LrIdx table_offset: LR0–LR15 holding the row offset

General description: Emulator-only. Apply the exact Python activation to the active elements of the forwarded R_ACC and store the row as 128 FP32 values (512 bytes) at XMEM row CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset]; inactive lanes are written 0. Valid in FP32 mode only: a program that uses it is rejected when loaded into an NX8-mode IPU. R_ACC is not modified.

Pseudo code: row = CR[table_id] + LR[table_offset] Memory[row] = activation(R_ACC[i]) as FP32 for active i, 0 for inactive i rsqrt(x) = 0 for x <= 0; window(x) = 1 for a <= x < b, else 0. α for elu and the window bounds are emulator settings (docs/content/reference/isa/activate-quantize.md).

Example of usage: 

ACTIVATE.EXACT relu CR15.L CR2 LR0;;

Register reads: table_id (CR): cycle start; table_offset (LR): after LR writes; ds (CR): cycle start; R_ACC: same-cycle forward.

docs.title: Break Instructions
docs.text:
Emulator-only slot — not implemented in real IPU hardware: not in the hardware word or the SV package.

Debug break instructions for halting execution and entering debug mode.

docs.title: BREAK — Break
docs.text:
Syntax: BREAK

Tag: EMULATOR (emulator only; not in the hardware word or the SV package)

Faults: none (fault list).

General description: Unconditional break.

Pseudo code: Halt execution

docs.title: BREAK.IFEQ — Break if Equal
docs.text:
Syntax: BREAK.IFEQ reg value

Tag: EMULATOR (emulator only; not in the hardware word or the SV package)

Faults: none (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LrIdx reg: Register to test (LR0–LR15) value BreakImmediate value: Immediate value to compare against

General description: Break execution if register equals value.

Example of usage:

docs.title: Operand types
docs.text: This page is generated by ipu_gen.docs_pages from VALID_OPERAND_TYPES in instruction_spec.py and the descriptions below. For encodings per instruction, see the Instruction reference.

docs.title: AaqActivationFn
docs.text: AAQ-slot keyword on ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE: identity (0), relu (1), relu6 (2), reciprocal (3), rsqrt (4), exp2 (5), generic (6), as ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md encodes them (code 7 is reserved). generic evaluates the LUT loaded with LD.LUT; the emulator computes the function a test declares as loaded (ADR 0007).

docs.title: ActivationFn
docs.text: Keyword on the emulator-only ACTIVATE.EXACT: one of identity, relu, relu6, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, softplus, elu, exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, silu, window (see ACTIVATION_FN_NAMES in ipu_isa.activations). Emulator-only calibration (including α and the window bounds a, b) is described in the ACTIVATE.EXACT section of docs/content/reference/isa/activate-quantize.md.

docs.title: AddbiImmediate
docs.text: 8-bit byte immediate for ADDBI: written as an unsigned value 0–255 or an equivalent signed -128–127 literal (both spellings encode the same bit pattern). The encoded byte is reinterpreted as a signed two's-complement int8 when broadcast-added to ADDB/ADDBI's 8 destination byte elements.

docs.title: BreakImmediate
docs.text: 16-bit value for BREAK / breakpoint slot conditions.

docs.title: CrIdx
docs.text:
Constant-register index: CR0 … CR15. CRs are read-only in assembly; the harness initializes them (e.g. base pointers, strides, QF and DS halves). SET in the LR slot copies the full 32-bit CR value (or a sign-extended half) into an LR.

CR as an element scalar. When a CR is a multiply's scalar element operand (MULT.VE, MULT.EE, a CR src of MULT.RC.VE), NX8 mode decodes it with the MULT constant layout (value[7:0], scale[15:8], fe[19:16], sign[23:20]; ipu_isa.cr_halves) and FP32 mode reads it as IEEE float32 bits. CR0 reads as 0.0 and CR1 as 1.0 in both modes, so a multiply by CR1 is an identity; as an LR or integer operand CR1 is the integer 1.

docs.title: ElementsInRow
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: elements per row for ACC.STRIDE. Valid values: 16, 32, 64 (minimum is 16; encoded 0→16, 1→32, 2→64). See acc_stride_enums in ipu_isa.

docs.title: HalfCrIdx
docs.text: Half-CR selector: CR0.L, CR0.H, … CR15.H (code = 2 × index + H). .L is bits 15:0 of the CR, .H bits 31:16. Used for the ds (data structure) and qf (quantization format) operands of the MULT, AGG and AaQ instructions; their 16-bit layouts are in ipu_isa.cr_halves (ADR 0007). A bare CR13 is not accepted here: the operand always names a half. CR15.L holds the default DS at reset.

docs.title: HorizontalStride
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: horizontal stride mode for ACC.STRIDE. Valid values: off, on, on_inv (2-bit encoded enum; reserved3 is reserved). Expand padding is fixed hardware behaviour and is not programmable. See acc_stride_enums in ipu_isa.

docs.title: Label
docs.text: Branch target: a symbolic label or a relative offset accepted by the cond slot (e.g. loop, +3).

docs.title: LcrHalfIdx
docs.text: LR, CR or CR-half index in one 6-bit field: codes 0–15 are LR0–LR15, 16–31 CR0–CR15, 32–47 CR0.L–CR15.L and 48–63 CR0.H–CR15.H. A half is read as its 16 bits sign-extended to 32. The scalar source of the LR instructions (SET src, ADD/SUB/ADDB src_b, INC.MODP2 step) and the compared registers of the COND branches.

docs.title: LcrIdx
docs.text: LR or CR index in one field: lower indices map to LR0–LR15, higher indices to CR0–CR15 in the usual combined ordering used by the assembler. Used as src on MULT.RC.VE (an LR's stored value selects an element from R0/R1; a CR is the scalar directly, decoded as in CrIdx).

docs.title: LrIdx
docs.text: Loop register index: resolves to LR0 … LR15. Often used for addresses, strides, and control values. When marked read: live in the spec, the emulator reads the current LR value after earlier slots in the same cycle.

docs.title: LrIncDecImmediate
docs.text: Unsigned immediate for INC / DEC in the LR slot. The bit width W is not hardcoded — it is derived from the LR slot union layout so the total slot width stays constant. Valid range: 0 to 2^W − 1.

docs.title: LrModPow2KImmediate
docs.text: Four-bit immediate for INC.MODP2: encodes exponent k with semantic k ∈ [1, 9] as (k − 1) in the word.

docs.title: LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate
docs.text: Operand on ACC.RESHAPE (bit width auto-derived from union layout): selects the first participating element slot (elements reshape_mask…7 of the source/dest LRD pair participate). Accepts either an unsigned immediate 0–7 or an LR register (its value is used directly as the mask; a resolved value greater than 8 raises an error rather than being clamped). 0 uses all 8 slots; 7 uses only slot 7; 8 uses none.

docs.title: LrdIdx
docs.text: Register-pair index: LRD0, LRD2, LRD4, … LRD14 — named after the lower register in the pair — each aliasing two adjacent LR registers as one 8-byte-element value: LRDn = LR(n+1) (high elements) concatenated with LR(n) (low elements). Purely an assembler/emulator view; there is no separate physical storage. Used as dest on ADDB / ADDBI.

docs.title: LutAddrImmediate
docs.text: Three-bit immediate on LD.LUT: which of the five 1024-bit LUT segments the load fills (0–4; codes 5–7 are reserved).

docs.title: MultMaskOffsetImmediate
docs.text: Unsigned 3-bit immediate on multiply instructions: mask_offset selects slot 0–7, each a 128-bit region of R_MASK (eight mask slots total). mask_shift remains an LrIdx.

docs.title: MultStageReg
docs.text: Multiply-stage field in the VLIW encoding. Assembly accepts R0 and R1 only; the field is two bits wide (encoding 2 is reserved). Used as the destination of LD.MULT and as the ra operand of MULT.RC.VV.

docs.title: VerticalStride
docs.text: ACC-slot immediate: vertical stride bit pattern for ACC.STRIDE (see acc_stride_enums).

docs.title: Programmer's Guide: Pseudo-Instructions
docs.text: Pseudo-instructions are assembly mnemonics that the assembler expands into a real instruction at compile time. They never get an opcode and never appear in the binary, so they cost nothing at runtime — see Adding a pseudo-instruction for how they're declared. This page is generated from PSEUDO_INSTRUCTION_SPEC in instruction_spec.py.

docs.title: BGT.S — Branch if Greater Than (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BGT.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BLT.S (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrHalfIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) reg2 LcrHalfIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is greater than second.

Expands to BLT.S reg2 reg1 label at assemble time (operands swapped). Identical encoding and runtime cost to a hand-written BLT.S.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 > reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BGT.S LR0 LR1 bigger;;
bigger:
HALT;;

Expands to: BLT.S reg2 reg1 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BLE.S — Branch if Less or Equal (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BLE.S reg1 reg2 label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BGE.S (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg1 LcrHalfIdx reg1: First register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) reg2 LcrHalfIdx reg2: Second register to compare (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if first register is less than or equal to second.

Expands to BGE.S reg2 reg1 label at assemble time (operands swapped), exactly mirroring how BGT.S expands to BLT.S. Identical encoding and runtime cost to a hand-written BGE.S.

Pseudo code: if (reg1 <= reg2) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BLE.S LR0 LR1 smaller_or_equal;;
smaller_or_equal:
HALT;;

Expands to: BGE.S reg2 reg1 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BZ — Branch if Zero (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BZ reg label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BEQ (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LcrHalfIdx reg: Register to test (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if register is zero (CR0 is the constant 0).

Expands to BEQ reg CR0 label; CR0 is the read-only constant 0.

Pseudo code: if (reg == 0) PC = label

Example of usage: 

BZ LR0 done;;
done:
HALT;;

Expands to: BEQ reg CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.title: BNZ — Branch if Not Zero (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: BNZ reg label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BNE (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details reg LcrHalfIdx reg: Register to test (LR0–LR15, CR0–CR15, or a sign-extended half CR0.L–CR15.H) label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Branch if register is not zero (CR0 is the constant 0).

Expands to BNE reg CR0 label; CR0 is the read-only constant 0.

Pseudo code: if (reg != 0) PC = label

Example of usage: 

loop:
DEC LR0 1;;
BNZ LR0 loop;;

Expands to: BNE reg CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.title: B — Unconditional Branch (pseudo)
docs.text:
Syntax: B label

Tag: ASSEMBLER (expanded by the assembler; no opcode)

Faults: F-2, through BEQ (fault list).

Operands: (the Type column links to the operand type reference)

Name Type Details label Label label: Branch target label

General description: Always branch to label.

Expands to BEQ CR0 CR0 label. CR0 always equals itself, so the branch is always taken.

Pseudo code: PC = label

Example of usage: 

start:
INC LR0 1;;
B start;;

Expands to: BEQ CR0 CR0 label (cond slot)

docs.text:
