docs.title: IPU hardware requirements
docs.text:
The Inference Processing Unit (IPU) is a VLIW vector processor that runs neural-network kernels. Each VLIW word operates on 128-element vectors through a load, multiply, accumulate, and activate-quantize-and-store chain.

The requirements define what the IPU does and what it expects from the blocks around it. The IPU block specification and the sub-block specifications derive from the requirements.

docs.title: Specification levels
docs.text: Level Content Status 1. Requirements Goals, interfaces, main flows, faults, debug Draft 2. IPU block specification Ports, registers and timing of the IPU top Not started 3. Sub-block specifications CTRL, cache agent, MULT, ACC, AAQ, host register block Not started

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
ID Goal IPU-GOAL-1 Run every kernel in the kernel library: convolution, linear, normalization and shaping, attention, softmax, and MobileViT-S. IPU-GOAL-2 Execute one VLIW word per clock cycle while no memory access misses. IPU-GOAL-3 Close timing at 1 GHz on the TSMC 5 nm process. IPU-GOAL-4 Run consecutive kernels with no host action between them. IPU-GOAL-5 Detect every illegal state in the fault list. By default, stop with the architectural state intact and report the cause. IPU-GOAL-6 Give the host halt, single-step, breakpoints and register read-out. Later debug features extend this set without changing halt behaviour.

The kernel library is the throughput benchmark. Area and power are not constraints at this level.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Item In scope CTRL, cache agent, MULT, ACC and AAQ stages Yes Host register block and debug Yes Cache unit (CRM, XMEM, DMA) Interface and expected behaviour only RISC-V host Interface and expected software flow only AAQ_EXACT and BREAK ISA slots No. These slots exist in the emulator only.

docs.title: Requirement conventions
docs.text:
• Each requirement has an ID of the form IPU-<AREA>-<n>. Block specifications trace to these IDs.
  • "Shall" marks a requirement on the IPU.
  • CU-<n> marks a behaviour the IPU expects from the cache unit.
  • SW-<n> marks a behaviour the IPU expects from host software.
  • F-<n> marks a fault in the fault list.
  • OQ-<n> marks an open question. A-<n> marks an action on another document.
  • A row marked Proposed is not agreed. Open questions holds its open question.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning VLIW word One instruction word. It holds one sub-instruction per slot. Slot A field of the VLIW word executed by one stage: COND, LR (three lanes), LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ. Kernel A program in one IMEM bank, with its CR bank and its table set. Context Context 0 or context 1. A context holds one IMEM bank, one CR bank and one table set. Active context The context the running kernel uses. The other context is the inactive context. Locked A locked context rejects host writes. Execution flow defines when a context is locked. Armed The inactive context is queued to run when the running kernel ends. Retire A word retires when the IPU has committed its last effect, including its store. Done A kernel is done when its HALT word retires. Host The RISC-V processor that loads kernels and controls the IPU. Cache unit The CRM, XMEM and DMA. It moves data between DRAM and XMEM. XMEM bank One of 16 on-chip memory banks. Each bank holds 1024 rows. Table A cache-unit data structure that maps one array to XMEM banks and DRAM. Cache agent The IPU stage that decides whether a word's memory accesses hit. Hit, miss A memory access hits when its XMEM bank is valid for the requested tag. Otherwise it misses. Halt The IPU stops at a word boundary and keeps its architectural state. Debug cause A halt cause other than a fault: halt request, step done, or breakpoint. AXI error A SLVERR response on the host port. Fault An illegal state that the IPU detects.

docs.title: Source documents
docs.text:
Document Use Instruction reference Instruction semantics and encodings Control stage specification CTRL behaviour Accumulator stage specification ACC behaviour AaQ and store stage specification AAQ behaviour, including the store Cache unit specification CRM, XMEM and DMA behaviour

Open questions lists the conflicts between these documents.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: Block Inside the IPU Role Host register block Yes AXI4 slave. Holds commands, status, interrupt control and debug registers. CTRL Yes Holds the PC, the IMEM banks, the CR banks and the LR file. Fetches words, resolves branches, executes the LR slots, and resolves CR and LR operand values for the later stages. Cache agent Yes Decides hit or miss for the load and the store of each word. Stalls CTRL on a miss. Issues the XMEM read. MULT Yes Holds R0, R1, R_CYCLIC and R_MASK. Produces the 128-element multiply result. ACC Yes Holds R_ACC. Combines the multiply result into it. AAQ Yes Applies the activation function to R_ACC, quantizes the result and writes the row to XMEM. Loads LUT segments from XMEM. Cache unit No CRM, XMEM and DMA. Holds the tables, fills XMEM banks from DRAM and drains them to DRAM. Host No Loads kernels, configures tables, and controls and debugs the IPU.

docs.title: Architectural state
docs.text: State Size Owner Host access PC One. Width is log2 of the IMEM bank depth. CTRL Read. Write while HALTED. IMEM Two banks. Depth: OQ-4. CTRL One address window per bank. Write while the context is not locked. CR0–CR15 Two banks of 16 registers. CR0 = 0 and CR1 = 1 in both banks. Width: OQ-3. CTRL Read. Write while the context is not locked. LR0–LR15 16 registers. Width: OQ-3. CTRL Read through debug. R0, R1 128 elements each MULT None R_CYCLIC 512 elements MULT None R_MASK 8 masks of 128 bits MULT None R_ACC 128 elements of 32 bits ACC None AAQ output row 128 NX8 elements of 8 bits, plus a 16-bit metadata word (scale[7:0], dynamic_exponent[8]). The element type is the qf operand of ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (ADR 0007; OQ-45). AAQ None

docs.title: Execution model
docs.text: ID Requirement IPU-ARCH-1 Each VLIW word shall execute atomically. The state after a word equals the state produced by executing its slots in this order: COND and LR, LOAD, MULT, ACC, AAQ. IPU-ARCH-2 The COND and LR slots shall read CR and LR values from before the word. IPU-ARCH-3 The LOAD, MULT, ACC and AAQ slots shall read LR values from after the LR writes of the same word. See OQ-10. IPU-ARCH-4 The IPU shall implement every ISA slot except AAQ_EXACT and BREAK. IPU-ARCH-5 The COND slot shall provide HALT, at the opcode the instruction reference assigns it. HALT ends the kernel after every slot of its word has retired. IPU-ARCH-6 Instruction semantics shall follow the instruction reference. The AaQ stage follows the AaQ architecture specification: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activates with the 3-bit function list, quantizes to one NX8 row and stores it with its metadata (ADR 0007). See OQ-5.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
The five stages are architectural. One word moves through them in order.

flowchart LR
    CTRL["CTRL<br/>fetch, branch, LR"] --> AGENT["Cache agent<br/>hit or miss"]
    AGENT --> MULT["MULT"] --> ACC["ACC"] --> AAQ["AAQ<br/>activate, quantize, store"]
    AGENT -.->|stall| CTRL
ID Requirement IPU-ARCH-10 The IPU shall process each word through five stages in this order: CTRL, cache agent, MULT, ACC, AAQ. IPU-ARCH-11 The IPU shall accept one word per clock cycle while the cache agent does not stall. IPU-ARCH-12 MULT, ACC and AAQ may each take more than one clock cycle. The latency of each stage shall be fixed. IPU-ARCH-13 Pipelining shall not change any architectural result. Only timing differs from the atomic model of IPU-ARCH-1. IPU-ARCH-14 The cache agent shall be the only source of backpressure. It stalls CTRL only. IPU-ARCH-15 A word that the cache agent has accepted shall retire a fixed number of cycles later. IPU-ARCH-16 CTRL shall take one clock cycle per word: LR update, branch decision and fetch of the next word. A taken branch costs no extra cycle. IPU-ARCH-17 CTRL shall commit the LR writes and the PC update of a word only when the cache agent accepts the word. See OQ-16.

IPU-ARCH-17 makes stalls, halts and faults precise: a word that is not accepted has changed nothing.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text: The host debugs the IPU through the host port. Step 0 is the debug feature set of the first hardware version.

docs.title: Step 0 requirements
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-DBG-1 The host shall be the only debugger. All debug access uses the host port. IPU-DBG-2 HALTED shall mean: the pipeline is empty and the architectural state is at a word boundary. This holds for every halt cause. IPU-DBG-3 The IPU shall record the halt cause: halt request, step done, breakpoint, or fault. IPU-DBG-4 For a breakpoint the IPU shall record the breakpoint index. For a fault it shall record the fault code. IPU-DBG-5 When one word meets several halt causes, the IPU shall record the first of: fault, breakpoint, halt request. IPU-DBG-6 STEP shall execute exactly one word, wait for it to retire, and enter HALTED with cause "step done". IPU-DBG-7 During a step the run state shall be RUNNING_UNARMED or RUNNING_ARMED. The IPU accepts HALT and ABORT. IPU-DBG-8 When the stepped word holds the HALT instruction, the kernel is done. After a handoff, the IPU shall enter HALTED at PC 0 of the next kernel. IPU-DBG-9 The IPU shall provide PC breakpoints. The number of breakpoints is a parameter with default 4. IPU-DBG-10 Each breakpoint shall hold an enable bit, a context and a PC. IPU-DBG-11 When the PC and active_ctx match an enabled breakpoint, the IPU shall halt before the matched word executes. IPU-DBG-12 RESUME and STEP shall execute the word at the PC without triggering its breakpoint again. IPU-DBG-13 The host shall be able to read the PC, LR0–LR15, both CR banks and the run state in every run state. IPU-DBG-14 The host shall be able to write the PC in HALTED with a debug cause. IPU-DBG-15 The host shall be able to read the IMEM bank of the active context in HALTED and IDLE. IPU-DBG-16 LR and the CR bank of a locked context shall be read-only to the host.

In a running state, the PC and LR values that the host reads change from cycle to cycle.

IPU-DBG-8 without a handoff leaves the IPU in IDLE. With a handoff, kernel_start pulses and the first word of the next kernel does not execute.

A halt request also takes effect while a word is stalled on a miss: IPU-EXEC-22 in Execution flow.

Step 0 has no read-out of R0, R1, R_CYCLIC, R_MASK and R_ACC. A kernel exposes vector data by storing it to XMEM.

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-DBG-20 The debug registers shall occupy their own address window in the register file: capability, PC, LR read-out and breakpoints. IPU-DBG-21 The first register of the window shall be a capability register. It holds the debug version, the number of breakpoints and one bit per optional feature. IPU-DBG-22 A debug feature beyond step 0 shall add registers in the window and a bit in the capability register. It shall not change IPU-DBG-2.

Every debug feature reads or writes state while the IPU is HALTED. HALTED always means an empty pipeline at a word boundary, so a feature beyond step 0 needs no change to halt behaviour.

Candidate features beyond step 0: vector register read-out, LR and CR writes, data watchpoints, and execution trace.

docs.title: Flow: halt
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as Host (RISC-V)
    participant I as IPU (CTRL, registers)
    participant A as Cache agent
    Note over I: RUNNING (armed or unarmed)
    alt Breakpoint
        Note over I: PC matches a breakpoint register
    else Fault
        Note over I,A: CTRL or cache agent detects<br/>an illegal state at word W
    else Halt request
        H->>I: HALT
    end
    Note over I: Word W and younger words<br/>do not execute.<br/>Older words retire.
    Note over I: HALTED, cause and PC = W recorded
    I-->>H: irq HALTED
    H->>I: Read cause, PC, LR, CR
    alt Debug cause
        H->>I: STEP
        Note over I: Execute one word, HALTED again
        H->>I: RESUME
        Note over I: RUNNING, armed flag as before
    else Fault cause
        H->>I: ABORT
        Note over I: IDLE, armed flag cleared
    end

docs.title: Contexts
docs.text:
The IPU has two contexts, 0 and 1. Context k holds IMEM bank k, CR bank k and table set k. The active_ctx bit selects all three for the running kernel. The IPU owns active_ctx and drives it to the cache unit.

A context is locked:

  • while it is the active context and the IPU is not IDLE, or
  • while it is armed.

The host loads a kernel into the inactive context while that context is not locked.

docs.title: Run states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> IDLE: reset
    IDLE --> RUNNING_UNARMED: ARM<br/>flip active_ctx, PC = 0
    RUNNING_UNARMED --> RUNNING_ARMED: ARM
    RUNNING_ARMED --> RUNNING_UNARMED: DISARM
    RUNNING_ARMED --> RUNNING_UNARMED: kernel done<br/>flip active_ctx, PC = 0
    RUNNING_UNARMED --> IDLE: kernel done
    RUNNING_UNARMED --> HALTED: halt request, breakpoint,<br/>step done, fault
    RUNNING_ARMED --> HALTED: same causes<br/>armed flag kept
    HALTED --> RUNNING_UNARMED: RESUME or STEP<br/>armed flag clear
    HALTED --> RUNNING_ARMED: RESUME or STEP<br/>armed flag set
    HALTED --> IDLE: ABORT
    RUNNING_UNARMED --> IDLE: ABORT
    RUNNING_ARMED --> IDLE: ABORT
State Meaning IDLE No kernel runs. The pipeline is empty. Both contexts are unlocked. RUNNING_UNARMED A kernel runs. No kernel is armed. RUNNING_ARMED A kernel runs. The kernel in the inactive context starts when the running kernel is done. HALTED The kernel stands at a word boundary. The pipeline is empty. The armed flag keeps its value. The HALT instruction does not enter this state: it ends the kernel (IPU-EXEC-11; to confirm, OQ-31). The HALT command does.

ARM and DISARM in HALTED change the armed flag only. The diagram omits them.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
The host issues a command by writing 1 to its bit in the command register.

Command Accepted in Effect ARM IDLE Starts the kernel in the inactive context. ARM RUNNING_UNARMED, or HALTED with the armed flag clear Sets the armed flag. DISARM RUNNING_ARMED, or HALTED with the armed flag set Clears the armed flag. HALT RUNNING_UNARMED, RUNNING_ARMED Halts with cause "halt request". STEP HALTED with a debug cause Executes one word and halts with cause "step done". RESUME HALTED with a debug cause Returns to the running state. ABORT RUNNING_UNARMED, RUNNING_ARMED, HALTED Stops the kernel and goes to IDLE. Clears the armed flag.

A command written in a state that does not accept it has no effect and returns an AXI error. A DISARM that returns an AXI error tells the host that the handoff already happened.

docs.title: Start
docs.text: ID Requirement IPU-EXEC-1 The IPU shall be in exactly one run state: IDLE, RUNNING_UNARMED, RUNNING_ARMED or HALTED. IPU-EXEC-2 The IPU shall accept ARM only while tables_valid of the inactive context is high. Otherwise ARM returns an AXI error. IPU-EXEC-3 An ARM accepted in IDLE shall flip active_ctx, set PC = 0 and start fetching. See OQ-13. IPU-EXEC-4 An ARM accepted in RUNNING_UNARMED or HALTED shall set the armed flag and lock the inactive context. IPU-EXEC-5 A kernel start shall change no architectural state except active_ctx and the PC. LR and the vector registers keep their values. IPU-EXEC-6 The IPU shall reject host writes to the IMEM bank and the CR bank of a locked context with an AXI error.

docs.title: Done and handoff
docs.text: ID Requirement IPU-EXEC-10 The word that holds the HALT instruction shall be the last word of the kernel. Its other slots execute. CTRL fetches no word after it. IPU-EXEC-11 A kernel is done when its HALT word retires. IPU-EXEC-12 When a kernel is done and the armed flag is clear, the IPU shall go to IDLE. active_ctx keeps its value. IPU-EXEC-13 When a kernel is done and the armed flag is set, the IPU shall start the armed kernel in the same clock cycle. It flips active_ctx, sets PC = 0 and clears the armed flag. IPU-EXEC-14 The first word of the next kernel shall enter the pipeline only after the previous kernel is done. IPU-EXEC-15 The IPU shall pulse kernel_done when a kernel is done and kernel_start when a kernel starts. IPU-EXEC-16 At a handoff, kernel_done, kernel_start and the active_ctx flip shall occur in the same cycle. IPU-EXEC-17 The IPU shall set an interrupt status bit at each kernel start and each kernel done. IPU-EXEC-18 Kernel done shall not wait for the cache unit to drain output banks to DRAM.

docs.title: Halt and abort
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-EXEC-20 On a halt, the cache agent shall stop accepting words. Accepted words retire. The IPU then enters HALTED. IPU-EXEC-21 In HALTED, the PC shall hold the address of the next word to execute. IPU-EXEC-22 A halt or an abort shall take effect while a word is stalled on a miss. The stalled word does not execute. IPU-EXEC-23 RESUME shall return to RUNNING_ARMED when the armed flag is set and to RUNNING_UNARMED when it is clear. IPU-EXEC-24 On ABORT, the cache agent shall stop accepting words. Accepted words retire. The IPU then enters IDLE. IPU-EXEC-25 On entering IDLE after ABORT, the IPU shall clear the armed flag and pulse kernel_abort. active_ctx keeps its value. IPU-EXEC-26 When the cache agent has accepted the HALT word before a halt takes effect, the kernel shall be done first. IPU-EXEC-27 After IPU-EXEC-26 with the armed flag clear, the IPU shall go to IDLE and drop the halt. With the armed flag set, it shall enter HALTED at PC 0 of the next kernel. IPU-EXEC-28 The IPU shall evaluate a command against the run state that follows any kernel done of the same cycle. IPU-EXEC-29 A write that sets more than one command bit shall have no effect and shall return an AXI error.

The effect of ABORT on the XMEM banks of the aborted kernel is open: OQ-12.

docs.title: Flow: one kernel from IDLE
docs.text:
After reset active_ctx is 0, so the host loads the first kernel into context 1.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as Host (RISC-V)
    participant I as IPU (CTRL, registers)
    participant A as Cache agent
    participant C as Cache unit
    Note over I: IDLE, active_ctx = 0
    H->>I: Write kernel N to IMEM bank 1 and CR bank 1
    H->>C: Write table set 1, then commit
    C-->>I: tables_valid[1] = 1
    H->>I: ARM
    Note over I: Accepted because tables_valid[1] = 1
    I->>C: active_ctx = 1, kernel_start
    Note over I: PC = 0, RUNNING_UNARMED
    I-->>H: irq KERNEL_START
    I->>A: First word with a LOAD
    A->>C: Miss: bank_req
    Note over A: Stall CTRL
    C-->>A: bank_pub
    Note over A: Release stall
    Note over I,A: Kernel N executes<br/>one word per cycle on hits
    Note over I: HALT word fetched<br/>fetch stops, pipeline drains
    Note over I: HALT word retires
    I->>C: kernel_done
    Note over I: IDLE
    I-->>H: irq KERNEL_DONE
    C-->>I: tables_valid[1] = 0
    Note over C: DMA drains kernel N output banks
    C-->>H: Outputs are in DRAM (cache unit status)

docs.title: Flow: handoff between two kernels
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as Host (RISC-V)
    participant I as IPU (CTRL, registers)
    participant A as Cache agent
    participant C as Cache unit
    Note over I: RUNNING_UNARMED, kernel N<br/>active_ctx = 0
    H->>I: Write kernel N+1 to IMEM bank 1 and CR bank 1
    H->>C: Write table set 1, then commit
    C-->>I: tables_valid[1] = 1
    Note over C: DMA prefetches kernel N+1 data<br/>into banks tagged ctx 1
    H->>I: ARM
    Note over I: Accepted because tables_valid[1] = 1<br/>RUNNING_ARMED
    I->>C: ctx_locked[1] = 1
    Note over I,C: Context 1 is locked: IMEM bank 1, CR bank 1<br/>and table set 1 reject host writes
    Note over I,A: Kernel N keeps executing<br/>and hits only on banks tagged ctx 0
    Note over I: HALT word of kernel N retires
    I->>C: active_ctx = 1, kernel_done, kernel_start
    Note over I,C: Same cycle: IMEM, CR and table set switch to context 1<br/>PC = 0, RUNNING_UNARMED, kernel N+1
    I-->>H: irq KERNEL_DONE (N) and KERNEL_START (N+1)
    C-->>I: tables_valid[0] = 0
    I->>A: First word of kernel N+1
    Note over A: Hit: banks tagged ctx 1 were prefetched
    Note over C: DMA drains kernel N output banks.<br/>Table set 0 then accepts host writes.
    Note over H,C: The host loads kernel N+2 into context 0

The handoff is coherent because:

  1. One bit, active_ctx, selects the IMEM bank, the CR bank and the table set. The IPU owns it. The cache unit follows it.
  2. ARM succeeds only when the host has committed the table set of the next kernel.
  3. An armed context is locked on both sides.
  4. XMEM bank tags carry the context bit, so a kernel never hits on a bank of the other context.

docs.title: Expected from the cache unit
docs.text: ID Expected behaviour CU-10 The cache unit holds two table sets, one per context. CU-11 The cache unit raises tables_valid[k] when the host commits table set k. One commit allows one kernel run. CU-12 The cache unit clears tables_valid[k] on the kernel_done or kernel_abort of context k. CU-13 The cache unit rejects host writes to table set k while ctx_locked[k] is high. CU-14 The cache unit rejects host writes to table set k until it has drained the output banks of the last kernel of context k. CU-15 The cache unit uses the table set that active_ctx selects for IPU accesses, in the same cycle active_ctx changes. CU-16 The DMA may fill XMEM banks for a committed table set before its context is active. CU-17 On kernel_done, the cache unit drains every written bank and frees every other bank tagged with the context of that kernel. CU-18 The cache unit reports to the host when the outputs of a kernel are in DRAM.

docs.title: Expected from host software
docs.text: ID Expected behaviour SW-1 Before ARM, the host writes the kernel to the IMEM bank and the CR bank of the inactive context. SW-2 Before ARM, the host writes and commits the table set of the inactive context. SW-3 Every path through a kernel reaches a HALT word. SW-4 A kernel does not read LR or vector register values left by an earlier kernel. SW-5 The two table sets do not claim the same XMEM bank at the same time. See OQ-11.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text: A fault is an illegal state that the IPU detects. The fault policy is agreed. The fault list is a proposal: OQ-1.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-FLT-1 The IPU shall detect every illegal state in the fault list. It shall never continue silently with wrong data. IPU-FLT-2 The IPU shall detect every fault in CTRL or in the cache agent, before the cache agent accepts the faulting word. IPU-FLT-3 Faults shall be precise. The faulting word and all younger words have no architectural effect. All older words retire. IPU-FLT-4 On a fault, the IPU shall enter HALTED and record the fault code and the PC of the faulting word. IPU-FLT-5 Each fault shall have an enable bit. When the bit is set, the fault halts. When it is clear, the fault only sets a sticky flag. IPU-FLT-6 All fault enable bits shall be set after reset. IPU-FLT-7 After a fault halt, the IPU shall reject RESUME, STEP and PC writes with an AXI error. The host stops the kernel with ABORT. IPU-FLT-8 When one word raises several faults, the IPU shall record the fault with the lowest number. IPU-FLT-9 An illegal host access shall not halt the IPU. It returns an AXI error and sets the HOST_ERR interrupt status bit.

IPU-FLT-2 is possible because CTRL resolves every CR and LR operand value before it dispatches a word. Every check in the fault list uses values that CTRL or the cache agent holds.

The behaviour of a word whose fault enable bit is clear is open: OQ-2.

docs.title: Fault list
docs.text:
Status: Proposed. Owner: Yuval Harary.

ID Illegal state Detected in Proposed behaviour F-1 A slot holds a reserved opcode or a reserved operand encoding. CTRL Halt F-2 CTRL fetches at a PC at or beyond the program length, by sequential flow, branch or BR. CTRL Halt. Needs a program-length register per IMEM bank. F-3 Two LR lanes of one word write the same LR. CTRL Halt F-4 The index of LD.MULT.CYCLIC is not 0, 128, 256 or 384. CTRL Halt F-5 ACC.RESHAPE has a mask above 8, or a participating source or destination index of 128 or more. CTRL Halt F-6 A load or a store addresses a table that is not configured, or a row beyond the table size. Cache agent Halt F-7 A load addresses a write-only table, or a store addresses a read-only table. Cache agent Halt F-8 A word stalls for longer than a programmable limit. Cache agent Halt. A limit of 0 disables the check. F-9 A kernel runs for more cycles than a programmable limit. CTRL Halt. A limit of 0 disables the check.

Reserved encodings for F-1, from the instruction reference:

Slot Reserved encodings COND One opcode of the 3-bit field. LR Seven opcodes of the 4-bit field. k outside 1 to 9 in INC.MODP2. LOAD MultStageReg values other than R0 and R1. MULT Two opcodes of the 3-bit field. MultStageReg values other than R0 and R1. ACC Three opcodes of the 4-bit field. Values above 2 of elements_in_row, horizontal_stride and vertical_stride. AAQ One opcode of the 2-bit field. lut_addr outside 0 to 4 in LD.LUT. Values above 6 of activation_fn.

The fault list and this table are mirrored as data in ipu_isa.faults, which derives the reserved encodings from the ISA. A test (//src/ipu-isa:test_faults_docs) checks that both tables state the same as that data.

docs.title: In the emulator
docs.text:
The emulator raises ipu_emu.errors.EmulatorFault for a fault. The exception carries the fault (FaultId) and the PC of the faulting word. The cycle that raises it first records IpuState.halt as HaltRecord("fault", pc, fault). A HALT word records HaltRecord("halt", pc, None). run_until_complete re-raises the fault, unless it is called with raise_on_fault=False. Faults are precise (IPU-FLT-3): a faulting word changes no register, XMEM byte, PC or statistic, only the halt record and the sticky flag. F-1 and F-3 are found before any slot runs; F-4 to F-6 by a check phase after the LR slot (whose results the other slots see forwarded), which undoes the LR writes on a fault. When one word raises several faults, the lowest number is recorded (IPU-FLT-8).

IpuState.faults (ipu_emu.fault_control.FaultControl) holds each fault's enable bit, all set at construction, and the sticky flags, which every fault sets, enabled or not (IPU-FLT-5, IPU-FLT-6). With F-1 disabled, the slot with the reserved encoding runs as NOP and the rest of the word retires (the proposal in OQ-2). With F-9 disabled, the run goes on past its limit. Clearing the bit of F-2 to F-6 raises ConfigurationError, because OQ-2 does not say what the word then does; clearing F-7 or F-8 changes nothing, as neither is modelled.

Fault In the emulator F-1 At fetch: an opcode the ISA does not define, or an operand code that is reserved (the table above) or past its operand type's width (a union column can be wider). F-2 A fetch at or past IpuState.program_length, which load_program sets, by sequential flow, branch or BR, including a target past IMEM. A state whose IMEM is written directly keeps all of IMEM. F-3 Two LR sub-slots write the same LR, detected before any LR write. F-4 An LD.MULT.CYCLIC index that is not a slot boundary. F-5 An ACC.RESHAPE mask above 8, or an index of 128 or more. F-6 An XMEM row beyond the address space. There is no table model yet, so the row is checked against XMEM; with the row in range, no load or store reaches past the allocation. F-7 Not modelled. The emulator has no table configuration, so no table is read-only or write-only. F-8 Not modelled. The emulator has no stall model (Q59, OQ-28). F-9 A run reaches IpuState.cycle_limit (default 1 000 000; a runner's max_cycles replaces it for that run; 0 disables the check). The fault's PC is the word that would have run next.

docs.title: Arithmetic events
docs.text:
Status: Proposed. Owner: Yuval Harary.

Accumulator overflow, NaN results and quantization saturation occur in ACC and AAQ, after the cache agent accepts the word. They are not faults and never halt. Step 0 does not detect them. The fault control registers reserve one sticky flag for each event.

In the emulator, ACC and AGG store the IEEE float32 result (an overflow is an infinity, a NaN stays) and set the event's flag in IpuState.arith_flags: ACC_OVERFLOW when a finite result rounds to an infinity (an AGG sum is judged on its exact total), NAN_RESULT when a stored lane is NaN, computed or copied (so R_ACC holding a NaN flags again at each ACC word). ACC.RESHAPE moves raw words and reports nothing. Flags are sticky: no run clears them, a reset does. A commit record lists each word's events. ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE sets QUANT_SATURATION when an element saturates: ±inf, a rounding carry above the row's scale, or a negative input to an unsigned NX8 type (ADR 0007). MULT stores the IEEE float32 product (an overflow is an infinity, in either mode: NX8 elements reach FP32's range through their row scale) and reports no event; whether a MULT overflow is an arithmetic event is open (OQ-18).

docs.text: Access Response Write to the IMEM bank, the CR bank or the program-length register of a locked context AXI error, HOST_ERR Write to CR0 or CR1 AXI error, HOST_ERR Write to a read-only register AXI error, HOST_ERR Read of the IMEM bank of the active context in a running state AXI error, HOST_ERR Write to the PC outside HALTED, or in HALTED after a fault AXI error, HOST_ERR Command in a state that does not accept it AXI error, HOST_ERR ARM while tables_valid of the inactive context is low AXI error, HOST_ERR Write that sets more than one command bit AXI error, HOST_ERR Access to an unmapped address AXI error, HOST_ERR

docs.text:
The instruction reference defines these cases.

Case Behaviour mask_shift outside −3 to +3 Clamps to −3 or +3 valid_elements above 128 Clamps to 128 dest_slot of AGG.* above 127 Uses the value modulo 128 offset of ACC.STRIDE above 3 Uses the value modulo 4

docs.title: Host registers
docs.text: The host reaches the IPU through the host port, one AXI4 slave. The IPU block specification assigns register offsets and field layouts.

docs.title: Address spaces
docs.text:
Space Content Write Read IMEM window 0 IMEM bank 0 While context 0 is not locked In every state, except a running state with context 0 active IMEM window 1 IMEM bank 1 While context 1 is not locked In every state, except a running state with context 1 active Register file The register groups below Per register Per register

The hardware VLIW word is 169 bits (IPU_COMPOUND_INST_WIDTH), 192 bits padded to 32-bit beats; how it packs into the beats is open: OQ-14.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-HOST-1 The host port shall be one AXI4 slave with 32-bit data. IPU-HOST-2 The host port shall decode three address spaces: IMEM window 0, IMEM window 1 and the register file. IPU-HOST-3 The IMEM windows shall accept INCR bursts. IPU-HOST-4 The IPU shall check the access rules on each beat of a burst. IPU-HOST-5 An illegal access shall return an AXI error. It shall change no state except the HOST_ERR interrupt status bit. IPU-HOST-6 A host access shall never stall or disturb the pipeline. IPU-HOST-7 The IPU shall drive one level-sensitive interrupt, irq. irq is high while any interrupt status bit with its enable bit set is high. IPU-HOST-8 The host shall clear an interrupt status bit by writing 1 to it.

Faults lists the illegal accesses.

docs.text: Group Content Access Identification Block ID and version Read-only Command ARM, DISARM, HALT, STEP, RESUME, ABORT Write 1 to one bit to issue a command Status Run state, active_ctx, armed flag, tables_valid, ctx_locked, halt cause, breakpoint index, fault code, fault PC Read-only Interrupt status One bit per interrupt event Read, write 1 to clear Interrupt enable One bit per interrupt event Read and write CR bank 0 CR0–CR15 of context 0 Read. Write while context 0 is not locked. CR0 and CR1 are read-only. CR bank 1 CR0–CR15 of context 1 Read. Write while context 1 is not locked. CR0 and CR1 are read-only. Fault control One enable bit and one sticky flag per fault Read and write. Flags: write 1 to clear. Program length One register per IMEM bank. Proposed, for fault F-2. Read. Write while the context is not locked. Limits Stall limit and kernel cycle limit. Proposed, for faults F-8 and F-9. Read and write Debug window Capability register, PC, LR0–LR15, breakpoint registers See Debug

docs.title: Interrupt events
docs.text:
Event The IPU sets the status bit when KERNEL_START A kernel starts. KERNEL_DONE A kernel is done. HALTED The IPU enters the HALTED state, for any cause. HOST_ERR The IPU rejects a host access.

At a handoff, the IPU sets KERNEL_DONE and KERNEL_START in the same cycle.

docs.title: External interfaces
docs.text: Signal names and widths are provisional. The IPU block specification fixes them.

docs.title: Interface groups

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Group Signal Direction Width Description Clock and reset clk Input 1 Clock. rst_n Input 1 Active-low reset. Asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk. Host AXI4 s_axi_* Slave 32-bit data AXI4 slave with all five channels. Address and ID widths: OQ-15. Interrupt irq Output 1 Level-sensitive. High while an enabled interrupt status bit is set. Table view tbl_view Input TBL_W Both table sets as configured at the cache unit. TBL_W and the signal list: OQ-15. Kernel context tables_valid Input 2 Bit k is high when the table set of context k is committed. active_ctx Output 1 Active context. ctx_locked Output 2 Bit k is high while context k is locked. kernel_start Output 1 One-cycle pulse when a kernel starts. kernel_done Output 1 One-cycle pulse when a kernel is done. kernel_abort Output 1 One-cycle pulse when an ABORT takes the IPU to IDLE. Bank events bank_pub_valid Input 1 One-cycle pulse: an XMEM bank became valid. bank_pub_id Input 4 XMEM bank that became valid. bank_pub_tag Input 15 Tag the bank holds: {ctx, table_id[3:0], page[9:0]}. bank_free_valid Input 1 One-cycle pulse: a flushed XMEM bank is drained and free. bank_free_id Input 4 XMEM bank that is free. Bank requests bank_req_valid Output 1 One-cycle pulse: the cache agent needs a bank that is not valid. bank_req_tag Output 15 Tag the cache agent needs. bank_req_write Output 1 High when the bank is needed for a store. bank_release_valid Output 1 One-cycle pulse: the cache agent releases a bank the IPU read. bank_release_id Output 4 XMEM bank released. bank_flush_valid Output 1 One-cycle pulse: a bank the IPU wrote is ready to drain to DRAM. bank_flush_id Output 4 XMEM bank to drain. Load port ld_valid Output 1 Load request. ld_bank Output 4 XMEM bank to read. ld_row Output 10 Row in the bank. ld_data Input 1024 Row data. ld_meta Input 16 Row metadata. The port table is also available as CSV.

The other pages name each bank event by its prefix. For example, bank_pub is the event that bank_pub_valid, bank_pub_id and bank_pub_tag carry.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-IF-1 The IPU shall use one clock domain, clk. IPU-IF-2 The IPU shall use one active-low reset, rst_n, asserted asynchronously and released synchronously. IPU-IF-3 Reset shall put the IPU in IDLE with active_ctx = 0 and PC = 0. IPU-IF-4 Reset shall clear the armed flag, the interrupt status and enable bits, and the breakpoint enables. IPU-IF-5 Reset shall mark every XMEM bank as not valid in the cache agent. IPU-IF-6 The IPU shall drive ld_valid only for the load of a word that the cache agent accepts. IPU-IF-7 The IPU shall drive st_valid only for the store of a word that the cache agent accepted. IPU-IF-8 The IPU shall never wait on the load port or the store port. Neither port has a ready signal.

The host port and irq requirements are in Host registers.

docs.title: Expected from the cache unit
docs.text:
ID Expected behaviour CU-1 XMEM returns ld_data and ld_meta one clock cycle after ld_valid. CU-2 XMEM accepts every store in the cycle st_valid is high. CU-3 tbl_view is stable for a context while ctx_locked of that context is high. CU-4 rst_n resets the cache unit: every XMEM bank is free and tables_valid is 0.

Execution flow and Memory access hold the other expected behaviours.

docs.title: Memory access
docs.text: The IPU reads and writes XMEM rows. The cache unit fills XMEM banks from DRAM and drains them to DRAM. The cache agent decides, for each word, whether its memory accesses can proceed.

docs.title: Address
docs.text:
Every XMEM access names a base register (CR) and an offset register (LR): the loads of the LOAD slot, and LD.LUT, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE and ACTIVATE.EXACT in the AAQ and AAQ_EXACT slots. CTRL computes the row address:

row_address = CR[base] + LR[offset]      // LR value after the LR writes of the same word

The row address identifies a table and an offset in that table.

Field Bits Meaning table_id 4 Table that holds the array. Position in the row address: OQ-8. page offset[19:10] Page of the table. One page maps to one XMEM bank. row offset[9:0] Row in the XMEM bank

The tag of an access is {ctx, table_id, page}, where ctx is active_ctx. An access hits when the XMEM bank for that page is valid and holds the same tag.

docs.title: XMEM bank states
docs.text:
State Meaning Hit Free The bank holds no tag. No Valid The bank holds a tag. The IPU can load from it or store to it. Yes, on a tag match Draining The IPU flushed the bank. The DMA writes it to DRAM. No

Each table has a jump_back parameter. When an access reaches row jump_back or beyond in a bank, the kernel does not access the previous bank of the table again. That access is the jump-back point of the previous bank. The cache unit specification, sections 9.1 and 9.2, defines the rule.

docs.title: Cache agent
docs.text:
ID Requirement IPU-MEM-1 The cache agent shall decide hit or miss for the load and the store of a word in the cycle CTRL presents the word. See OQ-16. IPU-MEM-2 The cache agent shall decide from state it holds: the table view of the active context and the state and tag of each XMEM bank. IPU-MEM-3 The cache agent shall accept a word only when every memory access of the word hits and the word raises no fault. IPU-MEM-4 The cache agent shall accept a word that has no memory access without delay. IPU-MEM-5 On a miss, the cache agent shall stall CTRL and send one bank_req for each missing tag. IPU-MEM-6 The cache agent shall send at most one bank_req per cycle. The request for the load goes first. IPU-MEM-7 The cache agent shall accept the stalled word when the cache unit has published every bank the word needs. IPU-MEM-8 For a load that hits, the cache agent shall issue the XMEM read of the accepted word. The MULT slot of the same word uses the loaded data. See OQ-9. IPU-MEM-9 The cache agent shall not flush or release an XMEM bank while an accepted word has an unwritten store to it. IPU-MEM-10 The cache agent shall hit only on tags whose ctx bit equals active_ctx. IPU-MEM-11 The cache agent shall never report a hit for a bank that is not valid. IPU-MEM-12 The cache agent may report a miss for a bank that became valid in the last few cycles.

A load of a row that an older word in the pipeline stores to is open: OQ-17.

docs.title: Bank state ownership
docs.text:
The cache agent and the cache unit each hold the state of the 16 XMEM banks. The cache unit makes the changes that make a bank available. The cache agent makes the changes that give a bank back. Each side reports its changes to the other side.

Change Trigger Made by Reported with Free to valid: the DMA filled the bank DMA fill complete Cache unit bank_pub Free to valid: the cache unit claimed the bank for a store bank_req with bank_req_write Cache unit bank_pub Valid to free: the IPU loaded past the jump-back point of a read bank IPU load Cache agent bank_release Valid to draining: the IPU stored past the jump-back point of a written bank IPU store Cache agent bank_flush Draining to free: the DMA wrote the bank to DRAM DMA drain complete Cache unit bank_free Every bank of a context leaves valid Kernel done or abort Both, in the same cycle kernel_done, kernel_abort ID Requirement IPU-MEM-20 The cache agent shall compute the bank state changes that IPU accesses trigger, from the accesses of accepted words and the table view. IPU-MEM-21 The cache agent shall report each such change to the cache unit with bank_release or bank_flush. IPU-MEM-22 The cache agent shall apply each bank_pub and bank_free event to its bank state. IPU-MEM-23 On kernel_done and on kernel_abort, the cache agent shall mark every bank tagged with the context of that kernel as not valid.

docs.title: Expected from the cache unit
docs.text:
ID Expected behaviour CU-20 The cache unit never takes a bank out of the valid state on its own. A bank leaves valid only through bank_release, bank_flush, kernel_done or kernel_abort. CU-21 The cache unit publishes a read bank only after the DMA has filled the whole bank. CU-22 On bank_req, the cache unit makes a bank valid for the requested tag and publishes it. CU-23 The cache unit ignores a bank_req for a tag that is valid or that the DMA is filling. CU-24 On bank_flush, the cache unit drains the bank to DRAM and then sends bank_free. CU-25 On bank_release, the cache unit treats the bank as free. CU-26 Every bank tag carries the context bit.

With CU-20, a late event costs a stall cycle and never a wrong result. The cache agent can learn late that a bank became valid. A bank that the cache agent holds as valid is always valid.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
An open question blocks the requirement or the block specification that links to it. To close a question, move its answer into the requirement and delete the row.

Questions OQ-18 onwards concern the emulator and the ISA definition, not only the hardware requirements.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text: ID Question Proposal Owner OQ-1 Which illegal states does the IPU detect, and what does each do? The fault list, rows F-1 to F-9, and the arithmetic events Yuval Harary OQ-2 What does a word do when its fault enable bit is clear? Decide per fault. For F-1, the slot with the reserved encoding executes as NOP. Yuval Harary

docs.title: Conflicts between existing documents
docs.text: ID Topic Conflict Proposal Owner OQ-3 CR and LR width The control spec diagram says 20 bits. Its text and the instruction reference say 32 bits. 32 bits Unassigned OQ-4 IMEM bank depth The control spec says 128 words per bank and a 7-bit PC. The branch label field is 10 bits. The emulator holds 1024 words. 1024 words per bank and a 10-bit PC, as a parameter Unassigned OQ-5 SET source The instruction reference takes a CR index only. The control spec takes a 5-bit source with a signed immediate mode. CR index only Unassigned OQ-8 Row address to table mapping CTRL produces CR[base] + LR[offset]. The cache unit expects {table_id, offset[19:0]}. No document defines the mapping. The 24-bit sum is {table_id[3:0], offset[19:0]}. The base CR carries the table ID. Unassigned OQ-9 Load and use in one word The instruction reference allows LD.MULT and a MULT that reads the same register in one word. The control spec tells software to avoid it. Allowed. The MULT slot sees the data the LOAD slot of the same word fetched. This matches IPU-ARCH-1. Unassigned OQ-10 LR values in the ACC slot The control spec forwards LR values from after the LR writes of the word. The accumulator spec marks dest_slot, source and dest as values from before the word, and offset as the value after. One rule for all slots after CTRL: values from after the LR writes (IPU-ARCH-3) Unassigned

docs.title: Kernel flow
docs.text: ID Question Proposal Owner OQ-11 How does a kernel hand a table to the next kernel inside XMEM, with no DRAM round trip? The banks carry the context bit of the first kernel. The second kernel hits only on its own context bit. The cache unit retags the handed-over banks at kernel_done. The table set of the next kernel names the table it inherits. Cache unit owner OQ-12 What does the cache unit do with the XMEM banks of a kernel on kernel_abort? The cache unit frees every bank of the aborted context and drains none. Cache unit owner OQ-13 How does the host run the kernel in the active context again from IDLE? ARM always starts the inactive context. ARM takes a context argument in IDLE. Unassigned

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text: ID Question Proposal Owner OQ-14 How does the hardware VLIW word pack into 32-bit AXI beats? The width is answered (E03-22, ADR 0007): the emulator word without the emulator-only AAQ_EXACT and BREAK slots, 169 bits (IPU_COMPOUND_INST_WIDTH in the generated SV package, word_bits(Tag.HARDWARE) in ipu_isa.layout), 192 bits (24 bytes, six beats) padded to 32-bit beats, as assemble --target hardware writes it. Still open: how the 192 bits pack into AXI beats. Unassigned OQ-15 What are the AXI address and ID widths, and the width and signal list of tbl_view? Fix in the IPU block specification, together with the cache unit owner Unassigned

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text: ID Question Proposal Owner OQ-16 How do CTRL and the cache agent meet 1 GHz? IPU-ARCH-17 commits LR writes only when the cache agent accepts the word, and IPU-MEM-1 decides in the cycle CTRL presents the word. Option A: the cache agent decides in the CTRL cycle. Option B: it decides one cycle later and CTRL restores the LR file and the PC when the word is not accepted. Choose in the CTRL and cache agent specifications. Unassigned OQ-17 What happens when a word loads a row that an older word in the pipeline stores to? The store reaches XMEM several cycles after the load reads it. Scratch-pad and read-after-write tables allow both accesses. The cache agent stalls the load until the AAQ stage has written the row. Unassigned

docs.title: Emulator and ISA
docs.text: ID Question Evidence Proposal Owner OQ-18 What does the emulator do on an FP32 accumulator overflow or a NaN result? ACC and AGG store the IEEE float32 result (±inf, NaN) and set the sticky ACC_OVERFLOW or NAN_RESULT flag (E04-23; test_arith_events.py). MULT stores the IEEE product (an overflow is an infinity, in FP32 and NX8 modes alike) but sets no flag. ACTIVATE.EXACT (FP32 debug mode only) still raises OverflowError: float too large to pack with f format when an exact result does not fit FP32. Follow the arithmetic events: store the IEEE result (±inf, NaN), set the per-event sticky flag, never halt. Emulator change in E04 (faults and sticky arithmetic flags). Close when the arithmetic-events requirement leaves "Proposed". Yuval Harary OQ-21 What does exp2 return for large inputs? ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE follows the AaQ architecture spec, whose exp2 takes non-positive inputs only: a positive input is an emulator error (ADR 0007). The emulator-only ACTIVATE.EXACT computes math.exp(x * math.log(2.0)) (activations.py), which raises OverflowError for x above about 1024; results between about 2^128 and 2^1024 are finite doubles, and the FP32 store then raises float too large to pack. Decide with OQ-18: ACTIVATE.EXACT returns +inf. Unassigned OQ-24 What do reciprocal(0) and rsqrt(0) return? The AaQ architecture spec adds epsilon = 2^-127, with the input's sign, to a zero or subnormal input (§4.3.1), so reciprocal(0) is 2^127 and rsqrt of a negative input is NaN; ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE does that (ADR 0007). The microarchitecture spec's pseudocode returns inf (MAS-stage-aaq-str.md:188, :190) and its function table 0 (:205-206). The emulator-only ACTIVATE.EXACT returns 0, and rsqrt 0 for every x ≤ 0 (activations.py). The architecture spec's rule; bring the microarchitecture spec in line (OQ-42). The answer fixes OQ-27. Unassigned OQ-27 Does LayerNorm add an epsilon before rsqrt? The kernel golden has no epsilon, because rsqrt maps a non-positive variance to 0 (ipu_kernels.reference.ops.layernorm, which every kernels/normalize LayerNorm uses as its golden, E07-10). The MobileViT full-layer chains use the same reference, with no epsilon (kernels/mobilevit/mobilevit_layer.py, E07-24). One reference that matches the kernel, with no epsilon. The LayerNorm kernels store rsqrt with the emulator-only ACTIVATE.EXACT (FP32), whose rsqrt keeps the 0. Revisit with OQ-24 when a LayerNorm runs in NX8. Unassigned OQ-28 How is F-8 (word stall limit) checked when the emulator has no stall model? The emulator executes one word per cycle and never stalls, so F-8 can never fire. E04 models the other faults with their IDs and enable bits. List F-8 as "not modelled" in the emulator and in the reference-model contract, until a cache-agent timing model exists. Yuval Harary OQ-29 When, and how, does the reference model move to ETISS? Out of scope for the architecture-deepening program. The reference contract is language-neutral: a versioned JSON commit-record and trace schema plus a conformance suite stored as data (ADR 0004), so another implementation can be checked against the same suite. Keep the contract language-neutral. Decide timing and scope (whole model or fast path only) later. Unassigned OQ-30 Where does the ELU α default come from, and how is it changed? apply_activation and ActivationParams read the module default DEFAULT_ELU_ALPHA when called or built, so patching it changes the α of states built afterwards; IpuState copies it at construction (activations.py). Only the emulator-only ACTIVATE.EXACT has elu; on hardware α would be baked into the loaded LUT of generic (OQ-38). Decide with OQ-38. Until then, set α through IpuState(activation=ActivationParams(elu_alpha=...)). Unassigned OQ-31 After the HALT instruction retires, does the IPU hand off (kernel done: IDLE, or the armed kernel starts) or enter HALTED? IPU-DBG-8 and IPU-EXEC-11 say the kernel is done; the execution flow lists halt requests (the HALT command), breakpoints, step done and faults as the causes that enter HALTED, not the HALT instruction. The emulator ends the run. Kernel done, as IPU-DBG-8 says. The requirements owner confirms. Unassigned OQ-32 Does the RTL repository use BRANCH_COND_COUNT as a parameter name? The control spec keeps BRANCH_COND_COUNT = 5 (the branches) and adds COND_OP_COUNT = 6 (branches plus HALT) rather than renaming it. Keep both until the RTL owner says which one the RTL uses. Unassigned OQ-36 What does ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE write for an inactive element? The AaQ architecture spec writes NaN (ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md §4.3); NX8 has no NaN code. The microarchitecture spec writes 0 (MAS-stage-aaq-str.md §6.2). The emulator writes 0 (ADR 0007). 0, until NX8 defines a NaN code (OQ-37). Yuval Harary OQ-37 Does NX8 have NaN and ±inf encodings? The MULT architecture spec marks it "TBD - ask Jacob" (ARCH-stage-mult.md §3.2.1). The AaQ architecture spec leaves elements that quantize to inf or NaN out of the scale (§4.3.2.1), and DS mask_type 3 is NaN. The emulator saturates ±inf to the largest magnitude and raises an error for NaN. Define them, or state that NX8 has none. Unassigned OQ-38 How is the AaQ LUT evaluated? The architecture spec defines the entry points (§4.2.3) but not the 17-bit entry format, nor how a value between entry points is computed. §4.2.2 calls max_exp_num a biased exponent; §4.2.3 uses it as 2^max_exp_num. range_mode = 3 and the entry order of version 3 are undefined. The emulator stores the LUT bits exactly and evaluates with exact math. Specify the entry format, the interpolation and the open fields. Unassigned OQ-39 Where does the LUT load read its data? Both specs load a segment from the low 32 words of R_ACC (ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md §4.2, MAS-stage-aaq-str.md §6.3); the architecture spec's LOAD_LUT also names table_id and table_offset that its operation never uses. The hardware reads the segment from XMEM. The emulator's LD.LUT reads the first 128 bytes of a row, and a word may not hold LD.LUT and another load (one XMEM read port). Correct both specs to an XMEM read. Unassigned OQ-40 What are the published QF and DS layouts? The architects' 16-bit QF and DS halves (ADR 0007) are not in a spec. The architecture specs have two different 32-bit quantizion_format layouts (AaQ §3.1, MULT §3.2) and a 32-bit dstructure with pad_mode at a TBD position (MULT §3.1). The emulator implements the 16-bit drafts. Publish the 16-bit layouts in both architecture specs. Unassigned OQ-41 Which mnemonics does the hardware use? The architecture specs name LOAD_LUT, LDR_MULT_REG, LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG and LDR_MULT_MASK_REG. The repo standard is UNIT.OP with no underscore (GLOSSARY.md, Mnemonic): LD.LUT, LD.MULT, LD.MULT.CYCLIC, LD.MASK. The specs adopt the repo names. Unassigned OQ-42 Where do the AaQ architecture and microarchitecture specs disagree? The store (merged into ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, or a separate ST.AAQ); the operands; the format source (a CR, or the table); the activation encodings (0–6 or 1–7); inactive elements (NaN or 0); reciprocal and rsqrt at 0 and below; the exp2 domain; the LUT metadata (46 or 75 bits); the LUT load operands; the opcode order. The emulator follows the architecture spec. Bring the microarchitecture spec into line with the architecture spec. Unassigned OQ-43 Is the dynamic exponent rule defined for 8-bit elements only? Dynamic quantization is signed with W = 8 (ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md §4.3.2.3), but the worked example uses W = 6. The rule scores truncation errors, while the quantizer it chooses for rounds to nearest. Give a W = 8 example and state which error the rule scores. Unassigned OQ-44 Does row metadata carry dynamic_static? The MULT architecture spec lists Scale, dynamic_static and dynamic_exponent (§3.2.1); the AaQ store (§4.3.3) and the cache unit (§6) write scale and dynamic_exponent only. MULT learns "dynamic" from its QF. The emulator stores no dynamic_static bit. Drop it from the MULT spec. Unassigned OQ-45 Is the element format a table property or an instruction operand? The cache unit gives each table a 9-bit format (§5); the architecture specs take the format from a QF operand. Drop the table format from the cache unit spec. Cache unit owner OQ-46 What does an all-zero row quantize to? The AaQ architecture spec treats every FP32 input as normalized (§4.3.2), zero included: a zero has exponent field 0, so an all-zero row gets scale 0 and each element the code of 1.0 × 2^-127, which reads back as 2^-127, not 0 (ipu_isa.nx8.row_scale, encode_row). A zero among nonzero elements reads back as 0 only when the row scale (biased) is at least 2^fe + fm; below that it reads back as a tiny nonzero value (in E7, any row whose largest magnitude is under 2.0). The emulator follows the spec. Special-case zero: an all-zero row stores code 0 in the clamp exponent (0.0). Unassigned OQ-47 Is the emulator's 17-bit LUT entry encoding the hardware's? No spec defines the entry format (OQ-38). ipu_isa/lut.py writes each entry as the top 17 bits of its FP32 pattern (sign, exponent, 8 mantissa bits) and max_exp_num as range_exp + 127; lut_image builds test rows with it. The emulator stores the bits exactly and evaluates with exact math, so the provisional encoding affects only what a test writes. Replace the encoding in ipu_isa/lut.py when the format is published; until then it is provisional. Unassigned OQ-48 What does an unsigned NX8 format do with a negative input? Neither AaQ spec says (ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md §4.3.2, MAS-stage-aaq-str.md). The emulator encodes a negative element, -inf included, as 0 and sets QUANT_SATURATION (ipu_isa.nx8.encode_row). A negative element still takes part in choosing the row scale, by its magnitude (row_scale), so a large negative input can lower the precision of the positive elements. State the rule in the AaQ architecture spec: clamp to 0, and say whether negative elements count toward the scale. Architects OQ-49 In which units does the dynamic-exponent rule measure errors? ARCH-stage-aaq-str.md §4.3.2.3 gives the steps as 2^(scale - E - fm1) and multiplies the squared errors by 2^(2*fm1); read literally, the scores shrink by 4 per binade the row's scale sits below 1.0, so a row of small values always selects fe2. Its own "both estimators are unbiased" table (A's pre-RTN value uniform on [1, 3)) holds only when errors are in units of 2^scale, and its worked example uses scale 0, where both readings agree. The emulator measures errors in units of the row's scale (ipu_isa.nx8.dynamic_scores), so scaling a row by a power of two never changes its choice. State in §4.3.2.3 that the errors are relative to 2^scale (the mantissa bits below the row's scale). Architects

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The AaQ (Activation and Quantization) stage perfome the following tasks:

  • Activation: The stage applies activation functions and special functions to each element of the fp32 vector. ReLU and GeLU are examples of the activation functions.
  • Quantization: The stage changes each fp32 element into the NX8 format. The quantization method is fixed or dynamic.
  • Store: After the quantization, the stage writes the result to XMEM.

Note: A configurable lookup table (LUT) implements some of the activation functions and special functions.

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text: Name Direction Description input data Input The 128-element fp32 vector from the ACC stage. Instruction Input The operation that the stage does on the input data. output data Output The 128-element NX vector. XMEM write address Output The XMEM address to which the stage writes the output data.

docs.title: 3.1 quantizion_format Layout
docs.text:
The quantizion_format operand names a 32-bit CR that holds the quantization format. It has four 8-bit fields:

Bits Field Description [31:24] dynamic_static 0 = static, 1 = dynamic. In dynamic mode, the exponent format is e1 or e2 (section 4.3.2.3). [23:16] sign 0 = unsigned, 1 = signed. [15:8] num_bits Total element width W: 1-8. 0 is reserved/invalid. [7:0] exponent_format Exponent width fe in static mode: 1-7 = e1-e7.

docs.title: CR layout (dstructure)
docs.text:
The dstructure operand names a 32-bit CR that holds the data structure format (DS) of the 128-element vector. It has four 8-bit fields:

Bits Field Description [31:24] N/A Not used. [23:16] valid_partition Number of valid groups. The rightmost num_partition - valid_partition groups are masked. [15:8] num_partition Number of groups: 1, 2, 4 or 8. 1 means one line of 128 elements, 2 means two lines of 64 elements. [7:0] valid_elements Number of valid elements in a group.

docs.title: Active elements rule
docs.text:
The dstructure fields select which of the 128 elements are active.

The 128 elements are split into num_partition equal groups. Each group has group_size = 128 / num_partition elements. Then:

  1. Only the first valid_partition groups are active. The remaining groups are masked.
  2. In each active group, only the first valid_elements elements are active.
group_size = 128 / num_partition
active[i] = (i / group_size < valid_partition) and (i % group_size < valid_elements)

Example: num_partition = 4, valid_partition = 3, valid_elements = 10. Each group has 32 elements, so active elements are 0-9, 32-41 and 64-73 (30 elements). Group 3 (96-127) is masked.

docs.title: 4. AaQ-Str ISA
docs.text:
The AaQ slot is resolved by CTRL and forwarded down the pipeline. The stage does not read the CR/LR register files itself (see the Control Stage spec, section 5).

The opcode enum (aaq_inst_opcode_t, package ipu_instr_pkg) is generated from instruction_spec.py by sv_package.py.

Note: Each CR0-CR15 and LR0-LR15 register named in the instruction operands is 32 bits wide.

Instructions in this section:

Instruction Purpose NOP Do nothing. LOAD_LUT Fill the function estimation LUT. ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE Activate, quantize and store.

docs.title: 4.1 NOP: No Operation
docs.text: No operation for the AaQ slot.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: NOP

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: NOP;;

docs.title: 4.2 LOAD_LUT: Load Function Estimation LUT Segment
docs.text:
LOAD_LUT fills one segment (1024 bits) of the function estimation LUT (section 4.2.1). The data comes from the lower 32 words of input data.

lut_addr selects which segment is written:

lut_addr What it loads 0-3 One 1024-bit slice of the table. 4 The last 256 bits of the table, plus the metadata block (section 4.2.2).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: LOAD_LUT lut_addr table_id table_offset

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Details lut_addr Imm 0-4. LUT segment index: 0-3 = table slices, 4 = last table bits + metadata. table_id CrIdx CR0-CR15. Supplies the table ID. table_offset LrIdx LR0-LR15. Supplies the offset in the table.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
payload[1023:0] = {input_data[31], ..., input_data[0]}     // 32 words x 32 bits

if lut_addr <= 3:                                          // full table slice
    TABLE_BITS[1024*lut_addr +: 1024] = payload

else if lut_addr == 4:                                     // last table bits + metadata
    TABLE_BITS[4351:4096] = payload[255:0]
    {pos_mode, neg_mode, range_mode, pos_c, neg_c, max_exp_num} = payload[301:256]
    // field layout in section 4.2.2

docs.title: Example
docs.text: LOAD_LUT 4 CR13 LR0;;      // load the metadata block

docs.title: 4.2.1 Function Estimation LUT
docs.text:
The stage holds one function estimation LUT. It has two parts:

Part Size Purpose Table 256 entries x 17 bits = 4,352 bits The function values. Metadata block 46 bits Configures range handling.

Both parts are filled by LOAD_LUT, one segment per instruction. The 3-bit lut_addr selects the segment. Five LOAD_LUT instructions (lut_addr 0-4) program the whole LUT.

docs.title: 4.2.2 Metadata Block
docs.text:
Where it lives. The metadata is in bits [301:256] of the lut_addr = 4 payload.

Fields.

Local bits Name Meaning [7:0] max_exp_num Largest biased FP32 exponent still inside the LUT range. exp > max_exp_num flags the element as out-of-range. [24:8] neg_c 17-bit constant substituted for negative out-of-range elements. [41:25] pos_c 17-bit constant substituted for positive out-of-range elements. [43:42] range_mode LUT version. See the range_mode table. [44] neg_mode Result for negative out-of-range elements: 0 = x (identity), 1 = neg_c. [45] pos_mode Result for positive out-of-range elements: 0 = x (identity), 1 = pos_c.

range_mode.

Value Version LUT entries LUT range 0 Version 1 256 entries for positive x. 0 <= x < 2^max_exp_num 1 Version 2 256 entries for negative x. -2^max_exp_num < x <= 0 2 Version 3 128 entries for negative x and 128 entries for positive x. -2^max_exp_num < x < 2^max_exp_num

docs.title: 4.2.3 LUT Addressing
docs.text:
The LUT entries are at linear intervals in the LUT range, with step = 2^max_exp_num / 256:

Version Interval Entry points Version 1 step 0, step, 2*step, ..., 2^max_exp_num - step Version 2 step 0, -step, -2*step, ..., -(2^max_exp_num - step) Version 3 2*step -(2^max_exp_num - 2*step), ..., -2*step, -0 and +0, 2*step, ..., 2^max_exp_num - 2*step

Version 3 has 128 entries for each side, so the interval is 2*step.

Version 3 has two entries at zero: -0 is the last negative entry and +0 is the first positive entry.

Example, Version 1. The LUT range is 0 to 4 (2^max_exp_num = 4). step = 4/256. The entry points are:

0, 4/256, 8/256, ..., 4 - 4/256

Example, Version 3. The LUT range is -2 to 2 (2^max_exp_num = 2). step = 2/256. The interval is 2*step = 4/256. The entry points are:

-2 + 4/256, ..., -4/256, -0, +0, 4/256, ..., 2 - 4/256

docs.title: 4.3 ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE: Activate and Quantize
docs.text:
Activation, quantization and store happen in a single instruction.

The instruction works in three steps:

Step What happens Section 1. Activate Applies an element-wise activation function to every element of input data. 4.3.1 2. Quantize Converts each activated fp32 element into the NX8 format. 4.3.2 3. Store Writes the result to XMEM. 4.3.3

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE activation_fn, dstructure, quantizion_format, table_id, table_offset

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Used by Details activation_fn Imm Activate Enum that names the activation (see activation_fn Values). dstructure CrIdx Quantize CR0-CR15. Supplies the structure of the 128-element vector: valid_partition, num_partition, valid_elements (section 3.2). quantizion_format CrIdx Quantize CR0-CR15. Supplies the quantization format (section 3.1). table_id CrIdx Store CR0-CR15. Supplies the ID of the destination table. table_offset LrIdx Store LR0-LR15. Supplies the offset in the destination table.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
for i in 0..127:
    activated[i] = activate(activation_fn, input_data[i])   // 4.3.1: all elements

for i in 0..127:                                            // active[i]: section 3.2
    if active[i]:
        aaq_out.elements[i] = quantize(activated[i])        // 4.3.2
    else:
        aaq_out.elements[i] = NaN

aaq_out.scale            = scale                        // section 4.3.2.1
aaq_out.dynamic_exponent = dynamic_static ? (fe == 2) : 0     // section 4.3.2.3
XMEM[table_id, table_offset] = aaq_out                  // 4.3.3: store

docs.title: Example
docs.text: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu, CR15, CR14, CR13, LR0;;

docs.title: 4.3.1 Activate
docs.text:
Applies the function named by activation_fn to every element of input data.

Computed activation_fn Directly identity, relu, relu6 Through the LUT reciprocal, rsqrt, exp2, generic

There is a LUT, loaded by LOAD_LUT (section 4.2). For the LUT-based functions, load the matching function before ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE.

docs.title: activation_fn Values
docs.text: Encoding Name Formula Computed by 0 identity f(x) = x Direct 1 relu f(x) = max(0, x) Direct 2 relu6 f(x) = min(max(0, x), 6) Direct 3 reciprocal f(x) = 1/x LUT + dedicated logic 4 rsqrt f(x) = 1/√x LUT + dedicated logic 5 exp2 f(x) = 2^x LUT + dedicated logic 6 generic f(x) = Generic(x) LUT + dedicated logic

docs.title: Special Cases
docs.text:
epsilon = 2^-127.

Function Input x Result reciprocal non-negative subnormal f(x) = 1/(x + epsilon) reciprocal negative subnormal f(x) = 1/(x - epsilon) reciprocal inf 0 rsqrt non-negative subnormal f(x) = 1/sqrt(x + epsilon) rsqrt inf 0 rsqrt negative NaN exp2 -inf 0 exp2 positive not supported (input must be non-positive)

docs.title: The generic Function: LUT Versions
docs.text:
The LUT for generic has three versions. range_mode selects the version. The drawings that follow are a reference for each version.

Note: pos_c is the constant for the positive side of the x axis. neg_c is the constant for the negative side of the x axis. The value of each constant can be positive or negative.

docs.title: Version 1 (range_mode = 0)
docs.text:
All 256 LUT entries are for positive x. Out of the LUT range, pos_mode and neg_mode select the result: x (identity) or a constant.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{LUT}(x) & 0 \le x < 2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{pos\_c} & x \ge 2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{neg\_c} & x < 0 \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Version 2 (range_mode = 1)
docs.text:
All 256 LUT entries are for negative x. Out of the LUT range, pos_mode and neg_mode select the result: x (identity) or a constant.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{LUT}(x) & -2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} < x \le 0 \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{neg\_c} & x \le -2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{pos\_c} & x > 0 \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Version 3 (range_mode = 2)
docs.text:
The LUT entries are divided into 128 entries for negative x and 128 entries for positive x. Out of the LUT range, pos_mode and neg_mode select the result: x (identity) or a constant.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{LUT}(x) & -2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} < x < 2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{pos\_c} & x \ge 2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \\ x \ \text{or} \ \mathrm{neg\_c} & x \le -2^{\mathrm{max\_exp\_num}} \end{cases} \]

docs.title: 4.3.2 Quantize
docs.text:
Converts each activated fp32 element (IEEE-754 single precision: sign S, 8-bit exponent e, 23-bit mantissa) into the NX8 format set by quantizion_format (section 3.1).

Outputs:

Output Description Elements One 8-bit element per input element. Elements that are not active output NaN. scale One 8-bit scale shared by the whole block. dynamic_exponent e1 or e2: the exponent width chosen in dynamic quantization.

Element format. Each element is packed from the MSB as {S?, Exp, M, 0-pad}:

Field Width Present when Value S 1 bit sign = 1 (signed) The input sign, passed through. Exp fe bits (fe >= 1) always Section 4.3.2.2. M fm = W - fe - sign bits (fm >= 0) always Section 4.3.2.2. 0-pad the rest of the 8 bits W < 8 0

docs.title: 4.3.2.1 Block Scale and Exponent Distance
docs.text:
Scale. scale is an 8-bit e8m0 value (exponent only). It is the largest raw exponent among the active elements:

scale = max(e[i] for i in 0..127 if active[i] and not is_inf_nx8[i] and not is_nan[i])
    // is_inf_nx8: inf or -inf; is_nan: NaN

Note: An element that quantizes to inf or -inf in the NX8 format is left out of the scale.

Exponent distance. Each element is encoded by its distance from the scale:

E = scale - e

E >= 0 for every element. E = 0 at the element(s) with the block maximum, and E grows as the element gets smaller relative to that maximum.

docs.title: 4.3.2.2 Exponent and Mantissa Encoding
docs.text:
RTN is round to nearest. An exact half rounds up (away from zero in magnitude): 0.5 -> 1, 1.5 -> 2, 2.5 -> 3.

Branch Condition Exp M Direct 0 <= E < 2^fe - 1 E RTN(1.M) rounded to fm bits Clamp E >= 2^fe - 1 2^fe - 1 (saturated) RTN(1.M >> [E - (2^fe - 1) + 1])

In the clamp branch the extra right-shift keeps the element's magnitude.

Rounding carry. When RTN carries out of the fm bits (M == 2^fm), the result is corrected:

Branch Corrected result Reason Direct, E > 0 Exp = E - 1, M = 0 1.11...1 rounded up to 10.00...0: the value moved one binade up. Direct, E = 0 Exp = 0, M = 2^fm - 1 There is no binade above the scale, so the element saturates at the largest value. Clamp Exp = 2^fe - 2, M = 0 0.11...1 rounded up to 1.00...0: the smallest directly-encoded value.

docs.title: 4.3.2.3 Dynamic Exponent Selection (fe = 1 or fe = 2)
docs.text:
Applies when dynamic_static = 1 (dynamic). Dynamic mode supports two formats, both signed and 8 bits wide (sign = 1, num_bits = 8):

Format fe fm dynamic_exponent e1m6 1 6 0 e2m5 2 5 1 Split Exponent bits Mantissa bits Encodable E Step at E fe1 1 fm1 0, 1 2^(scale - E - fm1), clamped at E >= 1 fe2 2 fm1 - 1 0, 1, 2, 3 2^(scale - E - fm1 + 1), clamped at E >= 3
  • fe1 is one bit finer near the top of the block.
  • fe2 reaches two binades further down before it clamps.

The rule uses fm1 only in the two multipliers, so it holds for any W and sign_bit.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• fm1 = W - 1 - sign_bit: the mantissa bits under fe1.
  • err1: the element's truncation error under fe1.
  • err2: the element's truncation error under fe2.

docs.title: Element classification
docs.text: Condition Sum Meaning E = 0 A fe1 is finer here. A measures the cost of choosing fe2. E = 1 none Don't care. 1 < E <= fm1 + 2 B fe2 is finer here. B measures the cost of choosing fe1. E > fm1 + 2 none Out of range for both splits.

docs.title: Per-element terms
docs.text:
A = RTN( |err2^2 - err1^2| * 2^(2*fm1) )
B = RTN( |err2^2 - err1^2| * 2^(2*(fm1 + 1)) )

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
if sum(B) - 4 * sum(A) < 0:  choose fe1        // dynamic_exponent = 0
else:                        choose fe2        // dynamic_exponent = 1

The B multiplier 2^(2*(fm1 + 1)) is four times the A multiplier 2^(2*fm1). Multiplying sum(A) by 4 puts both sums in the same units.

docs.title: Both estimators are unbiased
docs.text:
Assume the mantissa bits are uniformly distributed. Then r, the finer split's error as a fraction of its own step, is uniform on [0, 1), and the dropped bit is 1 with probability one half.

Term Pre-RTN value Distribution Outcomes E[RTN] E[pre-RTN] A 1 + 2r uniform on [1, 3) 1, 2, 3 at 0.25, 0.5, 0.25 2 2 B (1 + 2r) / 4 uniform on [0.25, 0.75) 0, 1 at 0.5, 0.5 0.5 0.5

Including the zero case, E[A] = 1 and E[B] = 0.25. Rounding adds noise to the sums, with no drift toward either format as the block grows.

docs.title: 4.3.3 Store
docs.text:
Writes the quantized result to XMEM, at the destination selected by table_id and table_offset.

Written Size Description Quantized elements 128 x 8 bits The quantized vector. scale 8 bits Scale shared by the whole vector. dynamic_exponent 1 bit e1 or e2: the exponent width chosen in dynamic quantization.

Note: The AaQ-Str stage gets the XMEM write address explicitly.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The ACC (Accumulator) stage owns R_ACC, a 128-element register of 32-bit elements, and combines each cycle's multiply result into it. It performs the following tasks:

  • Accumulate: Sets R_ACC to the multiply result, or adds, subtracts or takes the maximum of the multiply result and R_ACC, element by element.
  • Stride: Reshapes the multiply result with a predetermined pattern (every second column and/or row) into a range of R_ACC.
  • Aggregate: Reduces the valid elements of the multiply result to one value (sum or maximum) and writes it into one R_ACC element.
  • Reshape: Copies up to 8 elements of the multiply result to R_ACC. The source and destination of each element are arbitrary.
  • Bypass: Sends the multiply result to the output. R_ACC keeps its value.

Note: R_ACC is the stage's output to the AaQ stage every cycle, except in a BYPASS cycle.
