docs.text: Name Direction Description input data Input The multiply result from the MULT stage: 128 elements of 32 bits. Instruction Input The operation that the stage does on the input data. output data Output R_ACC, or input data: 128 elements of 32 bits, to the AaQ stage.

docs.title: 3.1 dstructure Layout
docs.text:
The cr_idx operand of ACC.STRIDE, AGG.SUM and AGG.MAX names a 32-bit CR that holds the data structure format of the 128-element vector. It has four 8-bit fields:

Bits Field Description [31:24] N/A Not used. [23:16] valid_partition Number of valid groups. The rightmost num_partition - valid_partition groups are masked. [15:8] num_partition Number of groups: 1, 2, 4 or 8. 1 means one line of 128 elements, 2 means two lines of 64 elements. [7:0] valid_elements Number of valid elements in a group.

docs.title: 3.2 Element Format
docs.text: Each R_ACC element is an FP32 value (IEEE-754 single precision), the same as each element of input data. It can be inf or -inf.

docs.title: 3.3 Running and .FIRST Variants
docs.text:
AGG.SUM and AGG.MAX each have a .FIRST variant:

Variant Uses the current R_ACC value Purpose Running (AGG.SUM) Yes Accumulate across cycles. .FIRST (AGG.SUM.FIRST) No: the result depends on input data only Start a new operation.

docs.title: 4. Accumulator ISA
docs.text:
The ACC slot is resolved by CTRL and forwarded down the pipeline. The stage does not read the CR/LR register files itself (see the Control Stage spec, section 5).

The opcode enum (acc_inst_opcode_t, package ipu_instr_pkg) is generated from instruction_spec.py by sv_package.py.

Note: Each CR0-CR15 and LR0-LR15 register named in the instruction operands is 32 bits wide. An LRD operand (a pair of LRs) comes with its value, as a CR operand does.

Instructions in this section:

Instruction Purpose NOP Do nothing. ACC.SET, ACC.ADD, ACC.SUB, ACC.MAX Set R_ACC to input data, or combine them, element by element. ACC.STRIDE Reshape input data into a range of R_ACC with a predetermined pattern. AGG.SUM, AGG.MAX Reduce input data to one R_ACC element. ACC.RESHAPE Copy chosen input data elements to chosen R_ACC elements. BYPASS Send input data to output data.

docs.title: 4.1 NOP: No Operation
docs.text: No operation for the ACC slot. R_ACC keeps its value.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: NOP

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: NOP;;

docs.title: 4.2 ACC.SET, ACC.ADD, ACC.SUB, ACC.MAX: Element-wise Accumulate
docs.text: Sets each element of R_ACC to the same element of input data, or combines them. All 128 elements are written.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
ACC.SET
ACC.ADD
ACC.SUB
ACC.MAX

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
For each element i in 0..127:

Mnemonic R_ACC[i] becomes ACC.SET input_data[i] ACC.ADD R_ACC[i] + input_data[i] ACC.SUB R_ACC[i] - input_data[i] ACC.MAX input_data[i] if input_data[i] > R_ACC[i], else R_ACC[i]

Special cases. param1 is R_ACC[i] and param2 is input_data[i]. x is any value that is not NaN. f is a finite value. ±inf is inf or -inf.

Mnemonic Case Result ACC.ADD, ACC.SUB, ACC.MAX param1 or param2 is NaN NaN ACC.ADD One parameter is inf, the other is -inf NaN ACC.SUB param1 and param2 are the same infinity NaN ACC.ADD One parameter is ±inf, the other is f or the same infinity That infinity ACC.SUB param1 is ±inf, param2 is f or the opposite infinity param1 ACC.SUB param1 is f, param2 is ±inf -param2 ACC.MAX One parameter is inf, the other is x inf ACC.MAX One parameter is -inf, the other is x x

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
ACC.SET;;            // first partial product of a dot product
ACC.ADD;;            // add the next ones

docs.title: 4.3 ACC.STRIDE: Accumulator Stride
docs.text: A reshape with a predetermined pattern. It views input data as rows, keeps every second column and/or every second row, and writes the kept elements, row by row, into a range of R_ACC. The other R_ACC elements keep their values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: ACC.STRIDE cr_idx, horizontal_stride, vertical_stride, offset

docs.title: Operands
docs.text:
Name Type Details dstructure CrIdx CR0-CR15. Supplies num_partition (section 3.1): the number of rows of input data. horizontal_stride Imm off, on or on_inv. Column pattern. vertical_stride Imm off, on or on_inv. Row pattern. offset Imm 0, 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96 or 112. The first written R_ACC element.

Pattern modes:

Mode Columns kept (horizontal_stride) Rows kept (vertical_stride) off all all on even: 0, 2, 4, ... even: 0, 2, 4, ... on_inv odd: 1, 3, 5, ... odd: 1, 3, 5, ...

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
rows = num_partition
elements_in_row = 128 / num_partition
view input_data as [rows][elements_in_row]          // row r = input_data[r*elements_in_row ...]
keep the columns selected by horizontal_stride
keep the rows selected by vertical_stride
kept = the kept elements, row by row                  // N elements

R_ACC[offset + k] = kept[k]   for k in 0..N-1

The number of written elements is:

horizontal_stride vertical_stride N (num_partition = 2, 4, 8) N (num_partition = 1) off off 128 128 on / on_inv off 64 64 off on / on_inv 64 128 on / on_inv on / on_inv 32 64

offset + N is at most 128.

Example: num_partition = 8, horizontal_stride = on, vertical_stride = on, offset = 0. input data is 8 rows of 16. The even columns of rows 0, 2, 4 and 6 are kept: 32 elements, written to R_ACC[0..31].

Note: When a data structure has fewer than 8 elements, the hardware pads it to 16.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: ACC.STRIDE CR3, on, on, 0;;

docs.title: 4.4 AGG.SUM, AGG.MAX: Aggregate
docs.text: Reduces the first valid_elements elements of input data to one value and writes it into one R_ACC element. The other R_ACC elements keep their values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
AGG.SUM dest_slot, cr_idx
AGG.SUM.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx
AGG.MAX dest_slot, cr_idx
AGG.MAX.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Details dest_slot LrIdx LR0-LR15. selects the written element. dstrcture CrIdx CR0-CR15. Supplies valid_elements (section 3.1).

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
n    = min(valid_elements, 128)
Mnemonic R_ACC[dest_slot] becomes AGG.SUM R_ACC[dest_slot] + sum(input_data[0..n-1]) AGG.SUM.FIRST sum(input_data[0..n-1]) AGG.MAX max(R_ACC[dest_slot], input_data[0..n-1]) AGG.MAX.FIRST max(input_data[0..n-1])

Special cases. AGG.SUM and AGG.SUM.FIRST follow the ACC.ADD special cases. AGG.MAX and AGG.MAX.FIRST follow the ACC.MAX special cases (section 4.2).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: AGG.SUM.FIRST LR0, CR3;;      // R_ACC[LR0 % 128] = sum of the first valid_elements elements

docs.title: 4.5 ACC.RESHAPE: Reshape
docs.text: A reshape with an arbitrary pattern: each element goes from any source index to any destination index. It copies up to 8 elements of input data to R_ACC. Two LRD register pairs hold the element indices: one list of 8 source indices and one list of 8 destination indices. The other R_ACC elements keep their values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: ACC.RESHAPE source, dest, number_idx

docs.title: Operands
docs.text:
Name Type Details source LrdIdx LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14. 8 byte indices source[0..7] into input data. dest LrdIdx LRD0, LRD2, ..., LRD14. 8 byte indices dest[0..7] into R_ACC. number_idx LrIdx / Imm An immediate 0-7, or LR0-LR15 whose value is 0-8. Elements 0..number_idx - 1 take part.

number_idx values. number_idx is the number of copied elements. Elements k = 0..number_idx - 1 are copied:

number_idx Copied k Skipped k 0 none 0-7 1 0 1-7 2 0-1 2-7 3 0-2 3-7 4 0-3 4-7 5 0-4 5-7 6 0-5 6-7 7 0-6 7

LRD layout. LRDn is the 64-bit pair {LR(n+1), LR(n)}. It holds 8 indices of 1 byte. Index 0 is in byte 0 of LR(n):

Byte Register byte Index 7 LR(n+1) byte 3 [7] 6 LR(n+1) byte 2 [6] 5 LR(n+1) byte 1 [5] 4 LR(n+1) byte 0 [4] 3 LR(n) byte 3 [3] 2 LR(n) byte 2 [2] 1 LR(n) byte 1 [1] 0 LR(n) byte 0 [0]

Every participating source[k] and dest[k] is 0-127.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
for k in 0..number_idx-1:                   // ascending k
    R_ACC[dest[k]] = input_data[source[k]]

When two dest[k] are equal, the higher k wins.

Example: number_idx = 6, source = 5, 9, 127, 100, 64, 42, 33, 20, dest = 0, 1, 18, 40, 64, 90, 101, 126. Elements k = 0..5 are copied, for example R_ACC[0] = input_data[5] and R_ACC[18] = input_data[127]. Elements k = 6, 7 are skipped. The figure has one column per k.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: ACC.RESHAPE LRD0, LRD2, 6;;      // copy elements 0-5 of the index lists

docs.title: 4.6 BYPASS: Bypass
docs.text: Sends input data to output data. R_ACC keeps its value.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: BYPASS

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
for i in 0..127:
    output_data[i] = input_data[i]

docs.title: Example
docs.text: BYPASS;;      // send the multiply result to the AaQ stage

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The MULT (Multiply) stage performs the following tasks:

  • Dequantize: Converts each NX8 input element to FP32, with the format from quantizion_format and the vector scale.
  • Multiply: Multiplies 128 pairs of FP32 elements. The operands come from R0/R1, R_CYCLIC or a scalar. Each product is an FP32 value.
  • Mask: Replaces the products of masked elements with a pad value. The mask comes from R_MASK.
  • Load: Owns the load instructions (LDR_MULT_REG, LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG, LDR_MULT_MASK_REG). Writes the load data from XMEM into one of the stage registers: R0, R1, one slot of R_CYCLIC or R_MASK.

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text:
Name Direction Description XMEM read address Output The XMEM row that a load instruction reads: offset + base. load data Input One XMEM row: 128 8-bit elements (128 B) and the vector metadata (section 3.2.1). Instruction Input The operation that the stage does on its registers. quantizion_format Input The NX8 format of the input elements (section 3.2). output data Output MULT_RES: 128 FP32 elements, to the ACC stage.

Note: The stage reads R0, R1, R_CYCLIC and R_MASK as they were at the start of the cycle. A load into them in the same cycle is visible in the next cycle.

docs.title: 3.1 dstructure Layout
docs.text:
The cr_idx operand (dstructure_cr_idx in MULT.VE and MULT.EE) names a 32-bit CR that holds the data structure format of the 128-element vector. It has four 8-bit fields:

Bits Field Description [31:24] N/A Not used. [23:16] valid_partition Number of valid groups. The rightmost num_partition - valid_partition groups are masked. [15:8] num_partition Number of groups: 1, 2, 4 or 8. 1 means one line of 128 elements, 2 means two lines of 64 elements. [7:0] valid_elements Number of valid elements in a group.

The stage also reads pad_mode, the value written into masked elements (section 3.4):

pad_mode Pad value 0 0 1 +inf 2 -inf

TBD: the bit position of pad_mode in the dstructure CR.

TBD - ask Jacob: whether pad_mode 1 and 2 can be used. They write +inf and -inf, and FP32 elements are never inf or -inf.

docs.title: 3.2 Element Format
docs.text:
Input elements are in the NX8 format. One format applies to all elements. Each product (MULT_RES element) is FP32.

Each MULT instruction (except NOP) names the format in its quantizion_format operand, a 32-bit CR. It has four 8-bit fields:

Bits Field Description [31:24] N/A Not used. [23:16] sign 0 = unsigned, 1 = signed. [15:8] nx_format Exponent format. 0 = dynamic, 1-7 = e1-e7 (fixed exponent width fe). [7:0] num_bits Total element width W: 1-8. 0 is reserved/invalid.

docs.title: 3.2.1 NX8 to FP32
docs.text:
Every MULT instruction converts each NX8 input element to FP32 before it multiplies. The conversion uses the element x (8 bits), the vector scale s (8-bit e8m0) and the exponent width fe.

Exponent width fe:

nx_format fe 1-7 The nx_format value. 0 (dynamic) 1 if dynamic_exponent = 0, 2 if dynamic_exponent = 1. Dynamic elements are signed and 8 bits wide.

Fields. An element is packed from the high end as {S, Exp, M, 0-pad}:

fm   = num_bits - fe - sign                // mantissa bits
S    = (sign == 1) ? x[7] : 0
Exp  = x[7 - sign -: fe]                   // fe bits after S
M    = x[7 - sign - fe -: fm]              // fm bits after Exp, 0 when fm = 0
Emax = 2^fe - 1

Value:

if Exp < Emax:                                            // direct
    fp32 = (-1)^S x 2^(s - 127 - Exp) x (1 + M / 2^fm)
else:                                                     // clamp, Exp = Emax
    fp32 = (-1)^S x 2^(s - 127 - (Emax - 1)) x (M / 2^fm)

TBD - ask Jacob: an NX8 element that is NaN, inf or -inf: which FP32 value does it convert to?

Vector metadata. Each vector is loaded and saved with its metadata:

Metadata Size Description Scale (s) 8 bits Scale shared by the whole vector. dynamic_static 1 bit Dynamic or static quantization. dynamic_exponent 1 bit e1 or e2: the exponent width chosen in dynamic quantization. 0 in static quantization.

R0, R1 and each 128-element slot of R_CYCLIC keep the metadata of the vector loaded into them. Each element uses the metadata of the register or slot that holds it.

docs.title: 3.3 Operand Addressing
docs.text:
Operand source Element j Range of j Ra R0[j] for j < 128, R1[j - 128] for j >= 128 0-255 R_CYCLIC R_CYCLIC[j] 0-511

A vector operand is 128 consecutive elements from a start index: element i of the operand is Ra[start + i] or R_CYCLIC[start + i].

docs.title: 3.4 Element Masking
docs.text:
Every multiply instruction masks its result. Bit i of a mask belongs to element i. Elements whose mask bit is 1 keep their product; elements whose bit is 0 get the pad value (pad_mode, section 3.1).

The mask is built in two steps:

  1. mask_offset selects one of the 8 slots of R_MASK.
  2. mask_shift shifts that slot mask by up to 3 elements. After each one-element shift, the mask is ANDed with a partition vector, so mask bits never cross a group boundary.

shift = clamp(mask_shift, -3, 3)                       // mask_shift is two's complement
mask  = R_MASK.slot[mask_offset]                        // 128 bits
repeat |shift| times:
    if shift > 0: mask = (mask << 1) & partition_vector          // towards higher elements
    if shift < 0: mask = (mask >> 1) & inverse_partition_vector  // towards lower elements

for i in 0..127:
    if mask[i] == 0: MULT_RES[i] = pad_value

Partitions. The 128 elements form num_partition partitions (groups) of 128 / num_partition elements (section 3.1). Partition p holds elements p * (128 / num_partition) to (p + 1) * (128 / num_partition) - 1.

Partition vectors. Two 128-bit vectors mark the partition boundaries:

Vector Bits that are 0 Used by partition_vector The first element of each partition mask_shift > 0 inverse_partition_vector The last element of each partition mask_shift < 0

All other bits are 1. The vectors for each num_partition, element 0 first (1^n is n ones):

num_partition Elements per partition partition_vector inverse_partition_vector 1 128 1^128 1^128 2 64 0 1^63 0 1^63 1^63 0 1^63 0 4 32 (0 1^31) x 4 (1^31 0) x 4 8 16 (0 1^15) x 8 (1^15 0) x 8

Note: After reset, every bit of R_MASK is 1: every element keeps its product.

TBD - ask Aviv: the default value of R_MASK.

TBD - ask Aviv: do we add masking examples?

docs.title: 4. Multiply ISA
docs.text:
The MULT and LOAD slots are resolved by CTRL and forwarded down the pipeline. The stage does not read the CR/LR register files itself (see the Control Stage spec, section 5).

The opcode enum (mult_inst_opcode_t, package ipu_instr_pkg) is generated from instruction_spec.py by sv_package.py.

Note: Each CR0-CR15 and LR0-LR15 register named in the instruction operands is 32 bits wide. An LR operand is read after this cycle's LR updates.

Instructions in this section:

Instruction Purpose NOP Do nothing. LDR_MULT_REG Load one XMEM row into R0 or R1. LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG Load one XMEM row into one slot of R_CYCLIC. LDR_MULT_MASK_REG Load one XMEM row into R_MASK. MULT.RC.VV R_CYCLIC vector x R0 or R1. MULT.RC.VE R_CYCLIC vector x a scalar from Ra or a CR. MULT.RC.VS R_CYCLIC vector x itself. MULT.VE Ra vector x a CR scalar. MULT.EE One Ra element x a CR scalar, broadcast to all 128 elements.

In every MULT Operation below, x converts both NX8 operands to FP32 (section 3.2.1) and multiplies them. apply_mask is section 3.4.

docs.title: 4.1 NOP: No Operation
docs.text: No operation for the MULT slot.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: NOP

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: NOP;;

docs.title: 4.2 LDR_MULT_REG: Load R0 or R1
docs.text: Loads one XMEM row into R0 or R1, with its vector metadata.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: LDR_MULT_REG dest, offset, base

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Details dest Imm R0 or R1. The register that is written. offset LrIdx LR0-LR15. Row offset in XMEM. base CrIdx CR0-CR15. Base row in XMEM.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text: dest = XMEM[offset + base]      // 128 elements + metadata (section 3.2.1)

docs.title: Example
docs.text: LDR_MULT_REG R0, LR0, CR0;;

docs.title: 4.3 LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG: Load an R_CYCLIC Slot
docs.text: Loads one XMEM row into one 128-element slot of R_CYCLIC, with its vector metadata. The other slots keep their values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG offset, base, index

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Details offset LrIdx LR0-LR15. Row offset in XMEM. base CrIdx CR0-CR15. Base row in XMEM. index LrIdx LR0-LR15 whose value is 0, 128, 256 or 384. The first element of the written slot.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text: R_CYCLIC[index .. index + 127] = XMEM[offset + base]   // 128 elements + metadata (section 3.2.1)

docs.title: Example
docs.text: LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG LR0, CR0, LR1;;

docs.title: 4.4 LDR_MULT_MASK_REG: Load R_MASK
docs.text: Loads one XMEM row into R_MASK (8 slots of 128 bits, section 3.4).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: LDR_MULT_MASK_REG offset, base

docs.title: Operands
docs.text: Name Type Details offset LrIdx LR0-LR15. Row offset in XMEM. base CrIdx CR0-CR15. Base row in XMEM.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text: R_MASK = XMEM[offset + base]    // 128 B = 8 x 128 bits

docs.title: Example
docs.text: LDR_MULT_MASK_REG LR0, CR0;;

docs.title: 4.5 MULT.RC.VV: R_CYCLIC Vector x Ra Vector
docs.text: Multiplies a 128-element window of R_CYCLIC by R0 or R1, element by element.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: MULT.RC.VV rc_idx, ra, mask_offset, mask_shift, cr_idx, quantizion_format

docs.title: Operands
docs.text:
The Type column links to the operand type reference.

Name Type Details rc_idx LrIdx LR0-LR15. Start element of the R_CYCLIC window (section 3.3). ra Imm R0 or R1. mask_offset Imm 0-7. R_MASK slot (section 3.4). mask_shift LrIdx LR0-LR15. Mask shift, -3-+3 (section 3.4). cr_idx CrIdx CR0-CR15. Supplies num_partition and pad_mode (section 3.1). quantizion_format CrIdx CR0-CR15. Supplies the NX8 format of the input elements (section 3.2).

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
for i in 0..127:
    MULT_RES[i] = R_CYCLIC[rc_idx + i] x ra[i]
apply_mask(mask_offset, mask_shift, cr_idx)

docs.title: Example
docs.text: MULT.RC.VV LR0, R0, 0, LR2, CR15, CR14;;

docs.title: 4.6 MULT.RC.VE: R_CYCLIC Vector x Scalar
docs.text: Multiplies a 128-element window of R_CYCLIC by one scalar. The scalar is an element of Ra or the low byte of a CR.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: MULT.RC.VE rc_idx, src, mask_offset, mask_shift, cr_idx, quantizion_format

docs.title: Operands
docs.text:

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The AaQ (Activation and Quantization) stage applies element-wise activation and special functions to the 128-element accumulator and quantizes the 128-element vector into an 8-bit vector. On ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE it produces the POST_AAQ_REG payload, which is later written to external memory (XMEM) by ST.AAQ. It produces:

  • A 128-element vector of 8-bit quantized values.
  • A scale factor.
  • A dynamic_exponent bit (the exponent split chosen in dynamic mode).

The element format is not stored per XMEM row. It is global to a table (which may span several XMEM banks) and is supplied to the stage through the format input (section 3.3).

The stage also owns the function estimation LUT, which is filled by the LOAD instruction (section 6.3).

docs.title: 3.1 Inputs
docs.text:
Name Type and Direction Description clk input logic Clock signal. rst_n input logic Asynchronous, active-low op input logic [1:0] Selects the AaQ operation: AAQ_INST_OPCODE_NOP = 0, AAQ_INST_OPCODE_ACTIVATE_QUANTIZE = 1, AAQ_INST_OPCODE_LOAD = 2. r_acc input logic [127:0][31:0] 128-element accumulator (128 × 32-bit FP32). Also the data source for LOAD (section 6.3). function_type input logic [2:0] Encoded activation/special-function selector for ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (see section 5.0). lut_addr input logic [2:0] LUT segment address for LOAD (section 6.3); selects which of the 5 segments (0–4) the instruction writes. Values 5–7 are invalid. Ignored for every other op. valid_elements input logic [7:0] Number of valid elements per partition group, counted from the left (lowest index) of each group; range 0–128/partition (the group size). Values above the group size are invalid. With partition = 1 this is the valid count of the whole 128-element vector. 8 bits are required because 128 is not representable in 7. See section 6 for the resulting active-element mask. partition input logic [1:0] Element partition grouping: enum of 1/2/4/8 (encoded 00/01/10/11). Splits the 128 elements into partition equal groups of 128/partition elements. Together with partition_mask and valid_elements it determines which elements are active (section 6). partition_mask input logic [2:0] Count of partition groups, counted from the right (highest-indexed group), that are masked out entirely. 0 = all partition groups valid; k = the rightmost k groups are masked — their elements do not participate in activation/quantization and their output elements are forced to 0 (section 6.2). k must not exceed partition - 1 (masking every group is not a supported configuration). Example: partition = 8 splits the 128 elements into 8 groups of 16 (elements[0:15] \| elements[16:31] \| ... \| elements[112:127]); partition_mask = 2 masks the rightmost 2 groups, i.e. elements[96:127]. format input logic [8:0] Output element format of the destination table, global to the table (not stored per XMEM row). Bits [7:0] describe the element encoding; bit [8] (dynamic) selects static (0) or dynamic (1) quantization. See section 3.3. write_addr input logic [XMEM_ADDR_W-1:0] Destination XMEM address for ST.AAQ when writing POST_AAQ_REG to XMEM (see XMEM_ADDR_W in the Control stage spec, section 4).

op is sourced from the opcode field of the generated aaq_slot_t struct, typed aaq_inst_opcode_t (package ipu_instr_pkg). Generated from instruction_spec.py (the AAQ slot's "aaq" entry) by sv_package.py via the ipu_instr_pkg.sv.j2 template (bazel run //src/ipu-gen:ipu-gen -- sv-package --output <path>).

docs.title: 3.2 Output
docs.text:
On ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (and only on that opcode — see section 4), AaQ produces a single 1033-bit POST_AAQ_REG payload:

Field Width Description elements 128 × 8 = 1024 bits 128 quantized elements, 8 bits each (section 5.1). scale 8 bits Batch scale factor, e8m0 (section 5.1). dynamic_exponent 1 bit Exponent split chosen by the dynamic selection (section 5.1.1): 0 = fe = 1 (e1m6), 1 = fe = 2 (e2m5). Written as 0 when format[8] = 0 (static), and ignored by readers in that mode.

Total payload: 1024 + 8 + 1 = 1033 bits.

ST.AAQ performs the XMEM write (Memory[write_addr] = POST_AAQ_REG) as a separate STORE-slot operation.

The row does not contain the format field. The format belongs to the table as a whole, and whoever reads the row must get it from the same table-level configuration that drove the format input.

aaq_out is used below as the pseudocode name for this bundle; the concrete storage/register implementation is left to the designer.

docs.title: 3.3 format Field Layout
docs.text:
format is 9 bits. It is a property of the destination table (shared by every row of that table, across all of its XMEM banks) and is not written to XMEM:

Bits Name Description [8] dynamic Quantization mode: 0 = static, 1 = dynamic (section 5.1.1). [7] sign 0 = unsigned, 1 = signed. [6:4] exp_bits (fe) Number of exponent bits, 1–7. 0 is reserved/invalid. [3:0] width Total element width W, stored directly (no offset): value 1–8. 0 is reserved/invalid.

Bits [7:0] have the same meaning in both modes. In dynamic mode (format[8] = 1) the exponent width is chosen per row (section 5.1.1) and recorded in that row's dynamic_exponent bit, so format[6:4] is ignored.

The mantissa is the remainder — what is left of the element width once the sign and exponent bits are taken out:

sign_bit = format[7]                 // 0 or 1
fe       = format[6:4]               // exponent bits
W        = format[3:0]               // total element width, 1..8 bits (stored directly)
fm       = W - fe - sign_bit         // mantissa bits (the leftover)

fm must be >= 0, i.e. W >= fe + sign_bit; encodings that violate this are invalid. fm = 0 is legal (no mantissa bits). W <= 8 always, so a quantized element always fits in its 8-bit output slot; when W < 8 the unused low-order bits are zero-padded.

Example: signed, 2 exponent bits, 8-bit width (e2m5) is format = {1, 3'd2, 4'd8} → fm = 8 - 2 - 1 = 5.

docs.title: 4. Disclaimers
docs.text:
• The AaQ slot executes once per VLIW cycle.
  • AaQ is the pipeline's last stage; slot execution order within a VLIW word: CTRL → MULT → ACC → AaQ.
  • ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE computes the quantized bundle in POST_AAQ_REG; ST.AAQ performs the XMEM write as a separate STORE-slot operation.
  • NOP performs no state changes.

docs.title: 5.0 Activate and Quantize (ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE)
docs.text:
Activation and quantization happen in a single instruction; there is no separate activate-only or quantize-only instruction. It applies an element-wise activation function to every element of r_acc.

The function is selected via function_type and applied to each FP32 element. identity, relu, and relu6 are computed directly; exp2, reciprocal, rsqrt, and generic are evaluated through the LUT, so the selected function must already be loaded there (section 5.2).

for i in 0..127:
    x = r_acc[i]
    case function_type:
        // computed directly
        identity:    activated[i] = x
        relu:        activated[i] = max(0, x)
        relu6:       activated[i] = min(max(0, x), 6)

        // evaluated through the LUT, no special-casing
        exp2:        activated[i] = LUT(x)
        generic:     activated[i] = LUT(x)

        // evaluated through the LUT, with a guard for x's sign/zero
        reciprocal:  if x == 0:      activated[i] = FP32_MAX
                     else:           activated[i] = LUT(x)
        rsqrt:       if x == 0:      activated[i] = FP32_MAX
                     elif x < 0:     activated[i] = 0
                     else:           activated[i] = LUT(x)

FP32_MAX is the largest finite FP32 value, 0x7F7FFFFF ((2 - 2^-23) · 2^127 ≈ 3.4028235e38). The guards never produce inf.

There is a single LUT holding one function at a time: whichever was last loaded by LOAD (section 6.3). For the LUT-based types (exp2, generic, reciprocal, rsqrt), function_type selects only the guards in the pseudocode above; software must load the matching function before issuing ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE.

Supported function types: activation and special functions grouped onto a single field:

Encoding Name Formula Notes 1 identity f(x) = x Pass-through; no transform. 2 relu f(x) = max(0, x) Most common non-linearity. 3 relu6 f(x) = min(max(0, x), 6) Clipped ReLU; used in MobileNet. 4 generic f(x) = LUT(x) Any function loaded into the LUT (section 5.2); the set of supported functions is TBD. Common examples are listed below. All of them are called by the single name generic; which one is applied is decided by whichever function was loaded into the LUT, not by the encoding. 5 reciprocal f(x) = 1/x (FP32_MAX if x = 0) Multiplicative inverse; useful for normalization. 6 rsqrt f(x) = 1/√x (FP32_MAX if x = 0; 0 if x < 0) Reciprocal square root; used in layer normalization. 7 exp2 f(x) = 2^x Used for dequantization, softmax and attention scaling.

Examples of functions run through generic (encoding 4), each loaded into and called through the same LUT:

Name Formula sigmoid f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^-x) tanh f(x) = (e^x - e^-x) / (e^x + e^-x) gelu f(x) = x · Φ(x) = 0.5 · x · (1 + erf(x / √2)) softplus f(x) = ln(1 + e^x) elu f(x) = x if x ≥ 0, else α · (e^x - 1) (α = 1.0) silu f(x) = x · sigmoid(x) = x / (1 + e^-x) window f(x) = 1 if a ≤ x < b, else 0 (rectangular window over [a, b))

docs.title: 5.1 Quantization Algorithm
docs.text:
After activation (section 5.0), each activated FP32 element a (IEEE-754 single precision: 1-bit sign S, 8-bit exponent e, 23-bit mantissa) is quantized to the format selected by format (section 3.3): a sign bit present only if format[7] = 1 (signed; omitted when unsigned), fe exponent bits (format[6:4]), and fm mantissa bits derived as the leftover fm = W - fe - sign_bit, where W = format[3:0] (stored directly, no offset) is the total element width. Since the mantissa is the remainder of the width, sign + fe + fm always totals exactly W; when W < 8 the leftover low-order bits of the 8-bit quantized element are zero-padded. fe is at minimum 1 bit; fm may be 0 bits. FP32 inputs are always treated as normalized (implicit leading 1); subnormal inputs are not specially handled.

The scale factor s (8 bits, e8m0: exponent only, no mantissa) is the batch's shared scale, computed as the maximum raw exponent across the active elements of the batch (active[i], section 6), before quantization. Invalid and masked elements do not contribute to s:

s = max(e[i] for i in 0..127 if active[i])   // active[i]: section 6

For each element, define the exponent distance from the batch scale:

E = -(e - s)   // = s - e

Since s is the batch maximum, E >= 0 for every element, with E = 0 at the batch-max element(s) and E growing as an element's magnitude shrinks relative to the batch max. The output exponent and mantissa fields are then:

if 0 <= E < 2^fe - 1:                // representable directly in fe bits
    Exp = E
    M   = RTN(1.M)                   // round the 23-bit mantissa (implicit leading 1) to fm bits

    if M == 2^fm:                    // edge 1: 1.11...1 rounded up to 10.00...0
        if E > 0:
            Exp = E - 1              // the carry moved the value one binade up
            M   = 0
        else:                        // E = 0: no binade above the batch scale
            Exp = 0
            M   = 2^fm - 1           // saturate at the largest representable value

else:                                // E exceeds what fe bits can represent
    Exp = 2^fe - 1                   // exponent field saturates at its max value
    M   = RTN(1.M >> [E - (2^fe - 1) + 1])  // extra right-shift preserves magnitude instead of flushing to zero

    if M == 2^fm:                    // edge 2: 0.11...1 rounded up to 1.00...0
        Exp = 2^fe - 2               // the smallest directly-encoded exponent
        M   = 0

Both edges are the same event — RTN carrying out of the fm mantissa bits — resolved differently per branch. In the direct branch the carry means the value moved one binade up, so the exponent decrements and the mantissa clears; at E = 0 there is no binade above the batch scale, so the element saturates at the largest representable value instead of wrapping. In the clamp branch the carry turns the shifted fraction into 1.00...0, which is no longer a saturated value but the smallest directly-encoded one, so it is re-encoded as Exp = 2^fe - 2, M = 0.

RTN = round to nearest; an exact half rounds up (away from zero in magnitude), the same rule as section 5.1.1. Sign S (when present, format[7] = 1) is passed through unchanged. The final 8-bit quantized element is {S?, Exp, M, 0-pad}: S, Exp (fe bits), and M (fm bits) packed at the high end, zero-padded at the low end to fill 8 bits. The write payload also carries the batch Scale (s) and the dynamic_exponent bit, as described in section 3.2. format is not written; it is table-level.

Note: the S/Exp/M encoding above is the same in both modes, and s is computed the same way (batch max, as shown above) regardless of format[8]. format[8] = 1 (dynamic) restricts format to exactly two supported formats, both signed and both 8 bits wide (format[3:0] = 8): e2m5 and e1m6 — that pair is exactly fe = 2 and fe = 1 at W = 8, signed, since fm is the leftover (section 3.3). Only fe is chosen; the rule in section 5.1.1 makes that choice per block.

A block is the full 128-element batch of one ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE: one scale s and one dynamic_exponent decision per instruction, computed over the block's active elements (section 6). partition does not split it into smaller blocks.

docs.title: 5.1.1 Dynamic Exponent-Field Selection (fe = 1 vs fe = 2)
docs.text:
Applies only when format[8] = 1. The dynamic decision selects the exponent field width alone: fe = 1 or fe = 2. The input format[6:4] is ignored, and the choice is written to the row's dynamic_exponent bit (section 3.2). The mantissa is not chosen independently — it is the leftover fm = W - fe - sign_bit (section 3.3), so moving from fe = 1 to fe = 2 always buys one more exponent bit at the cost of exactly one mantissa bit, whatever W and sign_bit are. Each block shares one scale s and the quantizer picks one of the two splits per block:

Split Exponent bits Mantissa bits Encodable E Step at E fe1 1 fm1 = W - 1 - sign_bit 0, 1 2^(s - E - fm1), clamped at E >= 1 fe2 2 fm1 - 1 0, 1, 2, 3 2^(s - E - fm1 + 1), clamped at E >= 3

fe1 is one bit finer near the top of the block. fe2 reaches two binades further down before it clamps. The rule below decides which trade is better for the block actually being quantized. It depends on fm1 only through the two multipliers, so it holds for any W/sign_bit pairing, not just the signed 8-bit one.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• s: shared block scale exponent, selected by the same block scale procedure used for static quantization (section 5.1).
  • e: exponent of the individual element.
  • E = s - e. Always non-negative (section 5.1). E = 0 means the scale represents the element exactly.
  • fm1 = W - 1 - sign_bit: the last mantissa bits under fe1. fe2 always has exactly one fewer. For the signed, 8-bit case fm1 = 6.
  • err1: truncation error of the element under fe1.
  • err2: truncation error of the element under fe2.

docs.title: Element classification
docs.text:
Each element contributes to at most one accumulator:

Condition Accumulator Meaning E = 0 A fe1 is finer here. A measures the cost of choosing fe2. E = 1 none Don't care. 1 < E <= fm1 + 2 B fe2 is finer here. B measures the cost of choosing fe1. E > fm1 + 2 none Out of range for both splits.

Elements at E = 1 are don't cares. They enter neither sum and have no effect on the decision.

docs.title: Per-element terms
docs.text:
A = RTN( |err2^2 - err1^2| * 2^(2*fm1) )
B = RTN( |err2^2 - err1^2| * 2^(2*(fm1 + 1)) )

RTN is round to nearest integer, and an exact half rounds up: 0.5 -> 1, 1.5 -> 2, 2.5 -> 3.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
if sum(B) - 4 * sum(A) < 0:  choose fe1        // dynamic_exponent = 0
else:                        choose fe2        // dynamic_exponent = 1

The constant 4 is a unit reconciliation, not a tuning parameter. The B multiplier 2^(2*(fm1 + 1)) is exactly four times the A multiplier 2^(2*fm1), so scaling A by 4 returns both accumulators to a common error.

docs.title: Both estimators are unbiased
docs.text:
Assume mantissa bits are uniformly distributed, so r — the finer split's error as a fraction of its own step — is uniform on [0, 1) and the dropped bit is 1 with probability one half.

Term Pre-RTN value Distribution Outcomes E[RTN] E[pre-RTN] A 1 + 2r uniform on [1, 3) 1, 2, 3 at 0.25, 0.5, 0.25 2 2 B (1 + 2r) / 4 uniform on [0.25, 0.75) 0, 1 at 0.5, 0.5 0.5 0.5

In both rows the rounded mean equals the unrounded mean exactly. Including the zero case, E[A] = 1 and E[B] = 0.25. Neither sum drifts as the block length grows, so rounding contributes noise but never a systematic tilt toward one format.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Block of ten values, s = 0, fm1 = 4 (signed, W = 6). The A multiplier is 2^8 = 256 and the B multiplier is 2^10 = 1024. fm1 = 4 keeps the numbers short; for the signed 8-bit case fm1 = 6, the multipliers are 2^12 and 2^14, and the B region is 1 < E <= 8.

# v e E Acc err1 err2 |err2^2 - err1^2| Pre-RTN A B 1 1.83 0 0 A 0.0175 0.0800 6.09375e-3 1.560 2 2 1.21 0 0 A 0.0225 0.0850 6.71875e-3 1.720 2 3 1.57 0 0 A 0.0075 0.0700 4.84375e-3 1.240 1 4 0.94 -1 1 none don't care don't care 5 0.67 -1 1 none don't care don't care 6 0.41 -2 2 B 0.00375 0.00375 0 0 0 7 0.2345 -3 3 B 0.01575 0.000125 2.48047e-4 0.254 0 8 0.1780 -3 3 B 0.02175 0.006125 4.35547e-4 0.446 0 9 0.0920 -4 4 B 0.02950 0.013875 6.77734e-4 0.694 1 10 0.0555 -5 5 B 0.02425 0.008625 5.13672e-4 0.526 1

sum(A) = 5, sum(B) = 2.

2 - 4 * 5 = -18, which is negative, so the block selects fe1.

docs.title: 5.2 Function Estimation LUT
docs.text: The stage holds a function estimation LUT of 256 entries × 17 bits, plus a 75-bit metadata block that configures range handling. Both are filled by LOAD (section 6.3), which writes one segment per instruction; the 3-bit lut_addr selects the segment.

docs.title: 5.2.1 Segment Transfer
docs.text:
A segment is 1024 bits, sourced from the lower 32 words of the accumulator, r_acc[31:0] (32 words × 32 bits = 1024 bits). The upper words r_acc[127:32] are ignored by LOAD. The 1024-bit payload is the little-endian concatenation of those words:

payload[1023:0] = {r_acc[31], r_acc[30], ..., r_acc[1], r_acc[0]}
                                          // payload[32*j +: 32] == r_acc[j]

The table itself is a 4,352-bit flat bitstream — not split per word, and not reset per segment: LOAD transfers one 1024-bit slice of that stream per instruction, and a table entry may straddle the boundary between two segments (the same way the metadata field straddles word boundaries, section 5.2.2). lut_addr selects which slice:

lut_addr Contents Interpretation 0 Table bits [1023:0] 1st 1024-bit slice of the flat table bitstream. 1 Table bits [2047:1024] 2nd slice. 2 Table bits [3071:2048] 3rd slice. 3 Table bits [4095:3072] 4th slice — the table's first 4,096 bits are now fully loaded. 4 Table bits [4351:4096] (the last 256 bits) + metadata Mixed. payload[255:0] = the table's last 256 bits; payload[330:256] = the 75-bit metadata block (section 5.2.2); payload[1023:331] is unused/reserved. 5–7 Invalid Not a valid LOAD encoding.

Five LOADs (lut_addr 0–4) are required to fully program the LUT and its metadata. Only the last of them (lut_addr = 4) is partially reserved — the first four are fully packed with table bits (256 entries × 17 bits = 4,352 bits total).

docs.title: 5.2.2 Metadata Block
docs.text:
The metadata occupies bits [330:256] of the lut_addr = 4 segment's 1024-bit payload (i.e. local bits [74:0] of the metadata field itself, offset by the 256 bits of leftover table data ahead of it); the remaining bits [1023:331] are unused. Bits-to-word mapping follows payload[32*j +: 32] == r_acc[j] (section 5.2.1), so absolute bit 256 + m (for local metadata bit m) lands in r_acc[(256+m) / 32][(256+m) % 32]. Because the field is flat, it straddles word boundaries — for example max_exp_num is r_acc[8][7:0] and neg_c spans r_acc[8][31:8] together with r_acc[9][7:0].

Bits (local, within metadata) Name Consumed by Meaning [7:0] max_exp_num Quantactivation Largest biased FP32 exponent still inside the LUT range. exp > max_exp_num → lane flagged out-of-range. [39:8] neg_c pack_lutout_activ FP32 constant substituted for negative out-of-range lanes. [71:40] pos_c pack_lutout_activ FP32 constant substituted for positive out-of-range lanes. [72] asymetric Quantactivation Table domain + address form. [74:73] range_mode pack_lutout_activ Out-of-range policy.

TBD: the encodings of asymetric (which table domain and address form each value selects) and of range_mode (which out-of-range policy each of the 4 values selects) are not yet specified.

docs.title: 6. ISA-AaQ: Instruction Reference
docs.text:
The opcode enum (aaq_inst_opcode_t, package ipu_instr_pkg) is generated from instruction_spec.py by sv_package.py.

The AaQ slot is resolved by CTRL and forwarded down the pipeline; the stage does not read the CR/LR register files itself (see the Control Stage spec, section 5). The active elements are determined by ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE's mandatory cr_idx operand (supplying valid_elements) together with partition and partition_mask (section 3.1), at cycle start. The 128 elements are split into partition groups of G = 128/partition elements; the rightmost partition_mask groups are masked entirely, and in every remaining group the first valid_elements elements (from the left of the group) are active:

G = 128 / partition                                   // group size
for i in 0..127:
    g = i / G                                         // group index
    j = i % G                                         // position within group
    active[i] = (g < partition - partition_mask) and (j < valid_elements)

Example: partition = 4 (groups of 32), partition_mask = 1, valid_elements = 10 → active elements 0–9, 32–41, 64–73; group 3 (96–127) is masked. 30 elements are active. There is no implicit default register; cr_idx must always be named explicitly (any CR0-CR15; CR15 remains the conventional choice but is never assumed).

docs.title: 6.1 NOP: No Operation
docs.text:
• Summary: No operation for the AaQ slot; performs no state changes and no memory write.
  • Syntax: NOP
  • Operands: none.

docs.title: 6.2 ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE: Activate and Quantize
docs.text:
• Summary: Apply an element-wise activation function to the active elements of r_acc, quantize the result, and write the resulting 8-bit values, scale factor, and dynamic_exponent bit to POST_AAQ_REG. ST.AAQ performs the XMEM write in the STORE slot. identity, relu, and relu6 are computed directly; exp2, generic, reciprocal, and rsqrt are evaluated through the function pre-loaded into the LUT by LOAD (section 6.3), as described in section 5.0. r_acc is not modified.
  • Syntax: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE function_type, cr_idx
  • Operands:
  • function_type: activation/special-function keyword (see section 5.0): identity, relu, relu6, generic, reciprocal, rsqrt, exp2.
  • cr_idx: CR0…CR15, dstructure register supplying valid_elements (must be given explicitly; no implicit default).
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:                                     // active[i]: section 6
    if active[i]:
        activated[i] = activate(function_type, r_acc[i]) // section 5.0: direct or via LUT
        aaq_out.elements[i] = quantize(activated[i])     // section 5.1
    else:
        aaq_out.elements[i] = 0
aaq_out.scale = s                                    // section 5.1
aaq_out.dynamic_exponent = format[8] ? (fe == 2) : 0 // section 5.1.1
POST_AAQ_REG = aaq_out                              // 1033 bits, section 3.2
  • Example: ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu, CR15;;

docs.title: 6.3 LOAD: Load Function Estimation LUT Segment
docs.text:
• Summary: Fill one 1024-bit segment of the function estimation LUT (section 5.2) from the lower 32 words of r_acc. The 3-bit lut_addr selects the target segment: 0–3 each load a 1024-bit slice of the flat 4,352-bit table bitstream, 4 loads the table's last 256 bits plus the metadata block (section 5.2.1). Performs no XMEM write and does not modify r_acc.
  • Syntax: LOAD lut_addr
  • Operands:
  • lut_addr: LUT segment index, 0–4 (0–3 = table slices, 4 = last table bits + metadata). 5–7 are invalid.
  • Operation: 
    payload[1023:0] = {r_acc[31], ..., r_acc[0]}        // 32 words x 32 bits

if lut_addr <= 3:                                  // full table slice
    TABLE_BITS[1024*lut_addr +: 1024] = payload     // flat bitstream, section 5.2.1
else if lut_addr == 4:                             // last table bits + metadata
    TABLE_BITS[4351:4096] = payload[255:0]
    {range_mode, asymetric, pos_c, neg_c, max_exp_num} = payload[330:256]
    // payload[1023:331] unused; field layout in section 5.2.2
  • Example: LOAD 4;; (load the metadata block)

docs.title: 6.4 Summary Table
docs.text: Slot Mnemonic Operands One-line Effect AaQ NOP - no state change AaQ ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE function_type, cr_idx aaq_out.elements[i] = active[i] ? quantize(activate(function_type, r_acc[i])) : 0, aaq_out.scale/dynamic_exponent set, POST_AAQ_REG = aaq_out; active[i] from partition/partition_mask/valid_elements (section 6) AaQ LOAD lut_addr TABLE_BITS[1024*lut_addr +: 1024] = r_acc[31:0] for lut_addr 0-3; 4 = table bits [4351:4096] + metadata block (section 5.2.1)

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Accumulator (ACC) stage owns R_ACC, the 128-element accumulator register, and combines each cycle's multiply result (MULT_RES, produced by the MULT stage) into it. It is the third stage in the execute chain (CTRL → MULT → ACC → AAQ → STORE) and produces:

  • The updated 128-element R_ACC, forwarded to the AaQ stage.
  • aaq_vliw_bus and str_vliw_bus, forwarded unchanged to the AAQ stage (see the Control Stage spec, §7.2).

Depending on the mnemonic, ACC either runs a per-element elementwise reduction against MULT_RES (ACC.ADD/MAX/SUB), decimates and reorders MULT_RES into a sub-range of R_ACC (ACC.STRIDE), reduces all active MULT_RES elements to a single R_ACC word (AGG.SUM/AGG.MAX), or scatters MULT_RES elements into R_ACC via LRDn index pairs (ACC.RESHAPE).

docs.title: 2. Block Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart LR

    MULTRES(["mult_res 128x32bit"]):::yellow
    OP(["acc_vliw_bus (op + resolved operands)"]):::yellow
    RACC[("R_ACC 128x32bit")]:::purple
    OUT(["r_acc 128x32bit"]):::red

    mult_stage -->|128x32| MULTRES
    MULTRES --> RACC
    OP --> RACC
    RACC -->|read-modify-write| RACC
    RACC --> OUT
    OUT --> aaq_stage
    mult_stage -->|aaq_vliw_bus, str_vliw_bus| acc_stage

    subgraph LEGEND["Legend"]

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text: R_ACC is internal to the ACC stage (owned register, read-modify-write each cycle), analogous to how CR/LR are internal to CTRL. It is not directly writable from outside ACC; the only way to set it is via an ACC-slot instruction.

docs.title: 3.0 Black Box Diagram
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
              clk  ─────>│                                      │
              rst  ─────>│                                      │
               op  ─────>│                                      │
         mult_res  ─────>│                                      │
  acc_vliw_bus operands ─>│             ACC Stage                ├────> r_acc            [127:0][31:0]
                         │      (owns R_ACC, 128x32bit)          │
     aaq_vliw_bus  ─────>│                                      ├────> aaq_vliw_bus      [AAQ_BUS_W-1:0]
      str_vliw_bus  ─────>│                                      ├────> str_vliw_bus      [STR_BUS_W-1:0]
                         └──────────────────────────────────────┘

aaq_vliw_bus and str_vliw_bus arrive from the MULT stage and are forwarded unchanged to the AaQ stage (see the Control Stage spec, §7.2); ACC does not read or modify their contents.

docs.title: 3.1 Inputs
docs.text: Name Type and Direction Description clk input logic Clock signal. rst input logic Synchronous reset. Clears R_ACC to 0. op input logic [3:0] Selects the ACC operation: ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_ADD = 0, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_ADD_FIRST = 1, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_MAX = 2, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_MAX_FIRST = 3, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_SUB = 4, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_SUB_FIRST = 5, ACC_INST_OPCODE_NOP = 6, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_STRIDE = 7, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_SUM_FIRST = 8, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_SUM = 9, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_MAX_FIRST = 10, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_MAX = 11, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_RESHAPE = 12 (see §6 for the full opcode table; opcode = position in instruction_spec.py's "acc" slot). mult_res input logic [127:0][31:0] This cycle's multiply result from the MULT stage: 128 elements, each INT32 or FP32 depending on the active element dtype (INT8-mode multiplies produce INT32 products; FP8-mode multiplies produce FP32 products — see the MULT stage). resolved_operands input logic [131:0] Opcode-dependent union payload packed onto acc_vliw_bus alongside op. CTRL resolves every CR/LR operand this instruction needs (see §5) and packs it in here before dispatch; ACC never reads the CR/LR register files itself. Width is sized to the opcode with the largest operand set (ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_RESHAPE, 132 bits); other opcodes use only their low bits, and the rest are don't-care. Layout per opcode is in §3.1.1. aaq_vliw_bus input logic [AAQ_BUS_W-1:0] AAQ-slot bus, forwarded from MULT. Passed through unchanged (see Control Stage spec §7.2). str_vliw_bus input logic [STR_BUS_W-1:0] STORE-slot bus, forwarded from MULT. Passed through unchanged.

docs.title: 3.1.1 resolved_operands Layout (parsed relative to op)
docs.text: resolved_operands is a union, not a struct: since ACC executes exactly one opcode per cycle, each opcode's operands are packed starting at bit 0 and reuse the same physical bits as every other opcode's operands would. ACC parses the buffer using the field layout for the value of op (see §6 for the opcode table); bits above a given opcode's own fields are don't-care for that opcode.

docs.title: No operands
docs.text: ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_ADD, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_ADD_FIRST, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_MAX, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_MAX_FIRST, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_SUB, ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_SUB_FIRST, ACC_INST_OPCODE_NOP — entire buffer is don't-care.

docs.title: ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_STRIDE
docs.text:
Bits Field Description [1:0] elements_in_row Encoded row-width selector (0/1/2 → 16/32/64 elements per row); an immediate slot field, not CR/LR-resolved. [3:2] horizontal_stride Encoded column-decimation mode (0/1/2 → off/on/on_inv); an immediate slot field, not CR/LR-resolved. [5:4] vertical_stride Encoded row-decimation mode (0/1/2 → off/on/on_inv); an immediate slot field, not CR/LR-resolved. [7:6] offset CTRL-resolved live value of the offset LrIdx operand, truncated to its low 2 bits — offset % 4 is exactly those 2 bits since 4 is a power of 2, so no arithmetic is needed to derive them from the 32-bit LR register. 4 possible values; ACC multiplies by 32 (a shift) to get the R_ACC start index: 0, 32, 64, or 96.

Total: 8 bits used ([7:0]); [131:8] is don't-care.

docs.title: ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_SUM_FIRST, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_SUM, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_MAX_FIRST, ACC_INST_OPCODE_AGG_MAX
docs.text:
Bits Field Description [6:0] dest_slot CTRL-resolved post-LR-write value of the dest_slot LrIdx operand, truncated to its low 7 bits — dest_slot % 128 is exactly those 7 bits since 128 is a power of 2. Range 0–127, directly addressing an R_ACC word. [14:7] valid_elements The valid_elements field CTRL decodes out of the cr_idx DstructureCrIdx operand's CR register (8 bits, range 0–128); ACC clamps it to min(valid_elements, 128) itself.

Total: 15 bits used ([14:0]); [131:15] is don't-care.

docs.title: ACC_INST_OPCODE_ACC_RESHAPE
docs.text:
Bits Field Description [63:0] source CTRL-resolved post-LR-write value of the source LrdIdx operand — the concatenated LR(n+1):LR(n) pair, read as 8 byte elements (source[0..7]), each a MULT_RES word index. [127:64] dest CTRL-resolved post-LR-write value of the dest LrdIdx operand — the concatenated LR(n+1):LR(n) pair, read as 8 byte elements (dest[0..7]), each an R_ACC word index. [131:128] reshape_mask CTRL-resolved value of the reshape_mask LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate operand: the immediate value if the encoded field is < RESHAPE_MASK_LR_OFFSET (8), otherwise the value of LR[encoded − RESHAPE_MASK_LR_OFFSET]. Field width is derived from the shared union field at assembler-build time (currently 4 bits); ACC raises an error if this resolved value exceeds RESHAPE_ELEMENT_COUNT (8) rather than clamping it.

Total: 132 bits used ([131:0]) — the widest opcode, so it sets the buffer's overall width.

docs.title: 3.2 Outputs
docs.text: Name Type and Direction Description r_acc output logic [127:0][31:0] The updated 128-element accumulator, driven to the AaQ stage every cycle (see the AaQ spec, §3.1). aaq_vliw_bus output logic [AAQ_BUS_W-1:0] Forwarded unchanged to the AaQ stage. str_vliw_bus output logic [STR_BUS_W-1:0] Forwarded unchanged to the AaQ stage (AaQ forwards it again to STORE).

docs.title: 4. Disclaimers
docs.text:
• The ACC slot executes once per VLIW cycle.
  • Slot execution order within a VLIW word: CTRL → MULT → ACC → AaQ → STR.
  • NOP performs no state changes (R_ACC unchanged).
  • ACC never reads the CR/LR register files directly — every CR/LR-derived operand value (valid_elements, partition, resolved LR values, etc.) arrives pre-resolved on acc_vliw_bus from CTRL.

docs.title: 5. Data and Register Model
docs.text:
• R_ACC is 128 elements × 32 bits, matching MULT_RES's width and element count. (The hardware parameter for this count is named LANES.)
  • Each element's numeric interpretation (INT32 vs FP32) tracks whatever format MULT_RES was produced in that cycle — ACC's ALU does not carry an independent dtype selector of its own.
  • No dedicated clear/reset instruction. Initialization is done purely through the .FIRST mnemonic variants:
  • X (no suffix) — running accumulation: combines MULT_RES with the previous R_ACC value (read from the pre-cycle snapshot, so it does not see this same cycle's in-flight write).
  • X.FIRST — clean-init: overwrites R_ACC with a value derived purely from MULT_RES, ignoring whatever was previously in R_ACC.
  • This pairing applies to ACC.ADD/ACC.ADD.FIRST, ACC.MAX/ACC.MAX.FIRST, ACC.SUB/ACC.SUB.FIRST, and AGG.SUM/AGG.SUM.FIRST, AGG.MAX/AGG.MAX.FIRST.
  • AGG.SUM/AGG.MAX (and their .FIRST variants) reduce all active elements of MULT_RES — not R_ACC — down to a single scalar, written into one R_ACC word at an LR-selected index. The active element count (valid_elements) and partition come from a DstructureCrIdx operand (cr_idx: any CR0–CR15, must be given explicitly; CR15 conventionally holds dstructure config but is not an implicit default — see the CLAUDE.md project directives).
  • Historical note: cross-element aggregation (AGG.*) was moved into the ACC slot specifically to remove a RAW hazard that existed when it lived in a separate AAQ-writable scalar register file consumed by MULT/ACC (see the Control Stage spec, §9).
  • ACC.RESHAPE scatters MULT_RES elements into R_ACC at LR-pair-selected indices, rather than reducing MULT_RES elementwise or aggregating them. Like every other ACC-stage operation it reads this cycle's MULT_RES (the mult_res input, §3.1): a MULT.* in the same instruction word is the product it scatters. A participating source[i]/dest[i] outside [0, 127], or a resolved reshape_mask greater than RESHAPE_ELEMENT_COUNT (8), raises an error rather than being silently skipped or clamped.

docs.title: 6. ISA: Instruction Reference
docs.text: The opcode enum (acc_inst_opcode_t, package ipu_instr_pkg) is generated from instruction_spec.py by sv_package.py. Per the project's opcode-derivation rule, opcode = position within the "acc" slot dict — the table below lists mnemonics in that exact order.

docs.title: 6.1 ACC.ADD (opcode 0): Accumulate Add
docs.text:
• Summary: Running add accumulation: add the multiply result into each R_ACC element.
  • Syntax: ACC.ADD
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] += MULT_RES[i]
  • Example: ACC.ADD;;

docs.title: 6.2 ACC.ADD.FIRST (opcode 1): Accumulate Add (First)
docs.text:
• Summary: Clean-init add: overwrite each R_ACC element with the multiply result, ignoring the previous R_ACC.
  • Syntax: ACC.ADD.FIRST
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i]
  • Example: ACC.ADD.FIRST;;

docs.title: 6.3 ACC.MAX (opcode 2): Accumulate Max
docs.text:
• Summary: Running max accumulation: each R_ACC element takes the max of its current value and the multiply result.
  • Syntax: ACC.MAX
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] = max(R_ACC[i], MULT_RES[i])
  • Example: ACC.MAX;;

docs.title: 6.4 ACC.MAX.FIRST (opcode 3): Accumulate Max (First)
docs.text:
• Summary: Clean-init max: overwrite each R_ACC element unconditionally with the multiply result.
  • Syntax: ACC.MAX.FIRST
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i]   // unconditional overwrite
  • Example: ACC.MAX.FIRST;;

docs.title: 6.5 ACC.SUB (opcode 4): Accumulate Subtract
docs.text:
• Summary: Running subtract accumulation: subtract the multiply result from each R_ACC element.
  • Syntax: ACC.SUB
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] -= MULT_RES[i]
  • Example: ACC.SUB;;

docs.title: 6.6 ACC.SUB.FIRST (opcode 5): Accumulate Subtract (First)
docs.text:
• Summary: Clean-init subtract: set each R_ACC element to the negated multiply result.
  • Syntax: ACC.SUB.FIRST
  • Operands: none.
  • Operation: 
    for i in 0..127:
    R_ACC[i] = -MULT_RES[i]
  • Example: ACC.SUB.FIRST;;

docs.title: 6.7 NOP (opcode 6): No Operation
docs.text:
• Summary: No operation for the ACC slot; R_ACC unchanged.
  • Syntax: NOP
  • Operands: none.

docs.title: 6.8 ACC.STRIDE (opcode 7): Accumulator Stride
docs.text:
• Summary: Reorder MULT_RES into R_ACC using horizontal/vertical stride decimation. Only the written R_ACC indices change; the rest of R_ACC is left unchanged.
  • Syntax: ACC.STRIDE elements_in_row, horizontal_stride, vertical_stride, offset
  • Operands:
  • elements_in_row: elements per row viewed over the 128-element MULT_RES — encoded 0/1/2 → 16/32/64 elements (elements_per_row, minimum 16).
  • horizontal_stride: column decimation mode — encoded 0/1/2 → off/on/on_inv (on keeps even-indexed columns per row, on_inv keeps odd-indexed columns).
  • vertical_stride: row decimation mode — encoded 0/1/2 → off/on/on_inv (on keeps even-indexed rows, on_inv keeps odd-indexed rows).
  • offset: LR0–LR15 (LrIdx, live value); (offset % 4) * 32 gives the start index in R_ACC (0, 32, 64, or 96).
  • Operation: 
    rows = 128 / elements_per_row
view MULT_RES as [rows][elements_per_row]
if horizontal_stride enabled: keep every 2nd column per row (parity per on/on_inv)
if vertical_stride enabled:   keep every 2nd row (parity per on/on_inv)
N = 128 >> (horizontal_stride_enabled + vertical_stride_enabled)   // 128, 64, or 32
start = (offset % 4) * 32
R_ACC[start : start + N] = decimated MULT_RES, row-major
  • Example: ACC.STRIDE 16, off, off, LR0;;
  • Notes: when a data structure has fewer than 8 elements, hardware pads to 16 automatically (not programmable).

docs.title: 6.9 AGG.SUM.FIRST (opcode 8): Aggregate Sum (First)
docs.text:
• Summary: Sum active MULT_RES elements and write the result into R_ACC at the slot given by LR[dest_slot]. The current value at the destination slot is not included (clean initialization).
  • Syntax: AGG.SUM.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx
  • Operands:
  • dest_slot: LR0–LR15 (LrIdx, post-LR-write value) — its value gives the destination slot in R_ACC (0–127).
  • cr_idx: CR0–CR15 (DstructureCrIdx, must be given explicitly) — supplies valid_elements.
  • Operation: 
    n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128)
dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128
R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1])
  • Example: AGG.SUM.FIRST LR0, CR3;;

docs.title: 6.10 AGG.SUM (opcode 9): Aggregate Sum
docs.text:
• Summary: Sum active MULT_RES elements and add the result to R_ACC at the slot given by LR[dest_slot] (running cross-cycle accumulation).
  • Syntax: AGG.SUM dest_slot, cr_idx
  • Operands: identical to AGG.SUM.FIRST.
  • Operation: 
    n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128)
dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128
R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) + R_ACC[dest]
  • Example: AGG.SUM LR0, CR3;;

docs.title: 6.11 AGG.MAX.FIRST (opcode 10): Aggregate Max (First)
docs.text:
• Summary: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements and write it into R_ACC at the slot given by LR[dest_slot]. The current destination value is not used as a seed.
  • Syntax: AGG.MAX.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx
  • Operands: identical to AGG.SUM.FIRST.
  • Operation: 
    n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128)
dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128
R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1])
// when n = 0: identity seed (INT32_MIN for integer elements, -inf for float elements)
  • Example: AGG.MAX.FIRST LR0, CR3;;

docs.title: 6.12 AGG.MAX (opcode 11): Aggregate Max
docs.text:
• Summary: Find the maximum of active MULT_RES elements seeded with the current destination slot value (running cross-cycle max).
  • Syntax: AGG.MAX dest_slot, cr_idx
  • Operands: identical to AGG.SUM.FIRST.
  • Operation: 
    n = min(CR[cr_idx].valid_elements, 128)
dest = LR[dest_slot] % 128
R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1], R_ACC[dest])
  • Example: AGG.MAX LR0, CR3;;

docs.title: 6.13 ACC.RESHAPE (opcode 12): Reshape
docs.text:
• Summary: Scatter MULT_RES elements into R_ACC: for each of the trailing (8 - reshape_mask) byte elements of the source/dest LRDn pairs (indices reshape_mask..7), copy MULT_RES[source[i]] to R_ACC[dest[i]].
  • Syntax: ACC.RESHAPE source, dest, reshape_mask
  • Operands:
  • source: LRD0, LRD2, …, LRD14 (LrdIdx, post-LR-write value) — read as source[0..7], 8 byte elements, each a MULT_RES word index.
  • dest: LRD0, LRD2, …, LRD14 (LrdIdx, post-LR-write value) — read as dest[0..7], 8 byte elements, each an R_ACC word index.
  • reshape_mask: immediate 0–7 or an LR register (LrOrReshapeMaskImmediate) — selects the first participating element index; elements reshape_mask..7 participate (reshape_mask = 0 uses all 8, reshape_mask = 7 uses only element 7, reshape_mask = 8 uses none). When an LR is given, its value is used directly as the mask (not truncated).
  • Operation: 
    mult_res = MULT_RES   // this cycle's MULT result
mask = reshape_mask if immediate else LR[reshape_mask]
if mask > 8: raise error
for i in mask..7:
    if source[i] >= 128 or dest[i] >= 128: raise error
    R_ACC[dest[i]] = mult_res[source[i]]
  • Example: ACC.RESHAPE LRD0, LRD2, 0;;
  • Notes: reshape_mask skips the lowest-indexed elements 0..reshape_mask-1; the rest participate. Example: reshape_mask = 2 skips elements 0, 1; elements 2-7 participate. Example: reshape_mask = 5 skips elements 0-4; elements 5-7 participate.

docs.title: 6.14 Summary Table
docs.text: Opcode Mnemonic Operands One-line Effect 0 ACC.ADD - R_ACC[i] += MULT_RES[i] 1 ACC.ADD.FIRST - R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i] 2 ACC.MAX - R_ACC[i] = max(R_ACC[i], MULT_RES[i]) 3 ACC.MAX.FIRST - R_ACC[i] = MULT_RES[i] (unconditional) 4 ACC.SUB - R_ACC[i] -= MULT_RES[i] 5 ACC.SUB.FIRST - R_ACC[i] = -MULT_RES[i] 6 NOP - no state change 7 ACC.STRIDE elements_in_row, horizontal_stride, vertical_stride, offset decimate MULT_RES into R_ACC[start:start+N] 8 AGG.SUM.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx R_ACC[dest] = sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) 9 AGG.SUM dest_slot, cr_idx R_ACC[dest] += sum(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) 10 AGG.MAX.FIRST dest_slot, cr_idx R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1]) 11 AGG.MAX dest_slot, cr_idx R_ACC[dest] = max(MULT_RES[0..n-1], R_ACC[dest]) 12 ACC.RESHAPE source, dest, reshape_mask scatter MULT_RES elements into R_ACC per LRDn index pairs

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Cache Unit manages data movement between external DRAM and on-chip XMEM so the IPU can run continuously.

  • CRM resolves IPU addresses and checks tags.
  • DMA moves data between DRAM and XMEM using DMA tables.
  • XMEM stores active banks/pages used by IPU.

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text: Name Type and Direction Description riscv_cfg_bus input logic [TBD:0] Config bus from RISC-V for table setup and start signals. dram_addr output logic [TBD:0] Address to DRAM controller. dram_rd_data input logic [7:0] [XMEM_ROW_WIDTH-1:0] Read data from DRAM (array of bytes). dram_rd_metadata input logic [META_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] Metadata read from DRAM. dram_wr_data output logic [7:0] [XMEM_ROW_WIDTH-1:0] Write data to DRAM (array of bytes). dram_wr_metadata output logic [META_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] Metadata written to DRAM. ipu_addr input logic [ARRAY_ID_WIDTH+OFFSET_WIDTH-1:0] IPU virtual address (array_id + offset). ipu_rd_data output logic [7:0] [XMEM_ROW_WIDTH-1:0] Data returned to IPU (array of bytes). ipu_rd_metadata output logic [META_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] Metadata returned to IPU. ipu_wr_data input logic [7:0] [XMEM_ROW_WIDTH-1:0] Data written by IPU to XMEM (array of bytes). ipu_wr_metadata input logic [META_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] Metadata written by IPU to XMEM.

docs.title: 4. Parameters
docs.text: Name Default Description NUM_BANKS 16 Number of XMEM banks/pages. BANK_DATA_SIZE 1024 rows x 1024 bits = 128KB Size of one BANK/PAGE. OFFSET_WIDTH 20 Offset width inside the array address space. ARRAY_ID_WIDTH 4 Array ID width. XMEM_ROW_WIDTH 128 Width of one XMEM row (bytes). META_DATA_WIDTH 16 Width of metadata carried alongside row data (bits). For AaQ-produced rows, metadata carries scale[7:0] and row-local dynamic_exponent (metadata[8]); the destination table's format[8:0] is table-level state (Section 5), not per-row metadata.

docs.title: 4.1 XMEM Bank Property
docs.text:
Each XMEM bank carries the following per-bank state, in addition to its data rows.

Field Width (bits) Description tag 14 {TABLE_ID, offset[19:10]}. FFFF means the bank is free or not ready for the required operation. table_id 4 Table currently owning this bank. flush 1 When True, this bank is ready to be written to DRAM.

docs.title: 5. Tables
docs.text:
A table is a data structure that defines the methodology of a data movement and holds all the parameters needed for the task.

Table properties:

Field Width (bits) Description table_id 4 Table ID sent with the IPU address. type 2 read_only, write_only, read_after_write, scratch_pad. reletive to IPU dram_base_address 32 Resolution of BANK_DATA_SIZE. size 16 Resolution of BANK_DATA_SIZE. xmem_bank_list[16] 4 Ordered array of banks. xmem_num_of_banks 4 Amount of banks. jump_back 16 Flush all addresses that are below table_addr - jump_back. Actual flush is done for the entire bank, not per address. When accessing table_addr < jump_back, flush all table banks to prepare for another round of table traversing. repetitions 16 Number of times to read the table. Used to invalidate banks (using jump_back) on the last round of the read. format 9 Table-global output element format for AaQ destination tables: format[8] = dynamic flag, format[7:0] = element encoding fields. Shared by all rows in the table.

docs.title: 5.1 Table Types
docs.text:
• read_only — Table data is loaded from DRAM into XMEM. Once the IPU has finished reading the table, all of its bank tags are invalidated.
  • write_only — Table data is written from XMEM to DRAM. Once all of the table's data has been written to DRAM, all of its bank tags are invalidated.
  • read_after_write — Table data is written by the IPU into XMEM and stays valid until it has been read back; only then are its bank tags invalidated.
  • scratch_pad — Table data stays resident in XMEM for as long as the layer is executing on the IPU. Its bank tags are invalidated only when the currently executing kernel finishes.

docs.title: 6. Memory and Tag Model
docs.text:
• Tag = {TABLE_ID, offset[19:10]}
  • In this design, BANK = PAGE.
  • Each BANK/PAGE has 1024 rows.
  • Each row is 1024 bits.
  • Each row contains metadata (META_DATA_WIDTH = 16 bits) alongside its data:
  • scale[7:0] = 8-bit scale
  • dynamic_exponent[8] = row-local exponent split bit for dynamic AaQ rows (0=e1m6, 1=e2m5)
  • metadata[15:9] = reserved/implementation-defined
  • AaQ row readers obtain element format from the destination table's format[8:0] property (Section 5), not from per-row metadata.
  • Address split:
  • offset[9:0] = row index in bank (0..1023)
  • offset[19:10] = tag and bank-list index component
  • FFFF tag means bank is free or not ready for the required operation.

docs.title: 7. Handshake Model
docs.text:
• IPU and DMA are not directly connected — they synchronize only through per-bank tag/flush state in XMEM (Section 4.1).
  • IPU sends two things to CRM:
  • ipu_addr (virtual address)
  • Requested table ID — symbolic table names (e.g. W_Table, Xout_Table) are assigned a numeric table_id (0-15) at compile time.
  • CRM computes bank_pos/tag from the address and checks it against the bank's current tag. If they don't match, CRM stalls the IPU.
  • Read path: DMA runs in the background, waits for a free bank (tag == FFFF), fills it from DRAM, and publishes bank.tag when done. Once the published tag matches what CRM is checking for, CRM releases the stall.
  • Write path: the IPU claims free banks ahead of writing (Section 9.2, thread 0) and writes into them. When a jump boundary is crossed, CRM marks the previous bank flush = True instead of invalidating its tag immediately. DMA drains flushed banks to DRAM (Section 8.2) and clears the bank (tag = FFFF, flush = False) once the drain completes.

docs.title: 8. DMA Operations
docs.text:
• banklist is a cyclic linked list.
  • repetitions is the num of time this table must be loaded from dram during its lifetime.
  • dram_base_address is the DRAM base address used for this table's operations.

DMA can only handel write_only/read only table

docs.title: 8.1 DMA Read (DRAM -> XMEM)
docs.text:
dram_addr = dram_base_address + dram_offset
bank_pos = dram_offset[19:10] % NUM_BANKS
bank = banklist[bank_pos]
xmem_addr = {bank, dram_offset[9:0]}
tag = {TABLE_ID, dram_offset[19:10]}

if (bank.tag != FFFF)
   DMA_stall

if (done_filling_bank)
   bank.tag = tag
   bank.table_id = TABLE_ID

Behavior: - DMA cannot overwrite a busy bank (bank.tag != FFFF). - Tag is published only after the whole bank is filled.

docs.title: 8.2 DMA Write (XMEM -> DRAM)
docs.text:
dram_addr = base_dram_addr + dram_offset
bank_pos = dram_offset[19:10] % NUM_BANKS
bank = banklist[bank_pos]
tag = {TABLE_ID, dram_offset[19:10]}

if (bank.tag != tag and bank.flush == False)
     DMA_stall

if (dram_offset[9:0] == 0x3FF)   // row 1023
   bank.tag = FFFF
   bank.flush = False

Behavior: - DMA drains bank data to DRAM only when bank tag matches required tag. - At row 1023, drain is complete and bank is released (FFFF).

docs.title: 9.1 IPU Read (XMEM -> IPU)
docs.text:
// IPU request carries: IPU_ADDR (virtual) + TABLE_ID

bank_pos = offset[19:10] % NUM_BANKS
bank = banklist[bank_pos]
xmem_addr = {bank, offset[9:0]}
tag = {TABLE_ID, offset[19:10]}

if (tag != bank.tag or bank.table_id != TABLE_ID)
   IPU_stall

if (offset[9:0] >= jump_back && offset[19:10] != 0)
   banklist[(bank_pos - 1) % NUM_BANKS].tag = FFFF

if (offset == FFFF)
   for bank in banks:
      bank.tag = FFFF

Behavior: - CRM can free previous bank at jump boundary.

docs.title: 9.2 IPU Write (IPU -> XMEM)
docs.text:
thread 0
while (i != array_size):
   bank_pos = i % NUM_BANKS
   bank = banklist[bank_pos]
   if(bank.tag == FFFF)
      bank.tag = i
      bank.table_id = TABLE_ID
      i++

thread 1
bank_written_counter = 0 
bank_pos = offset[19:10] % NUM_BANKS
bank = banklist[bank_pos]
tag = {TABLE_ID, offset[19:10]}

if (tag != bank.tag or bank.table_id != TABLE_ID)
   IPU_stall

if (offset[9:0] >= jump_back && offset[19:10] != 0 )
   banklist[(bank_pos - 1) % NUM_BANKS].flush = True
   bank_written_counter++ 

if (offset == FFFF && bank_written_counter == size)
   for bank in banklist:
      if(bank.tag != FFFF)
         bank.flush = True

Behavior: - CRM table provides banklist (linked list) and jump_back (numeric value).

docs.title: 10. Layer1/Layer2 Timing Example
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
   participant RISCV as RISC-V
   participant DMA as DMA
   participant XMEM as XMEM
   participant CRM as CRM
   participant IPU as IPU

   RISCV->>RISCV: Config tables L1
   RISCV->>RISCV: Go L1
   RISCV-->>IPU: Start
   IPU->>CRM: Data fetch
   CRM->>XMEM: Wait for tag...
   CRM->>IPU: Stall
   RISCV->>DMA: Start fetching L1
   DMA->>XMEM: Publish first page tag L1
   XMEM->>CRM: Matching tag
   CRM->>IPU: Release Stall
   IPU->>IPU: Start working L1

   Note over RISCV,IPU: Working...

   RISCV->>RISCV: Config tables L2
   DMA->>DMA: Last page filled L1
   RISCV->>RISCV: Go L2
   DMA->>XMEM: Publish first page tag L2
   IPU->>IPU: Done working L1
   IPU->>CRM: Data fetch
   CRM->>XMEM: Matching tag
   CRM->>IPU: Start
   IPU->>IPU: Start working L2

docs.title: Mnemonic rename (E03-19): SystemVerilog names
docs.text:
The mnemonic standard (Q33, Q45) renamed nine instructions. Opcodes did not change, so every program assembled to the same bits, and every *_WIDTH localparam, typedef name and operand field name in ipu_instr_pkg.sv was unchanged. Only these enum members and union members of the package were renamed. (A later, breaking change, ADR 0007, removed two of the nine and changed widths: see RTL migration.) A downstream RTL repository that vendors the package replaces each old name with the new one.

tools/rename_mnemonics.py applies the same rename to assembly sources, Python, JavaScript and docs on another branch or checkout:

bazel run //tools:rename_mnemonics -- --check   # list what would change
bazel run //tools:rename_mnemonics              # rewrite the workspace in place
Old mnemonic New mnemonic Old enum member New enum member Old union member New union member Value LDR_MULT_REG LD.MULT LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LDR_MULT_REG LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LD_MULT ldr_mult_reg ld_mult 2'd0 LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG LD.MULT.CYCLIC LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LDR_CYCLIC_MULT_REG LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LD_MULT_CYCLIC ldr_cyclic_mult_reg ld_mult_cyclic 2'd1 LDR_MULT_MASK_REG LD.MASK LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LDR_MULT_MASK_REG LOAD_INST_OPCODE_LD_MASK ldr_mult_mask_reg ld_mask 2'd2 STR_POST_AAQ_REG ST.AAQ STORE_INST_OPCODE_STR_POST_AAQ_REG STORE_INST_OPCODE_ST_AAQ str_post_aaq_reg st_aaq 1'd0 STR_ACC_REG ST.ACC ACC_STORE_INST_OPCODE_STR_ACC_REG ACC_STORE_INST_OPCODE_ST_ACC str_acc_reg st_acc 1'd0 INCR_MOD_POW2 INC.MODP2 LR_INST_OPCODE_INCR_MOD_POW2 LR_INST_OPCODE_INC_MODP2 incr_mod_pow2 inc_modp2 4'd3 BLT BLT.S COND_INST_OPCODE_BLT COND_INST_OPCODE_BLT_S blt blt_s 3'd2 BGE BGE.S COND_INST_OPCODE_BGE COND_INST_OPCODE_BGE_S bge bge_s 3'd3 BKPT HALT COND_INST_OPCODE_BKPT COND_INST_OPCODE_HALT bkpt halt 3'd5

The pseudo-instructions BGT and BLE became BGT.S and BLE.S; they have no SV name. BLT.U, BGE.U, BGT.U and BLE.U are reserved for unsigned branches (ipu_isa.RESERVED_MNEMONICS): no spec may define them, and the assembler rejects them as "reserved, not implemented".

ST.AAQ and ST.ACC no longer exist: ADR 0007 removed the STORE and ACC_STORE slots (the AaQ stage stores its own row with ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE; a raw accumulator store is ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity, or ACTIVATE.EXACT identity in the FP32 mode). Their rows stay as a record of the rename; none of their names is in the SV package, and tools/rename_mnemonics.py still maps the old names, so a source it renames then needs the ADR 0007 migration as well.

//src/ipu-gen:test_sv_rename_table checks this table against the SV golden.

docs.title: RISC-V Host Integration (Design Spec)
docs.text:
Not yet updated for ADR 0007

ADR 0007 replaced the 32-bit dstructure with a 16-bit DS CR half and reduced the element formats to FP32 and NX8, and removed the post-AAQ register. This page still gives the host DSTRUCTURE register the old layout and resets a post-AAQ staging register; the action to update it is A-5 in Open questions.

Status

Proposal / design spec. This page describes a planned big feature: an emulated RISC-V host core that drives the IPU emulator through a memory-mapped control register block. The register block is the single source of truth (authored in SystemRDL), and is the same definition used by the Python emulator, the on-device Rust driver, and the generated documentation. The implementation is tracked as an epic and a set of sub-issues — see §9 Implementation Plan.

docs.title: 1. Motivation
docs.text:
Today the Python emulator is driven directly from Python: a test or app harness builds an IpuState, loads a program, sets CR registers, and calls run_until_complete(). The real hardware works differently — the Control Stage spec and the Cache Unit spec both describe an external RISC-V host that configures and sequences the IPU over an APB slave port: it writes the instruction memory and the CR file (inactive banks), triggers bank swaps, starts/stops the core, and reads back status.

This feature closes the gap between the emulator and the hardware model by:

  1. Emulating the host CPU itself. A RISC-V core (via the Unicorn CPU-emulation framework, embedded in the Python environment) runs the same firmware that would run on real silicon.
  2. Defining a real control/configuration register block that both the host firmware and the IPU emulator agree on, authored once in SystemRDL so that the Python model, the Rust driver, and the docs are all generated from one source.
  3. Driving IPU execution through that register block — start, halt, single-step, reprogram instruction memory, read/write the program counter, and reset — instead of via ad-hoc Python calls.

The end state: an integration test loads a Rust firmware image into the emulated RISC-V core; the firmware configures the IPU (CRs, dtype, dstructure), loads a program into the fully mapped instruction-memory region, starts the IPU, polls for completion, and reads back results — all through MMIO, exactly as it would on hardware.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• A memory-mapped IPU host-control register block authored in SystemRDL.
  • All current configuration surface reachable through the register block: dtype, dstructure (valid_elements / partition), CR2–CR14 application constants, and the activation elu_alpha.
  • Execution-flow control through the register block:
    1. Start execution.
    2. Halt execution.
    3. Reprogram the IPU instruction memory.
    4. Read and write the program counter.
    5. Reset the IPU (resets everything except instruction memory).
  • A RISC-V core emulated in-process via Unicorn, with the register block exposed as MMIO.
  • Rust (not C) firmware/driver running on the emulated core, generated from the same SystemRDL source.
  • Single source of truth preserved: no hand-duplicated register metadata.

docs.title: Non-Goals (for the initial epic)
docs.text:
• Cycle-accurate co-simulation of host ↔ IPU timing. The host/IPU handshake is functional, not cycle-accurate.
  • Modeling the full APB wire protocol (psel/penable/pready handshakes). We model the register semantics the APB slave exposes, addressed as a flat MMIO window; APB timing is out of scope.
  • DMA / CRM cache-unit modeling (see cache-unit.md). The control block focuses on CTRL-stage configuration and sequencing.
  • Replacing the existing direct-Python harness. run_until_complete() and the debug CLI keep working; the host path is additive.

docs.title: 3. Architecture Overview
docs.text:
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'defaultRenderer': 'elk'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    subgraph RUST["Rust firmware (no_std)"]
        FW["application firmware\n(main loop)"]:::purple

    subgraph UC["Unicorn RISC-V core (in Python)"]

    end

    subgraph PY["Python IPU emulator"]

    end

    RDL["ipu_ctrl.rdl\n(SystemRDL — source of truth)"]:::yellow

    FW --> DRV
    DRV -->|"lw / sw to MMIO"| CPU

    CPU --> MMIO
    MMIO -->|read/write callback| BRIDGE
    BRIDGE --> CTRLMODEL
    CTRLMODEL -->|"start / halt / step / reset / imem / pc"| ENGINE

    RDL -. "peakrdl: Python field constants" .-> CTRLMODEL

    classDef blue fill:#4a80c4,stroke:#2a5090,color:#fff
